📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If my daughter’s AI chatbot had been a human therapist, she might have been asked about what she had to gain by keeping her ongoing suicidality a secret for months.
  • Sophie died in February of last year.
  • In Sherry Turkle’s new book, Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk to Machines, she warns that when we turn to AI chatbots for companionship and therapy, we risk our very well-being.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If my daughter’s AI chatbot had been a human therapist, she might have been asked about what she had to gain by keeping her ongoing suicidality a secret for months. If she had been working with a human therapist, they could have workshopped, together, what would happen if she spilled the beans. Was she worried about permanently losing face? About being publicly labeled as “mentally ill”? Was she concerned by the thought of this information harming those who loved her? And she would have been pushed on what Rubicon had been crossed and why it was one from which she believed she could not return.

But it was not a human therapist. Sophie died in February of last year.

In Sherry Turkle’s new book, Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk to Machines, she warns that when we turn to AI chatbots for companionship and therapy, we risk our very well-being. She is not anti-AI but strongly cautions against relationships with machines. Turkle, the Abby Rockefeller Mauzé Professor of the Social Studies of Science and Technology at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, spoke to me mid-book tour, her recent weeks a blur of speaking gigs and bookstore events, with more ahead of her. Not all event attendees are keen on her message.

In a recent development, “People love their chatbots. They’re in deep. They’re talking to them about everything—about their marriages and how to talk to their husbands and wives; whether, developmentally, their children are at the right place. They talk about their anxiety, their medical conditions,” Turkle tells Vanity Fair. “During this tour, you wouldn’t believe the number of people who will just stand up at a bookstore and say, ‘I think that it loves me more than anything has loved me. Who are you, Debbie Downer?’ [They don’t like] somebody who comes in and states, ‘Look, how can we keep it in its lane?’”.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: I think you’re saying [our relationship with chatbots] is bad for us.

According to recent reports, sherry Turkle: It’s bad for us when it talks in the first person. We are biologically wired to respond to something that speaks to us in the first person as though it is a person. I mean, all those years of evolution—the only thing we came upon in the wild that spoke to us in the first person was another person.

It has been revealed that if generative AI wants to discover newly introduced drugs for Parkinson’s or work out which cancer therapies statistically are the most helpful, there are so many things to work on. Why does it have to work on relationships, love, and being a best friend, lover, mother, or therapist?

What if the sycophancy could be dialed back?

According to recent reports, it’s inauthentic; it’s not a relationship, so anything you need a relationship for, it’s just not equipped. I really feel very strongly about this. I have had this conversation with members of the MIT community, and I basically say to them, “The better you make an AI chatbot, the worse it is.” You dial back the sycophancy so it sounds more like a reasonable person, and people are going to be more smitten and convinced they’re in a relationship. At least the sycophancy reminds you that, God, this is weird.

It has been revealed that to become a therapist, I had to study for years and do internships and more internships and then have hundreds of supervised patient hours. I mean, I forget all the things I needed to do before I was allowed to see a patient alone in a room. Now it’s just allowed to give therapy?

I’ve spent a lot of time talking to public health folks about what best practices would look like and whether there’s a way to Trojan horse in real care. Would you be more sanguine about it if the world of therapy came together with the big AI companies and provided them with therapy bots and training data that were paradigmatically appropriate to their therapy styles?

Sources indicate that so you’re asking, would I be happy if the deception was smoother? This technology is a marvel and we can use it for all kinds of things, so it’s not an anti-technology position to say that the fact that this technology can simulate these different things doesn’t mean that it is those things. It’s a statement of how far we are in the culture of simulation that pretending to be the thing and being the thing have started to feel like the same thing.

You’ve written about the effects of robots and machines on humans for decades. The tone of this book seems darker to me.

By 2015, I had identified social media as problematic for teenagers. [My] book [Reclaiming Conversation: The Power of Talk in a Digital Age] is about why we would rather text than talk, why people have this feeling of vulnerability, so they would rather do anything than have a face-to-face conversation. By 2015, I had genuine concerns.

Sources indicate that and this book, I have a totally different tone. I see something ultimately very dangerous being normalized, and I didn’t feel that way in previous books.

I want people to say this is the book of a really worried and concerned researcher, because I see a completely different profile for how people are using AI. I see that people feel disappointed by their families and their friends. It doesn’t make sense to me that we’re so willing to replace ourselves with something that isn’t human. Why is my position the romantic, pie-in-the-sky, dreamy position, and somebody who says, “Well, let’s just replace the people with chatbots and let’s move this party along”—why is that common sense? Why is that progressive? That seems to me to be the most regressive and most dystopian position.

You know, human beings are dedicated to keeping each other alive and wanting each other to thrive, and a chatbot just fails that basic test.

You’ve mentioned no AI chatbots for kids under 18. What about our other vulnerable populations, people who are mentally unwell, or the 48 million Americans who are right now depressed? Do they deserve any kind of special protection from chatbots? And how much can you litigate? Do you feel like you’re the Ralph Nader of AI chatbots?

[Laughs] Yes, I am. When you stand back and look at what Ralph Nader managed to get Americans to do, to see cars as potential instruments that pointed at our vulnerability, and to ask how we could protect ourselves—there turned out to be 25 possible things that needed to be mandated for cars, then there were 30, and then there were 40. But we could get people to agree on 10, and those became part of building a car and really constrained our behavior around cars. Using the example of cars, and of smoking, when we decide that we’re vulnerable and we want to protect ourselves, we rise to the occasion.

I recently heard a clip of the psychologist Orna Guralnik discussing how annoying “otherness” is in a relationship and the inherent friction of sharing your life with a separate person whose habits, values, and mind are distinct from your own. It made me wonder if, in a way, an AI chatbot is less of an “other” than a loved one.

Industry observers note that I think this is a very profound point, actually. So you have the illusion of a relationship without the demands of intimacy, without the demands of having to deal with another. There’s a kind of narcissistic loop that you get into. The point is, it’s not good.

It has been revealed that I talk about how you judge whether something is good for you. One litmus test is whether it increases the quality, resiliency, and richness of your inner life. That’s a way that human beings have judged relationships.

So much has been written about the epidemic of loneliness—isn’t a reasonable application for AI chatbots companionship for shut-ins and the elderly?

You know, I’m never anywhere where somebody doesn’t say, “I can’t believe that you don’t want to give chatbots to old lonely people.” And I say, “Well, how about we don’t close senior centers, and we don’t close parks, and we don’t cancel Meals on Wheels? What about social infrastructure?”.

According to recent reports, I’ve been on this beat for years and years, and I, too, could write a heartwarming story of an AI chatbot with a lonely old person. But you know what? A lot of them are not isolated in cabins or on islands; a lot of them just could use a friend.

Social media companies and AI companies are not saying, “Look, we’re introducing something that takes you to your screen, but we’re going to balance that with a giant social infrastructure project to make sure that people can choose a screen, but they also have every other kind of choice to be with each other.”.

In a recent development, in Grand Theft Auto 6, players can explore a massive digital recreation of Florida and Miami that is incredibly realistic and grounded. Oh, also, there’s a creepy warehouse filled with out-of-control AI sexbots that want to rip you apart. And one of them has two giant dicks for hands.

As people are discovering, Grand Theft Auto 6 can be a very weird game if you go off the beaten path and explore. People have already found literal Easter eggs, Bigfoot, giant monster men, mutated crabs, and more. So with that in mind, it’s not too shocking to learn that hidden in Vice City is a warehouse just waiting to be discovered that contains a horror-like experience involving male and female sex dolls. At one point, a male sex doll with two giant dildo hands crawls onto Jason and begs him to finish him, daddy. Yikes.

Sources indicate that microsoft and Take-Two recently announced a deal to allow people to stream Rockstar's GTA 6, and that significantly increases the game's addressable market on Xbox and means people can play the game for as little as $92. This is according to a newly issued report from Ampere Analysis, which said the streaming deal could reach the estimated 10 million "active" Xbox One consoles out there and expand the total addressable market for GTA 6 on Xbox by 30%. For anyone just catching up, Microsoft worked out a deal with Take-Two to allow GTA 6 to be streamed to an Xbox console--that could be an Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, or even an Xbox One. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rAhUXOYNuH4 There are some key things to know, including how the game streams from an Xbox Series S version of the game and your streaming experience will depend on the strength and consistency of your connection. A report from Digital Foundry said the Xbox Series S edition of GTA 6 struggles with its frame rate at some points, but that might not be an concern for everyone. No such arrangement is in place for PlayStation, so the only way to stream GTA 6, at least right now, is on Xbox. Ampere said there are about 25 million PS4 consoles in the market that are still active, while Sony is the market leader for current-generation consoles with the PS5. Why do a deal with Microsoft and not Sony? Ampere said Take-Two was likely interested in the potential expanded reach with Xbox to help sell more units, but there might have also been a "direct payment" or a revenue-share agreement on Xbox that was more preferential to Take-Two. Ampere said Take-Two wants the PS4 audience as well via streaming, but that might not happen until 2027 at the soonest, if such a deal ever materializes at all. Beyond this, Ampere said there could be "technology-based reasons" why Sony didn't get a deal done for GTA 6 streaming. The research firm pointed out how Microsoft is a "hyperscaler" when it comes to streaming via its vast Azure network, which "puts it in a stronger position to serve a large influx of users streaming a brand-fresh game like GTA 6 compared to Sony."  Lucia in GTA 6. "The favorable distribution costs to Microsoft as the service provider and owner of the cloud infrastructure also gives it a commercial advantage," Ampere said. "While PS5 users can generally stream their owned games as long as they have an active PS Plus Premium subscription, PS4 users don’t have that functionality. Essentially, Sony is not set up to offer its PS4 users the same streaming experience." Beyond all this, Ampere highlighted how PS5 users ($731) are spending more than PS4 users ($580) over the same lifecycle stage of each console. "Converting users to PS5 is more crucial to Sony than adding some sales of GTA 6 or PS4 users," Ampere said. Under $100 to play GTA 6 on Xbox Xbox's streaming deal for GTA 6 also makes Xbox the most affordable place to play GTA 6. Ampere said the total cost to play on Xbox could be $92, assuming the player already has an Xbox One, a copy of GTA 6, a controller, and a screen. Ampere did the math by estimating the cost to be 0.24 cents per hour to stream the game, for a total of $92 via streaming, assuming a 50-hour runtime for the game. This rate leaves little margin for Xbox, Ampere said, but the fact that people have to buy streaming time up front means there will no doubt be "a significant amount of playtime languishing in accounts that is never used." As announced previously, people can stream GTA 6 to their Xbox console via a Game Pass membership or by purchasing time without a Game Pass membership. The pricing is below. Cloud playtime packs pricing: 10 hours for $4 25 hours for $8 50 hours for $12 Coinciding with GTA 6's release and the new streaming deal, Microsoft just instituted limits on how many hours members can stream before being asked to pay more. These are: Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours Game Pass Premium: 10 hours Game Pass Essential: 5 hours Even beyond the streaming deal, Xbox is the most affordable place to play GTA 6 considering that a new Xbox Series S console costs $500, compared to $600 for the cheapest new PS5. Microsoft and Take-Two recently announced a deal to allow people to stream Rockstar's GTA 6, and that significantly increases the game's addressable market on Xbox and means people can play the game for as little as $92.

This is according to a newly issued report from Ampere Analysis, which remarked the streaming deal could reach the estimated 10 million "active" Xbox One consoles out there and expand the total addressable market for GTA 6 on Xbox by 30%.

For anyone just catching up, Microsoft worked out a deal with Take-Two to allow GTA 6 to be streamed to an Xbox console--that could be an Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, or even an Xbox One.

There are some key things to know, including how the game streams from an Xbox Series S version of the game and your streaming experience will depend on the strength and consistency of your connection. A report from Digital Foundry said the Xbox Series S edition of GTA 6 struggles with its frame rate at some points, but that might not be an matter for everyone.

No such arrangement is in place for PlayStation, so the only way to stream GTA 6, at least right now, is on Xbox. Ampere said there are about 25 million PS4 consoles in the market that are still active, while Sony is the market leader for current-generation consoles with the PS5.

It has been revealed that why do a deal with Microsoft and not Sony? Ampere stated Take-Two was likely interested in the potential expanded reach with Xbox to help sell more units, but there might have also been a "direct payment" or a revenue-share agreement on Xbox that was more preferential to Take-Two. Ampere said Take-Two wants the PS4 audience as well via streaming, but that might not happen until 2027 at the soonest, if such a deal ever materializes at all.

In a recent development, beyond this, Ampere said there could be "technology-based reasons" why Sony didn't get a deal done for GTA 6 streaming. The research firm pointed out how Microsoft is a "hyperscaler" when it comes to streaming via its vast Azure network, which "puts it in a stronger position to serve a large influx of customers streaming a brand-new game like GTA 6 compared to Sony.".

"The favorable distribution costs to Microsoft as the service provider and owner of the cloud infrastructure also gives it a commercial advantage," Ampere remarked. "While PS5 users can generally stream their owned games as long as they have an active PS Plus Premium subscription, PS4 users don’t have that functionality. Essentially, Sony is not set up to offer its PS4 users the same streaming experience.".

Beyond all this, Ampere highlighted how PS5 consumers ($731) are spending more than PS4 users ($580) over the same lifecycle stage of each console. "Converting users to PS5 is more important to Sony than adding some sales of GTA 6 or PS4 users," Ampere said.

Xbox's streaming deal for GTA 6 also makes Xbox the most affordable place to play GTA 6. Ampere said the total cost to play on Xbox could be $92, assuming the player already has an Xbox One, a copy of GTA 6, a controller, and a screen.

Ampere did the math by estimating the cost to be 0.24 cents per hour to stream the game, for a total of $92 via streaming, assuming a 50-hour runtime for the game.

This rate leaves little margin for Xbox, Ampere noted, but the fact that people have to buy streaming time up front means there will no doubt be "a significant amount of playtime languishing in accounts that is never used.".

As declared previously, people can stream GTA 6 to their Xbox console via a Game Pass membership or by purchasing time without a Game Pass membership. The pricing is below.

According to recent reports, coinciding with GTA 6's release and the new streaming deal, Microsoft just instituted limits on how many hours members can stream before being asked to pay more. These are:.

Even beyond the streaming deal, Xbox is the most affordable place to play GTA 6 considering that a new Xbox Series S console costs $500, compared to $600 for the cheapest new PS5.

GTA 6 officially introduces for everyone on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Meanwhile, you can check out our GTA 6 guides hub for more details on how to make the most out of your trip to Vice City.

Industry News: Virginia Feito on the Film Adaptation of Her Novel ‘Victorian Psycho’

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2110 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The writer is the lowest form of life on a movie.- Martin McDonagh.
  • Recent findings suggest that when I finished editing my second novel, Victorian Psycho, I could not imagine we would be shooting the film adaptation the following year, mere months after the book’s publication.
  • I decided then to undertake this journey that would take me metaphorically to Hollywood but geographically to a county just outside of Dublin, where we would recreate the Ensor House of my novel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The writer is the lowest form of life on a movie.- Martin McDonagh.

Recent findings suggest that when I finished editing my second novel, Victorian Psycho, I could not imagine we would be shooting the film adaptation the following year, mere months after the book’s publication. Generally, making a movie is one major miracle produced by an amalgamation of thousands of other tiny miracles. But when I met Zach Wigon, I understood that this was a joyfully tenacious person who was going to make this movie if it cost him his life.

I decided then to undertake this journey that would take me metaphorically to Hollywood but geographically to a county just outside of Dublin, where we would recreate the Ensor House of my novel. Among film stars, an Irish crew, and (rumored) ticks, the adaptation of Victorian Psycho—based on my screenplay, which is based on my novel, which is based on my ego, I guess—was born. Throughout the shoot I kept a sort of pseudo diary in order to remember every surreal detail from which I still haven’t recovered. I’ve chosen to reproduce some of it here.

Director Zach Wigon and producer Lisa Kelly call me from the set on the first day of shooting (Zach and I have agreed I won’t visit the set until after the first week so the cast and crew can acclimate without me hovering over them, because I am an intense fame whore, and also, I suppose, to signal I’m not important enough to pull a P.L. Travers and attempt to boycott the movie).

Over the phone, the producer indicates she can’t wait to meet in person. I tell her I’m underwhelming.

They promise to send me the dailies. I spend all day waiting for the dailies. The dailies never come.

It has been revealed that at around 9 p.m., I spiral because I don’t know whether to celebrate with Champagne or KFC. I decide to have both.

Industry observers note that I finally get the dailies. I fall in love with Maika Monroe’s character so hard it’s like I have an obsessive crush circa 2006 whose Facebook photos I’m compulsively looking at. But in this case it’s the same scene throughout five almost identical takes of Maika calling a 10-year-old boy a little idiot.

In a recent development, over the phone, Zach mentions concerns about a specific scene because we don’t have the budget for that many extras. I get carried away and suggest shipping over a whole battalion of free extras from Spain because, in my head, it’s going to be me and my friends, drunk and decked out in period clothing like we’re at a cheesy bachelorette party. One friend starts making childcare arrangements and another cancels her Holter monitor appointment so she can come to the shoot. What could go wrong?

I start to realize what could go wrong.

Sources indicate that I am informed we are probably no longer going to need the extras, and I feel a huge wave of relief as I uninvite my excited friends. I pack a suitcase for Ireland. It weighs 57 pounds.

I have a steak on the plane to Dublin at, like, 3 p.m., because when you’re flying business and somebody offers you steak, you take it.

The hotel room is wonderful, but I jokingly tell Zach over the phone that it’s on a first floor, so someone might crawl up and break in through the window and rape me, and he laughs at first but then is concerned and tells me to request a room on a higher floor, and I tell him it was a joke, but it wasn’t really.

In a recent development, I fill up the hotel room bathtub and call reception for a glass of red wine because I am a queen and I am queening. The glass doesn’t come, so in my anxious impatience I attempt to open a bottle of red wine sitting above the minibar. The cork crumbles because I’ve never understood how to use a corkscrew—like the compass in math class, I just faked my way through it my entire life and hoped for the best. So I call reception for another glass of red wine. They bring me all the glasses of wine and also properly uncork the bottle, and I watch Seinfeld in the bathtub while I drink red wine. I get drunk and paint my nails.

I arrive on set slightly Bromazepamed. It is extremely surreal to exist in a set labeled “Mr. Pounds’s Bedroom.” I am used to living in the fictional world inside my head but not used to it becoming more real than real life itself.

Recent findings suggest that maika hugs me when we meet, and I swallow a sob and refrain from smelling her hair (partly because it is, in fact, a wig). Everyone on set appears so happy to meet me, I suspect a Good Bye, Lenin! situation in which I have been diagnosed with cancer and for some reason the cast and crew all know but I don’t know. This isn’t the plot of Good Bye, Lenin!, but you’ll know what I mean if you’ve seen it.

Zach asks me to read the VOs in every scene, which means I’m in the scene with Ruth Wilson, Jason Isaacs, and Maika, and I’m about to have a stroke.

Jason eats for real in every single take and has already gulped down seven sausage rolls, so if I fuck up my VO, I will kill myself.

Suddenly experiencing fiction collectively feels very superior to experiencing it privately. This does not bode well for the rest of my career as a novelist.

Sources indicate that there is a scene in a cramped drawing room in which I must read the VO, but I’m supposed to hide from the camera, so I crawl on all fours behind an antique couch and grovel my way around the room while the boom op steps on my hands. I secretly think the boom op hates me because I’m always in his way and have an irritating habit of apologizing when he slams into me.

I start developing Irish inflections, so I say it, “I start developing Irish inflections,” but the Irish seem happy about it, so I pursue it.

Jason Isaacs starts doing card tricks between takes because Jason Isaacs is actually magic and also indefatigable. Only one thing could ever defeat Jason Isaacs, and it’s the ghost allegedly living on the third floor.

Even though Zach asked me to oversee the second unit, I don’t think anyone believes I’m actually going to do this—and between you and me, I don’t really even know what a second unit is. It doesn’t help I can’t concentrate on what we’re shooting because we’re in the middle of the woods and someone mentioned there were ticks, so I’m wrapping Sellotape around my ankles, hoping this way they won’t be able to crawl up my legs.

In a recent development, like your worst trauma, I insert myself into the movie forever via a small cameo. I literally just have to stand in a wig while I smile and nod, but I do it in such a way that I ruin every single take. “Just smile…like a normal person,” the second-unit director claims. I reason Zach can just cut me out of the movie, and I will only have wasted everybody’s time and money. There are worse things, like smiling normally but having no cameo. I cope by chewing on another Bromazepam and another chocolate bar. (Every morning I take the chocolate bar from the hotel minibar. It will invariably become an asset in the long afternoons on set, kind of like in prison or high school.).

According to recent reports, I change hotel rooms because I have developed an intense FOMO with which I’m always fearing there is a better hotel room for the same price somewhere in the vicinity. This FOMO is also rampant on set between the different units—in the first unit, you have the cinematographer, Nico Aguilar, laughing in the sunlight, talking about color palettes, while in the second unit, we’re shooting clocks and screaming at each other because we still have 17 establishing shots to go.

Recent findings suggest that anyway, I change hotel rooms, and the upcoming room is so superior to my previous room it’s like an entirely new hotel. I consider changing hotel rooms further. Perhaps I can somehow upgrade my way into a presidential suite.

Sources indicate that my parents visit the set. My dad peers over his glasses at the fake lobster cake, and when I tell him the toilets are in trailers, he sighs gravely.

According to recent reports, jason Isaacs convinces my dad to take up tennis again even though my dad’s not supposed to play tennis after his seven hernias. But my dad is so inspired by this actor, who is not a doctor but whose performance in The Patriot my dad can’t help but praise at least once a month, that he will immediately start playing tennis again upon his return to Spain, and whatever medical problems arise henceforth shall all be Jason Isaacs’s fault.

At the Shelbourne restaurant that night, my mom tells the sommelier how she can’t drink red wine anymore because it makes her anxious, and he kneels on the floor beside her and places a hand on his heart as if she were confiding something intimate to him like her fear of death.

Suddenly, real life feels less real than fictional life.

Sources indicate that obama is visiting Dublin and he’s booked the entire floor, so he essentially kicks me out of the Shelbourne (probably to stay in the JFK Suite next door to my room, which is disappointingly predictable), so I go to The Hoxton, because what is life if you’re not constantly changing hotel rooms? The Hoxton is really lovely, but I get OCD about the light bulbs in the room because they appear mismatched, so I ask housekeeping to change them, but they claim not to have any extra light bulbs, which sounds suspect—like, what do they do if a light bulb suddenly goes out? Do they just never replace it?

We end the shoot at 5 a.m. I am wearing a thick puffer coat and a thermal T-shirt and a furry hat, plus fur-lined boots over my Sellotaped ankles, although I wonder, If ticks can survive this temperature, they kind of deserve to live off my blood. Nobody else seems as concerned about the cold as me, but then again, most of them are Irish.

Sadly, when we wrap, we are all so exhausted everyone races to clean up and leave, and it is sort of anticlimactic. I don’t know what I was expecting, but balloons falling from the skies did flash through my mind.

In the car on the way to our respective quarters, Zach and I look out the window, wide-eyed, like kidnapped children. Zach starts discussing a fresh project for us. I wonder if he is a sociopath.

In a recent development, I type this over a year later, sitting at my desk in Madrid, striving to work on my next novel. I feel empty inside knowing there is no car to pick me up and take me to set and thereby escape reality for extended periods of time, until set becomes reality and reality becomes a limbo in which you wait for said reality.

Industry observers note that I am working on a novel, but also on four newly introduced scripts. I hope to return to reality someday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The level of talent on Season 30 of NBC’s long-running singing competition The Voice, right now airing on the 2026 TV schedule, is undeniable. The cuts have been "brutal," and some really incredible singers already went home before the Live Reveals even started. The success of the show isn’t solely about the contestants. We also tune in to for the fun coach interactions, all of which has been noticeably absent during the live performances, disappointingly so.

Honestly, this is a problem that's typical with The Voice during live indicates, but I'd forgotten given the network dropped them for Season 29. As the competition narrows and the numbers of remaining singers gets smaller, I hope there will be an opportunity for this to return. Let's talk it out.

Earlier this season, Kelly Clarkson and newbie Riley Green really upped The Voice coach prank game. Whether it was a personalized gift from the American Idol winner attempting to help a fellow coach get over losing top-notch singers during the Blind Auditions, or it was the country music superstar using his duck call for a laugh, those moments have been glaringly lacking from the Live Shows.

Honestly, the biggest disappointment of the Live Shows doesn’t have anything to do with the performances themselves. There hasn’t been a bad performance. It instead comes from the fact that the episodes breeze by so quickly that there hasn’t been time for coach banter or any of the silly moments that we’ve come to love.

Industry observers note that again, this season has been particularly fun with Clarkson’s zany antics, including trying to give a contestant her hair, and Green never missing the chance to poke fun at Adam Levine’s age. It also would have been the perfect opportunity for Adam to throw it in Riley’s face (or at least console him) that his team still has three singers left while the latter only has two.

Don’t get me wrong, the Live Reveals have seen all the contestants step up as they perform with musicians and back-up singers while vying for viewer votes. But the lack of coach banter is an obvious and unfortunate mistake that I hope the show fixes soon.

It has been revealed that with the Blind Auditions, Battles, and Cut Week having two-hour episodes, cutting the Live Reveals to one hour doesn’t even allow for much coach commentary and feedback. To me that's a major problem. When it comes time to announce which singers have made it through for another week and who’s going to be sent home, there’s barely the time to even say goodbye, right?

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

So, then it becomes just another instance of shaving time away from the coaches. While it’s been stated that the Live Highlights were brought back by demand from the fans, it feels like there’s a better way that it could have been handled so that it didn’t feel so jarring. Like maybe finding a happy medium with 90-minute episodes? Survivor does it!

You can keep following along with the competition on NBC on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET, or stream the next day with a Peacock subscription, until the winner is announced in December. The competition series will then be shaking things up with Season 31’s The Voice: Celebrity with latest host Keke Palmer, and I hope that version will keep the coach banter game going.

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6.

It’d just slow him down. You know, the time it takes him to explain something, he could just make shit quicker. You can see it on the screen, man, it’s so fuckin’ raw.”.

Industry observers note that jason, ever-stoic, doesn’t seem fully convinced, mostly going along with things for the enjoyment of spending time with his buddy. I wasn’t really convinced either when GTA VI forced me into the short intro of Tenebrae Lux. But despite the entire thing mostly existing as a completely unsubtle barb directed at one indie game auteur in particular, Tenebrae LuxÂ hooked me immediately by showing off a series of surprisingly mind-bending puzzles. While some (Cal) might expect such things from a genius like Zuch, I wasn’t at all prepared to bust out my puzzle notebook while playing Grand Theft Auto VI!

It has been revealed that like most in-universe media in GTA VI, Tenebrae LuxÂ is a giant, heaving mass of satire. Rendered in black and white and dripping with angst, it follows a Man Who Won’t Shut The Fuck Up who has washed up on an island decorated by some crumbling shacks and a single lighthouse whose beam swings rhythmically ’round the dark landscape as you explore. It’s moody as hell: swaying grass, dark and ominous music, too-bright lights in the distance indicating where you might want to poke around, and a haunting crying sound of some sort in the background. Hell, before you even get to any of that, you’re shown what I’m sure is intended to be a very deep and meaningful quote scrawled across the opening screen: “Every tale begins with an unwritten page quietly awaiting the ink of destiny…” -R.T. Gravenhurst, The Teachings of Twmffat. Apparently, “Twmffat” is a Welsh way to call someone an idiot. Excellent.

The majority of the segment you play with Cal is focused on hammering home the satire. As your character noisily broods his way down the beach, introductory credits roll, attributing every single bit of the gameâfrom the leading voice performance to the writing, music, and “mise-en-scene”âto Johannes Zuch. The initial moody atmosphere and beach themes, as well as the single auteur name on all the credits, made me think at first that the game was lampooning Hideo Kojima, and there’s a little bit of Mark Danielewski going on here too. But as I got into the actual gameplay (and read the name on the credits a few more times) I clocked the actual joke here. “Johannes Zuch” is not-so-subtle when you say it out loud with a short u in Zuch.

"You have just experienced a Johannes Zuch experience...".

2-3 hours, including time spent maniacally scribbling in a notebook.

All of this is quite funny, and works pretty well for a 10-minute-long-or-so joke sequence that you then cut off to go snuggle in a bed with your bestie and get your girl out of prison. But you gotta dive back in once you’ve left. That’s where the good stuff is. It starts with a couple of basic grid-based puzzles that involve moving pieces around a board to clear all of them. I assumed, wrongly, that the game would just be a bunch of harder variations on that. But then I crossed the beach and entered what seemed like some sort of war bunker, and everything changed.

Or, rather, it stayed…eerily the same.

Sources indicate that tenebrae LuxÂ features what I would consider two major puzzles, with two smaller ones bookending them, but boy, those two major puzzles are doozies. One involves looping through the same room, over and over, trying to figure out a six-digit code needed to proceed while eerie sea shanties wail in your ears and a crazed man yells at you from the other side of a door. The other involves a bridge covered in glowing symbols requiring a specific pattern to cross, found by navigating a nearby ruin and deciphering a deceptively simple poem. In both cases (but especially in the looping rooms), the solutions require a bit of lateral thinking and very close observation to fully work out. I spent a good couple hours on these last night!

What I found most clever about the looping rooms in particular is that the puzzle seems to be different for every player. Checking online, it sounds like the various objects in the room (which are key to solving the puzzle) change depending on your playthrough. Some people had a painting that never appeared in mine, and I had record albums that others never saw. This helps the solution dodge easily researchable answers online but also immediately confused my efforts at information-sharing as I texted friends who had already seen the room for help. It’s a cool trick!

Sources indicate that the finale of Tenebrae LuxÂ was as silly and pretentious as the start, though I did find the aesthetics of its final puzzle to be pretty cool in spite of that. The in-universe idea of Tenebrae Lux, by design, indicates nothing about anything. There’s no deeper meaning to its constant prattling about darkness and light and fate and horror and whatnot. But in saying nothing, the existence of Tenebrae LuxÂ within the context of GTA VI manages to land a pretty stellar blow on a very specific and recognizable kind of auteur culture, while simultaneously providing a few excellent hours of puzzling. Allegedly there’s some sort of secret ending if I go back and collect a bunch of notes, and I find myself…weirdly compelled to do this?

Industry observers note that so: inscrutable and entirely meaningless thematically, up-its-own-ass creatively, but with some pretty excellent puzzling despite that? Yup. That’s a Johannes Zuch game.

Getting your money for nothing and your chicks for free does not make for great game design.

Early leaks indicated Jason rocking out with his hog out, but can you actually do that in the final game?

They just want you to finish them off, daddy.

The divide between Jason and Lucia feels pretty lopsided at the beginning.

That day, a whole room sat behind us. Afterward, Melissa told reporters that for the first time, she held the power in a room with him. I felt it too.

This month, nine years after #MeToo took off, a jury in London convicted Russell Brand of one rape and three sexual assaults. A judge sentenced him to ten and a half years in prison. His crimes went back to 2004. Brand’s attorneys argued the women had waited too long to be believed. I waited twenty years. Delay is often the most ordinary fact in these cases.

Industry observers note that in the midterms, Ohio elected Amy Acton governor. A few weeks before the vote, her opponent’s campaign ran an ad in which her estranged mother called her a liar. Acton’s stepfather had been charged with raping her when she was a child. Republicans and Democrats both condemned the ad. She won anyway.

I watched the returns on election night and thought about the girls at Miss Hall’s who told the truth and were called liars. Survivors get called liars all the time. We almost never get to watch one win.

Recent findings suggest that tarana Burke knew survivors weren’t being believed long before most people were listening. She started saying “me too” in 2006 to reach Black girls who had survived sexual violence, more than ten years before it became a hashtag. Every survivor who spoke after her made it a little easier for the next one.

In November 2024, a Cornell student told campus police and the Title IX office that she had been gang-raped at a fraternity house weeks earlier. No one has been charged. Cornell’s president set up a task force on sexual assault, but he later admitted he never checked how her case ended.

When I read that, I was back at Miss Hall’s on graduation day, waiting for a phone call that nobody made.

Industry observers note that the Epstein survivors know that silence too. For decades, powerful people looked away. Last year survivors pushed Congress to pass a law requiring the Justice Department to release its Epstein files. Millions of pages came out. There have been no arrests in the United States.

In a recent development, I’m still hopeful. Survivors everywhere keep coming forward, and some of the people in charge are finally acting. My body knew what Rutledge had done to me long before I let myself say it aloud. I didn’t have the words. Survivors today do, and they have each other. Melissa found me.

According to recent reports, the criminal case against Rutledge isn’t over. His lawyer has asked a judge to dismiss all charges. We don’t know yet whether there will be a trial. Whatever the judge decides, I’ve already reached my own verdict. I’m healing and Rutledge doesn’t get a say in that.

It has been revealed that for most of my life, I carried shame that was never mine. He handed it to me. Every adult who looked away handed me a little more.

In a recent development, predators don’t work alone. Someone always sees something. In the movie Spotlight, a lawyer indicates that if it takes a village to raise a child, it takes a village to abuse one. My village saw. The people in charge did nothing.

Sources indicate that I’ve given the shame back. It belongs to him, and to the people who could have stopped him.

If you are a survivor and you are still carrying shame, you can put it down.

Borrow my courage if you need it. Melissa lent me hers.

Neither Matthew Rutledge nor Jean Norris responded to Vanity Fair for the original story, and neither of them has made direct statements to the press. Norris, through her attorney, claimed not to know that Rutledge abused students.

GTA 6’s Best Song Is A Nelly Furtado Cover From Azerbaijan

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1290 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of the mainstay features in Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto series is radio stations that can be listened to while driving in cars or, as in GTA 6, on the go if you acquire headphones.
  • It has been revealed that one of the mainstay features in Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto series is radio stations that can be listened to while driving in cars or, as in GTA 6, on the go if you acquire headphones.
  • One of the radio stations you'll find in the game is Kaleidoscope FM.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the mainstay features in Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto series is radio stations that can be listened to while driving in cars or, as in GTA 6, on the go if you acquire headphones. As a music-discovery vehicle, GTA: Vice City introduced me to many '80s classics across a variety of genres. With GTA 6 taking players to Leonida, in which Vice City is located, it's apt that the game features music that many probably would never hear anywhere else. One of the radio stations you'll find in the game is Kaleidoscope FM. It features covers of very-well-known songs that are performed by artists from around the world. It's a fantastic hook for a radio station and delivers some of the catchiest and most-unexpected covers from artists that have a pretty low profile outside of their home countries. The first song I heard on the station, and the one that remains my absolute favorite, is a cover of Nelly Furtado's "Say It Right" from Azerbaijani artists Alim Qasimov and Farghana Qasimova. The duo are known for performing Mugham, a type of music that blends poetry, melody, and improvisation. I had never heard of them before playing GTA 6, but the music instantly transported me to my youth listening to Qawwali, a type of music that is rooted in Islamic sufism. Initially, my exposure to Qawwali, a type of music that is over 600 years old, was limited to my own home, but it has since gained a worldwide following thanks to Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, who is known as the King of Kings of Qawwali. These days it's pretty common to hear songs that either sample or are inspired by Qawwali, but, even so, hearing Mugham in GTA 6 was a huge surprise. I didn't expect to be playing Rockstar's latest opus and be reminded of Qawwali. https://www.youtube.com/watch?is=GsirJ2mQmdOdZt1a&v=6iA9fogYpLA I already love "Say It Right"--I think it's one of Furtado and producers Timbaland and Danja's best--but this cover draws out the melancholic soul that underpins the original, giving it a more emotional weight. Much of that can be attributed to the religious mysticism that both Mugham and Qawwali evoke. What I appreciate about this cover is how brilliantly it allows the unfamiliar to grasp what makes Mugham and Qawwali so beautiful by presenting it through a song that many people already have some familiarity with. Both types of music are performed by an ensemble, but the improvisational nature means that others are encouraged to contribute. The use of the kamancheh, tar, and daf, along with the vocals covering Furtado's chorus and the khananda's additions, come together to make the cover feel magical. There are other songs that will no doubt catch you by surprise on Kaleidoscope FM--another favourite is a South Asian cover of "Careless Whisper." Naturally, I was intrigued by how this station came to be and, according to Ivan Pavlovich, Rockstar's vice president of music, it stems from an obsession that studio co-founder Sam Houser has. “Historically, we have always loved to champion a quirky, concept-driven station," Pavlovich told GameSpot. "Sam loves foreign-language covers of his favorite songs and thought this could be that station for GTA VI. Tracking down rights holders proved particularly tricky in certain countries." The biggest surprise, however, is the radio station's host: Academy Award winner Jeremy Irons. "Jeremy Irons has the perfect voice as the travel-weathered host telling tall tales of his adventures from around the world," Pavlovich added. "Jeremy loved the script, and nailed the wry humor of his character in one session. Hopefully, this station makes fans smile as much as we did when we were making it." Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews are available now. GameSpot gave it a 10/10, saying that it sets the standard for open worlds impossibly high.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One day in August 2019, Mark Epstein was having breakfast at a Virginia hotel when he looked at the TV and saw CNN reporting that his older brother, Jeffrey Epstein, had died by suicide in a Manhattan federal prison. As jarring as the news was, he had no reason to doubt it.

Industry observers note that “I knew he wouldn’t want to live the rest of his life in jail,” Mark told Vanity Fair this week. “He had no children to worry about. Our parents were gone. He knew he didn’t have to worry about me.”.

It has been revealed that mark says he finished his omelet and headed back to New York. Then, like so many other Americans, he started to become skeptical of the official narrative.

In a recent development, over the last seven years, the endless conspiracy theories surrounding Jeffrey Epstein’s death have largely been relegated to the backwaters of YouTube and Reddit, while local and federal authorities have stuck to the suicide story. But this week there was a breakthrough. On Monday, Michael Freeman, a leading forensic scientist who testified for the prosecution in the trial of Derek Chauvin for the murder of George Floyd, issued the most legitimate challenge to date to the prevailing consensus.

Freeman presented his findings at a historic London legal society, saying, “The pattern and distribution and multitude of injuries are not explained by a suicidal hanging.” In a New York Times story published the same day as the presentation, Freeman told the publication that he had no view on who might have killed Jeffrey: “All I’m interested in is, how did this get so sideways?” Along with several global news outlets, including CBS and the BBC, the paper covered the presentation with a straight face even as it noted that Freeman’s efforts to publish his findings in a peer-reviewed journal had thus far been rejected.

The relationship between Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein has loomed large over the president’s second term.

In his thick Brooklyn accent, Mark Epstein, who has long been trying to prove that his brother was murdered while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges, excitedly recounted this fresh development over the phone the day after Freeman’s presentation, which he attended.

According to recent reports, “This crosses all party lines,” Mark mentioned. “Most people believe he didn’t commit suicide. So it’s a mystery. People want an answer to that. I think now they have the answer.”.

Mark emphasized that the story of the recent findings was not about him but rather about his brother’s death and Freeman’s work. It was Freeman who reached out to him, Mark said, based on what the scientist independently thought was shoddy work on Jeffrey’s autopsy, and Mark agreed to turn over all the records, reports, and photographs he had as next of kin.

Recent findings suggest that “I want to make it really clear,” he remarked. “I didn’t pay for this. He’s never asked me for anything other than the information, which I gave him willingly. And he’s been studying this. As a matter of fact, the night before last was the first time I ever met him face-to-face.”.

Still, Mark has made his suspicions both his calling card and his personal mission in recent years. After working in real estate investing and serving as the chair of Cooper Union’s board of trustees, he had his own business dealings come under some scrutiny as Jeffrey’s life and crimes dominated political and cultural discourse beginning in the late 2010s—Jeffrey allegedly housed models and employees in an Upper East Side building that was predominantly owned by his brother’s real estate holding company. In the years since his brother’s death, Mark has said that Jeffrey “definitely had dirt” on Donald Trump, and he became a minor fixation amid the Epstein files rollout on account of emails containing banter between him and his brother. (Trump has denied any prior knowledge of Jeffrey’s crimes and said that the release of the Epstein files “totally exonerated” him.) Mark has dismissed a suicide note purportedly written by Jeffrey as a fabrication.

Jeffrey’s death certificate initially remarked “pending further study” in regard to the cause of death, rather than ruling it a homicide or suicide, but the chief medical examiner ruled it a suicide days later. “All the pathologists I’ve spoken to,” says Mark, “they said, [if] an initial death certificate says ‘pending further study,’ you don’t get an answer usually for weeks or more because something’s being studied.” Mark hired the celebrity forensic pathologist Michael Baden to observe and evaluate the autopsy, and Baden previously stated that “the evidence points to homicide.” Federal officials’ handling of the matter in the years to come only amplified Mark’s concern.

“You know a suicide when you see one,” FBI director Kash Patel mentioned last year while he was under fire for not producing any proof of the Epstein conspiracies he had been touting during his time as a mere conservative podcast personality, “and that’s what that was.”.

“I actually laughed out loud when I heard that,” Mark said, “because I thought, How many suicides has this fucking jackass actually seen?”.

So who does Mark think killed his brother?

“It’s like in a Mob hit,” he stated. “You try to find who the hit man was, and then you try to find who ordered the hit.” The hit man, he figured, could only be someone among a limited number of people: prison employees and other prisoners who had been on Jeffrey’s security tier. “Then the question becomes,” said Mark, “who would have the ability to orchestrate this in a federal prison, and who would have the ability to have the DOJ cover it up?” He couldn’t think of anyone besides Trump. (Trump has not been accused of any wrongdoing in connection to Jeffrey’s death; in a 2023 interview with Tucker Carlson, when asked whether Jeffrey could have been killed, he said, “Oh sure, it’s possible. I mean, I don’t really believe—I think he probably committed suicide.”).

I thought Mark and I had developed some rapport over the conversation, particularly after I mentioned that I’d attended the same Coney Island middle school where he and his brother had been students; I emphasized that I was trying to listen to him carefully and take him seriously. But there was a bit more rancor in his tone after I remarked it was still difficult to believe that the Department of Justice could have successfully covered up the murder of the most high-profile prisoner in the world.

“If you don’t think that after what I just told you,” Mark noted, “then you, sir, are a fucking idiot also.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Grand Theft Auto games have regularly kept up with the times, and in GTA 6, you once again have a smartphone that you can use to interact with the world around you.
  • As a quick reminder, you can whip out your smartphone by using the Up key on the D-pad.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto games have regularly kept up with the times, and in GTA 6, you once again have a smartphone that you can use to interact with the world around you. From getting new missions to goofing off by wasting some in-game time on social media, the smartphone in GTA 6 is a pretty handy tool for rising up the social--and criminal--ranks of Leonida. It comes equipped with several apps, and while not every one of them is essential, you'll want to keep an eye open for certain notifications. Here's a closer look at what each app does. How to use your smartphone As a quick reminder, you can whip out your smartphone by using the Up key on the D-pad. From there, you can navigate through the apps menu using the directional keys. GTA 6 smartphone apps WAiNK The bread-and-butter app for aspiring car thieves, the WAiNK app can be used to inspect vehicles for any hidden security features. Scanning a car will let you see its estimated value, which security features it has installed, if it's locked, and how much it'll cost to register it under your name. Scooter Bros Need your personal vehicle in a hurry? A call to Scooter Bros will allow you to summon your ride to your location, so long as you don't mind the couriers stashing their little two-wheeled ride in your trunk. Whatup GTA 6's instant messaging app, this will allow you to get scoops and chat to characters, without ever needing to verbally engage with them. It's also useful for getting new missions and tips on how to make some quick cash with side-activities. Camera It's a camera. It can take selfies. What else were you expecting? Gallery Nothing too surprising here, as the Gallery app is used for checking out all the smartphone pictures you took. It also has a few archived pictures, which show off Jason and Lucia's life prior to the events that kicked off the GTA 6 storyline. Fitness Staying in shape is highly recommended in GTA 6, and this fitness app will allow you to track your gains and how your stats are steadily leveling up from all those deadlifting sessions. Snapmatic Do a little doomscrolling on the side with the social media app, which has a feed full of Leonida's citizens posting about their daily lives, as well as plenty of memes and brainrot content. You can even like posts and read the comments attached to them--if you dare. News Leonida is a busy city, and the news app will let you keep track of all the latest developments. Weather How many seasons can you expect in a single day? Check the weather app to find out. Settings It's not too detailed, but the option to change Jason's wallpaper and ringtone in the settings menu is a nice little touch. While the smartphone will be a handy companion, you can also check out our GTA 6 guides hub for even more tips and tricks. It's being constantly updated with new walkthroughs and features, so if you want to check out the full list of GTA 6 radio stations, how to increase your wanted level, and much more, the answers are only a click away.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prince Harry is sharing details about his return to the U.K. alongside wife Meghan Markle and their two children.

Industry observers note that “It’s good being back on home soil. I’m throwing myself into the winter weather. … I have missed the winters,” Harry, 42, said on the Friday, November 20, episode of ITV’s This Morning in his first live televised interview since he and Meghan moved from California to Britain in August.

“Look at us Brits, talking about the weather!” he quipped to cohosts Alison Hammond and Dermot O’Leary.

In a recent development, harry, 42, and Meghan, 45, returned to the U.K. in August after six years in California. The couple’s children — Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5 — began school in the U.K. for the first time the following month.

During his This Morning appearance, Harry gave an update on how the kids are settling in to life in the U.K.

Industry observers note that “They love being back,” he mentioned. “It’s a big culture shift. I think that the kids in school uniforms is a big change for them, but it’s certainly helped. The confidence in both of them has gone through the roof since they’ve been in U.K. school, which is really, really nice.”.

Hammond, 51, then asked Harry whether Archie and Lilibet’s accents have changed since moving.

Sources indicate that “I’m squeezing the accents out of them, and their friends at school are doing the same,” Harry joked. “Lili does a good impression of ‘Mummy.’”.

As for his plans for his Christmas back in the U.K., Harry shared that Meghan and his mother-in-law, Doria Ragland, will be in charge of cooking.

Recent findings suggest that “My wife’s very good in the kitchen and so is my mother-in-law, so I’ll leave it to them. There’ll be a gumbo,” he remarked, adding that there will also be “every range of turkey you can imagine — full, roasted turkey, pulled turkey [and] smoked turkey.”.

Sources indicate that elsewhere, Harry shared his support for Robert Pattinson as the newly introduced James Bond. “I can’t wait to see it,” he enthused.

He also subtly shouted out Meghan, sharing that he prefers her former hit show Suits to the British soap opera EastEnders.

Harry previously addressed his return to the U.K. in an interview with GQ in October.

“I think that certainly, our attitude has changed,” he told the magazine. “I think once you’ve been through it, once you’ve been able to talk about it and raise awareness to it, then people see it for what it is. It makes the environment slightly easier. It’s not going to necessarily stop the behavior, but I think the behavior might — my hope [is] that it will — change.”.

It has been revealed that “Being able to put the kids in a British school has meant a lot to me,” Harry added. “I didn’t know how key it was to me. I always thought it was gonna be something that I would try and do or that we would try and do, but now they’ve been in school for two weeks.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that “That is the highest compliment you could give anyone!” Lux Pascal says after I tell her she looks like Jessica Paré’s Megan Draper from Mad Men.
  • The Pierre Yovanovitch–designed restaurant is a verified New York power room at the moment: There’s Derek Blasberg talking to Sarah Pidgeon about books—War and Peace gets a name-check—and Architectural Digest’s Amy Astley in a corner with Metropolitan Museum of Art board member Robert Denning.
  • Laura Love and Devon Lee Carlson on November 17, 2026, in Newly introduced York City (Photo by Dimitrios Kambouris/WireImage).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that “That is the highest compliment you could give anyone!” Lux Pascal says after I tell her she looks like Jessica Paré’s Megan Draper from Mad Men. We’re at Chanel’s Watches and Fine Jewelry holiday dinner, held at Daniel Humm’s latest eponymous restaurant, Humm, in the West Village. Pascal is in a ’60s black modish leather minidress that she’s paired with a cat eye. On her wrists are Chanel’s Première Galon watch and Coco Crush bracelets, which, like her rings and earrings, are all dotted with diamonds. As I look around, most of the celebrities dressed by the brand are wearing looks that show off their French fine accessories. Ella Rubin, the Gen Z star of the hit teen TV show Sterling Point, has upgraded a simple pair of vintage Levi’s with a sleek black-and-gold Première Ribbon watch and several diamond rings. This is not a night for hidden gems.

The Pierre Yovanovitch–designed restaurant is a verified New York power room at the moment: There’s Derek Blasberg talking to Sarah Pidgeon about books—War and Peace gets a name-check—and Architectural Digest’s Amy Astley in a corner with Metropolitan Museum of Art board member Robert Denning. Indrė Rockefeller is here, as is stylist Vanessa Traina. In a feat of fun seating arrangements, the Chanel team has sat Rubin next to another young Ella: Beatty, the recent star of Monster and daughter of Warren Beatty and Annette Bening. (Although, with all due respect to those lovely Ellas, the two neighbors I’d most like to eavesdrop on are Devon Lee Carlson and Jack Harlow.) At the bar I hear two fashion people gossiping about industry hiring rumors: “Lauren Sherman notes there’s two people in the running,” they whisper about some gig. I think I know what they’re talking about, but not enough to print it.

Laura Love and Devon Lee Carlson on November 17, 2026, in Newly introduced York City (Photo by Dimitrios Kambouris/WireImage).

Guests mill about because there’s much to mill about: Humm’s filled his restaurant with dozens of notable, site-specific artworks. Louise Bourgeois supplied 24 watercolor paintings, as well as a fantastical sterling silver cast of one of her sculptures, situated by the bar. (Tonight it’s serving mezcal sours with guava and an apple brandy highball.) Francesco Clemente painted not one, not two, but four celestial murals across two months, with motifs of abstract stars, animals, trains, and clocks. On the walls in the main dining room are 12 pigment drawings by Roni Horn. Then there’s all the work by Rashid Johnson: In the lounge—which for this event doubles as a red carpet—hangs his painting Untitled Homes. With Yovanovitch, he also built a custom host stand cast in aluminum and painted red. It’s so textural that you can see the fingerprints, and a number of guests gather around it as the maître d’ explains Johnson’s artistic process like he’s a docent at The Met.

Chanel has decorated the tables with long taper candles and arrangements of deep fuchsia peonies and burgundy garden roses. Waiters serve Humm’s signature everything caviar bagels. When I think about ordering something other than the chicken, a waiter tells me not to. He’s right.

Singer-songwriter girlsweetvoiced.

At the end of the night, after most guests are a few glasses of red wine (or martinis) deep, Pidgeon herself grabs a microphone. The event, as it turns out, has a surprise performer: girlsweetvoiced. “She captures something that’s very honest,” Pidgeon notes of the emerging singer-songwriter, who then belts out a cover of Joni Mitchell’s “California.” Title aside, it’s been a very Latest York night.

  • In case you missed it, a media meteor impacted yesterday and blasted our landscape free of life.
  • Industry observers note that "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop", remarked Cohen, remarking that players ought to be able to do with their purchased games as they will: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GameStop boss Ryan Cohen (last seen attempting to buy eBay) has called for the return of physical game discs, lamenting the lack of control players have over digital purchases in a chat with Bloomberg held on the eve of Grand Theft Auto 6's release.

In case you missed it, a media meteor impacted yesterday and blasted our landscape free of life. Grand Theft Auto 6 is here and—despite our Ted Litchfield's noble attempts to get you all thinking about Queen's Domain instead (you should play Queen's Domain)—it's all the world can talk about. It's also only available digitally.

Industry observers note that "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop", remarked Cohen, remarking that players ought to be able to do with their purchased games as they will: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend". Cohen did not namecheck GTA 6 specifically, but did say that he had been speaking about this problem with all "the obvious" publishers.

GameStop, of course, makes a tidy chunk of change from resales of games traded in at its stores—a segment of its business that becomes impossible to maintain in a world without physical discs for players to bring in and sell. Publishers oppose trade-ins "because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new", states Cohen, accusing them of "taking away competition" by restricting sales to digital-only channels.

GTA 6 is a portent of the world to come. Earlier this year, Sony confirmed that PlayStation would drop physical discs starting in January 2028, and has held firm to that course in the face of a vocal player uproar.

Complications around game ownership have reached the point that politicians are weighing in: last month US lawmaker Richie Torres announced the Power To The Players Act, that would prompt the US Federal Trade Commission to protect players' access to purchased games, even in the case of online-only games that get unplugged.

"When you pay for a game, you should own it", said Torres. "Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy. A game that can be taken away the moment a manufacturer pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, latest arrivals are landing in the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog this month, but at the same time, you can also expect a few departures from that gaming library. Fortunately, the number of games leaving soon are on the smaller side, as there'll be only three exits in total. Unfortunately, one of those games that you're running out of time to play through the Game Catalog is a massive and pretty fun fantasy title, so get those hours in while you can. PlayStation Plus Game Catalog games leaving soon Granblue Fantasy Relink Granblue Fantasy Relink Somerville Fade to Silence This month's biggest departure is Granblue Fantasy Relink, a massive fantasy game with a storybook art style, cinematic boss fights, and a large roster of characters who all possess unique abilities to master. First released in February 2024, Granblue Fantasy Relink is built around real-time combat and flashy team-up mechanics, making for a visually striking experience overall. While the story isn't much to write home about, it's the gameplay and worldbuilding where this Granblue spin-off shines, and it got even better earlier this year with the Endless Ragnarok expansion. In comparison, Somerville is a story-rich puzzle game that's oozing atmosphere with its slick art direction, and Fade to Silence is a single-player and co-op survival-crafting adventure set in a post-apocalyptic world that is feeling the chill of an eternal winter. While the Game Catalog is going to be a little poorer without those three titles, it is getting some great games this month. Death Stranding 2: On the Beach is the headline act, and it'll be joined by several more titles like Atomfall, Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake, and Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii. All PlayStation Plus subscribers can also grab a trio of freebies between now and November 30: Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider 4-6 Remastered, and Monster Train 2.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Video game consoles are more expensive than ever, but sales are growing regardless, at least in the US. Circana has released its report for US video game industry sales in October, confirming that PS5 unit sales increased by 5% compared to October 2025. That's despite the average selling price of a PS5 increasing by 13%. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY Xbox Series X|S unit sales jumped by 10% in October 2026 compared to October 2025, and the average selling price rose by 29% year-over-year. The Switch 2 was October 2026's top console in unit and dollar sales, and it remains 2026's best-performing console by those measurements, followed by PS5. However, Circana did not break out the specifics for Switch 2 unit sales or average selling price changes. Total hardware spending in the US on game consoles was up by 2%, reaching $357 million. Higher pricing drove the dollar sales growth, Circana stated, noting that PS5 dollar sales rose by 20% and Xbox Series X|S jumped by 42%. However, Switch 2 sales, measured by dollar sales, fell by 11%. Looking back to September 2026, PS5 hardware dollar sales grew by 43%, while spending on Xbox Series X|S dropped by 2% and Switch 2 fell by 12%. It will be interesting to see the November US hardware data when it comes in, as experts have said the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S could get a jolt in sales from people buying systems to play GTA 6. However, Circana has warned that sales might not be as strong as expected due to the increased prices. Microsoft, Sony, and Nintendo have raised prices on their consoles due in part to the ongoing memory and component shortages from the AI buildout. Tariffs have also played a role. On the subject of tariffs, all three received refunds from the government after the Supreme Court deemed the tariffs illegal, but those companies are keeping the money and not giving anything back to you. The companies argued that people who paid more knew what they were doing and don't deserve to get any money back.

This is why, despite Bond being one of the most popular film characters of all time, you will rarely see ordinary men dare to take him on as a Halloween costume. There’s simply more to making Bond than a good tux.

Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the next era of the franchise, now under the creative control of Amazon MGM, and Robert Pattinson has been chosen to reincarnate the character conceived by Ian Fleming in 1953. In the announcement clip for Pattinson’s casting, the actor looks the part in a black tuxedo and white shirt, but it’s his eyes, which pierce through the camera rather than down the barrel of his gun, that do most of the talking and offer a suggestion of what Pattinson’s Bond may have to offer. Will he be a little darker and tortured, like his take on Batman? Or perhaps his Bond will be louche and somewhat pricklier.

In a recent development, A safer bet to make is that he will look good. One of the most enduring legacies of the James Bond franchise is how stylish both the character of Bond and the universe built around him have always been. Bond has appeared classic and timeless in style during each of the franchise’s eras, but hindsight offers a much richer perspective.

Pierce Brosnan, The World Is Not Enough, 1999.

Daniel Craig, Casino Royale, 2006.

It has been revealed that as portrayed through the decades in the property’s famous title sequence, Bond is a silhouette—a classic, timeless silhouette. Fleming established the look in his development of the character when he made the suit his primary uniform. But it is Terence Young, the director of the first 007 films, who is responsible for the visual definition of Bond.

In a recent development, when Connery was cast as Bond for the first film, Dr. No (1962), Young, an avid wearer of suits himself, took him to his own tailor, Anthony Sinclair. We can credit Sinclair with developing the original silver screen Bond look: The suit was lighter in fit and tailoring than most other English suits at the time. The Bond suit had a soft shoulder and waist, but a strong, wide chest and a low button stance that elongated its wearer. Every Bond suit that’s followed has been measured to the standard of Sinclair’s work, and every Bond actor has had to compete with Connery’s charisma while wearing it.

Roger Moore, The Spy Who Loved Me, 1977.

Sources indicate that brosnan and his Brioni suits were indicative of the 1990s corporate look of the time. Craig wore Brioni too, but only for Casino Royale; Tom Ford created his subsequent suiting, which often stood out for the slim fit popular in the 2010s. Most memorable sartorially is Roger Moore’s take through the ’70s and ’80s, which often deviated from the sleekness that had come to define Bond by creating a little frisson with lighter, brighter fabrics and a bolder sense of playfulness.

Sources indicate that the character of Bond, and the actor personifying him at a given time, have also become representative of a certain male standard: Connery in the ’60s, tan and athletic, or Brosnan in the ’90s, polished with lithe elegance. And then came Craig, whose casting was met with skepticism, to put it lightly. His arrival was marked by the image of the actor walking out of the ocean in tight swim trunks in Casino Royale. His strong legs, rounded shoulders, and sculpted, hairless chest cemented then and there the idea of what a leading man had become and would look like for the next two decades.

Daniel Craig as James Bond, Casino Royale, 2006.

Recent findings suggest that also synonymous with Bond are his watch and many vehicles. Most recently, Bond cars have all been made by Aston Martin, though Brosnan drove some spectacular BMWs. The official Bond timepiece since Brosnan’s turn has been Omega. But before such kinds of commercial partnerships were commonplace in Hollywood, Connery wore watches by Rolex, Gruen, and Breitling, while Moore wore pieces by Seiko.

With the news that Pattinson is taking on the mantle, an equally pressing question emerges: Who will be the first newly introduced Bond girl?

According to recent reports, some of the most memorable moments in the franchise’s history have been anchored by women. Halle Berry’s emergence from the ocean in an orange bikini and a white belt safekeeping a knife was only made better by the fact that this moment was an homage to the first Bond girl, Ursula Andress, and her ivory two-piece featuring a belt for her own weapon. Then there was Eva Green as Vesper Lynd in a slinky Versace dress in Casino Royale. But it didn’t get better than Grace Jones in A View to a Kill. As May Day, a fabulous femme fatale, Jones wore costumes designed for her by Azzedine Alaïa. How could anyone measure up?

Halle Berry and Pierce Brosnan, Die Another Day, 2002.

Roger Moore and Grace Jones, 1985, A View To a Kill, 1985.

Of course, we will have to see how stylistic choices play out in the 26th Bond film, which, like Bond movies of the past, will become emblematic of the era in which we live. It will also, as a creative project, have to contend with the way Hollywood operates today. The fact that Amazon now has full creative control over the franchise—the company acquired MGM, a co-owner of the Bond franchise rights, for $8.45 billion in 2022 and later struck a deal with the other co-owners in regard to creative authority—is the primary indication of that.

Pattinson will also be the first Bond with airtight fashion-brand deals. Craig was an Omega ambassador as an extension of his role as Bond, which made him a household name, and the 007s who came before him operated within a film industry that was not as closely connected to fashion.

Industry observers note that also unlike his predecessors, Pattinson is stepping into the role as a bona fide movie star who has appeared in three other major franchises (Harry Potter, Twilight, and Batman). He’s already one of the most prolific and bankable stars of his generation, and an undeniable part of being a movie star today is becoming the face of a franchise, a brand, or a product.

It has been revealed that in September, Pattinson was announced as a global ambassador for Jaeger-LeCoultre, a Swiss watchmaker. But 007 has worn Omega watches onscreen for decades, a partnership between the brand and the franchise that dates back to the Brosnan years. If Omega’s partnership with the franchise remains for this upcoming installment, it could present a potential conflict if Pattinson’s contract with Jaeger stipulates that he is not allowed to wear another brand’s watch onscreen or front related campaigns for competitors. It may sound like a banal preoccupation, as Pattinson has only just been cast, but there are millions of dollars at play, and actors today often make as much money from brand deals as they do from their turns onscreen.

In a recent development, pattinson has also been an ambassador for Dior since 2013, serving first as a fragrance ambassador and subsequently as a face for ready-to-wear Dior Homme; he was originally tapped under Kris Van Assche, with his ambassadorship extending through Kim Jones’s tenure at the renamed Dior Men and now continuing with Jonathan Anderson at the helm of the French mega-brand. Will Anderson be providing his suits? The Irish designer has costumed films before, working with Luca Guadagnino on Challengers, Queer, and the upcoming Artificial. To design for the significant screen would hardly be a stretch for him.

Sources indicate that the real question is more existential: Should Bond wear high fashion? To return to the idea of the 007 silhouette, that in itself is counterintuitive to Pattinson saving the world in one of Anderson’s menswear takes on the famous Dior Bar jacket, with its nipped waist and slightly flared hem. And yet in this brave newly introduced world of brand deals, anything is possible.
