In 2025, "Hunger Games" author Suzanne Collins released one of the most long-awaited stories in the entire franchise — the backstory of District 12 victor Haymitch Abernathy, "Sunrise on the Reaping." A film adaptation titled "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" immediately took shape, and after Joseph Zada was cast as a young version of Haymitch — before he's an aging, depressed, drink-swilling lout portrayed by Woody Harrelson in the four original films — the rest of the cast began to round out.

It has been revealed that immediately after I read the book, I wondered who might be cast as Lenore Dove Baird, the beautiful and wild girlfriend Haymitch is forced to leave behind in District 12 when he's essentially chosen to participate in the Games by mistake. I was then extremely pleased when Whitney Peak was cast in this vital part, who's not only Haymitch's love interest but a vital link to the other prequel "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes" ... in that Lenore Dove is distantly related to that film and novel's heroine Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler).

So where have you seen Peak before she took on the role of Lenore Dove? I should say that, in general, Peak's star is still on the rise, but there's a reason she earned this role; not only is she extremely talented, but she's appeared in some pretty high-profile projects in recent years. From a major HBO reboot (that did fail, by no fault of Peak's) to some independent films, here's where you've seen Whitney Peak, who plays Lenore Dove in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," before.

After small roles in films like "Molly's Game" and TV shows like "The Chilling Adventures of Sabrina," Whitney Peak booked her first lead role courtesy of the "Gossip Girl" reboot that aired on HBO Max from 2021 to 2023.

Sources indicate that as a huge fan of the ridiculous campfest that is the original "Gossip Girl" — which was adapted, very loosely, from a novel series written by Cecily von Ziegesar and ran on The CW from 2007 to 2012 — I was excited for this reboot, but sadly, it was a largely toothless and lackluster impersonation of the original. Still, Peak was very good! She plays Zoya Lott, a newcomer to the high-status Newly introduced York City preparatory school who finds out that her late birth mother had another daughter. After Zoya and her half-sister, the wealthy and popular Julien Calloway (Jordan Alexander), make plans to meet up, they end up attending Constance Billard together ... but Zoya, who doesn't come from extreme privilege, struggles to fit in with Julien and her high society friends.

Sources indicate that again, this version of "Gossip Girl" is entirely too concerned with social justice crusades, whereas in the original show, the 20-somethings did insane stuff like sell each other for hotels. (Social justice is ... just not the point of a show like "Gossip Girl!") It was ultimately canceled after its Season 2 finale aired, leaving the story unfinished ... but it also freed Peak up for bigger and better opportunities.

In terms of her massive-screen work, Whitney Peak has appeared in a solid mix of independent project and a few bigger movies — aside from "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." In 2022, Peak showed up in the supporting role of Becca in the legacy sequel "Hocus Pocus 2," and I already mentioned that she was in "Molly's Game," which marked her film debut.

Elsewhere, Peak led films like the independent horror movie "Eye for an Eye," directed by Colin Tilley and adapted from Elisa Victoria's book "Mr. Sandman" — in that, Peak plays a young woman grieving the tragic loss of her parents who finds herself newly traumatized by a shocking, violent incident in her upcoming home in Florida. Peak also appeared in the action thriller "Trap House" alongside Sophia Lillis, Inde Navarrette, Jack Champion, and Bobby Cannavale, as well as Tommy Wirkola's survival film "Thrash" with Phoebe Dynevor and Djimon Hounsou.

You can see Peak as Lenore Dove Baird in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" in theaters now.

According to recent reports, the Pokemon franchise turned 30 this year, and while you'll have to wait until next year for a upcoming mainline game installment, you can celebrate that anniversary with something that's much cooler: Rock-and-roll-type electric guitars. The Pokemon Firm revealed that it teamed up with guitar manufacturer Fender to produce a Stratocaster model inspired by Pokemon Red, and a Telecaster model inspired by Pokemon Green. Each guitar features an aesthetic that pays tribute to the original Pokemon Game Boy adventures, including pixel art pulled from the games, graphics, and color overlays for an extra pop. The guitars really shine with a special toggle that warps the music they produce into an 8-bit retro sound that’s reminiscent of vintage gaming hardware. The neck also pays homage to Pokemon, with a special design that commemorates the collaboration between Fender and Pokemon. Just remember: No Stairway. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tDt6S_MIk8A As you'd expect, these won't be cheap. While US pricing and availability will be confirmed later on the Pokemon Center retail site, in Japan, these will retail for around $2,600 each. You'll also need to enter a lottery to stand a chance at winning the option to purchase one of these Fenders, which should prevent the items from being pounced on en masse by Pokemon scalpers. This year has seen several promotions kick off to celebrate 30 years of Pokemon, and one of the biggest involved Krispy Kreme. The doughnut chain's boxes of digestible pocket monsters proved highly popular, and unsurprisingly, Pokemon scalpers wasted no time trying to flip those treats and packaging for cash online. At least the legally distinct Pokemoan sex toys re-released this year proved to be somewhat immune to scalper efforts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games just released Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19 to rave reviews and huge sales. Everyone wants to know what's coming next, and surely there will eventually be another GTA game, but not soon. Appearing on OpenAI's technology and business show TBPN recently, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked how a upcoming GTA game could possibly up the ante. TBPN's Jordi Hays theorized that GTA 7 could "be a live version of the entire world." Zelnick, for his part, said people should remember that the interview was recorded on November 19, the day that GTA 6 released, so it's not time to talk about GTA 7. "I can't help myself. We at Take-Two just went live GTA 6 on November 19. Let me check my watch. Oh, it's still November 19. And you're asking a question about GTA 7," he said. While Rockstar isn't talking about GTA 7 yet--and no one should expect that to happen anytime soon--Take-Two has already signaled that the next GTA game could come out sooner. He said the “nature and velocity” of the firm’s content releases in its major franchises, including GTA, will look “dramatically different over the next decade.” GTA 6 released more than 13 years after GTA 5 came out in 2013. However, development didn't begin in earnest on GTA 6 until after Red Dead Redemption II came out in 2018, according to reporter Jason Schreier. This is because Rockstar's network of studios around the world work together on one project at a time, though smaller teams are also cooking up new things simultaneously. For more, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first.

The day after the midterm elections, President Donald Trump met with Susie Wiles in the Oval Office. He asked his chief of staff whether she believed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth would survive the impeachment attempt that would soon be rolled out by a member of his own party.

Hegseth was in a precarious position. He had been among the most aggressive champions of the war with Iran, widely seen as the policy most responsible for the shellacking Republicans had taken the night before. Wiles remained officially supportive of Hegseth throughout her time in the White House, but she had harbored concerns about the secretary from the start. She did not believe he was forthright about his skeletons during a rocky confirmation process, and she considered the subsequent Signalgate scandal an amateurish disaster.

In the Wednesday meeting, according to a senior White House official, Wiles made clear that the war, the uncertainty of its next steps, and the inflation it had fueled all contributed to the midterms debacle. She offered her resignation, but Trump declined. On Thursday night, in a contentious meeting in the Oval Office, she offered to resign again. Trump announced the next day that Wiles would leave the White House for his outside political operation.

In a recent development, hegseth’s fate was still uncertain. A deeply unpopular figure among the American public, presiding over an even more unpopular war, he faced an impeachment push led by Representative Thomas Massie. “He is just failing,” stated Republican senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina—who voted to confirm Hegseth at the start of Trump’s term—in an interview with Vanity Fair. “In the same way that Kristi Noem failed at Homeland Security, he simply doesn’t have the instincts or the prior experience as an executive that is necessary for this particular role.”.

It has been revealed that the secretary of defense has now embarked on a campaign to save his job, and Stephen Miller’s elevation to replace Wiles as Trump’s chief of staff has helped to ensure a reprieve. Trump has so far backed Hegseth publicly, and last week, House Republicans blocked the impeachment effort. “Pete is a fighter,” the White House official explained. “Trump likes fighters.” And there are other reasons to keep him in place, the official noted: Confirming a replacement will not be easy, particularly when Democrats take control of Congress, and ousting Hegseth would signal an admission that at this point, Trump’s war is a failure.

It was the president’s taste for staffers out of central casting that helped put Hegseth—a weekend morning television host with no experience in government, but with the square jaw of an Army Wives extra—in charge of the Department of Defense. He has relied on his talents before the cameras, and a team of advisers attuned to the production of his persona, to both keep his job and sell Trump on aggressive military action from the Pacific to the Persian Gulf. His survival has depended in part on his ability to project strength—not to the public, or to the rank-and-file, but to the president.

Sources indicate that “In just under two years, Secretary Hegseth has worked side-by-side with President Trump to restore American power on the world stage, build the strongest military in generations, and instill a warrior ethos at the Pentagon,” White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales mentioned in a statement. “President Trump and Secretary Hegseth have taken bold, necessary action to deny the Iranian regime the ability to develop a nuclear weapon, bring narco-terrorist Nicolas Maduro to American justice, and defend our homeland from dangerous terrorists and cartels—saving American lives.”.

In a recent development, the morning after Hegseth survived the impeachment attempt, he attended a Veterans Day ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Hegseth was joined at the sacred memorial by his closest aides: Jennifer Hegseth, his third wife and a former Fox News producer who serves as an informal but influential adviser; his chief of staff Ricky Buria, a Marine Corps veteran who followed an unusual path into the top brass; and Tami Radabaugh, another former Fox News producer whom Hegseth hired as a senior adviser.

As the group posed for photos at the Tomb, they chatted and laughed loudly. The Pentagon did not elaborate on why a soldier was awarded a medal for an act as pedestrian as scolding noisy attendees at a memorial. “Hegseth would not have given him that award had the incident not been on TV,” stated a former senior defense official.

A loyal Trump backer, Ullyot initially supported Hegseth’s calls to restore standards and excise identity politics from the military. He has since emerged as a fierce public critic and now believes Hegseth should resign.

Sources indicate that in his newly introduced book, The President Deserves Better, Ullyot describes a secretary of defense fixated on self-promotion and content creation. She has helped produce—and starred in—dramatic videos of Hegseth posted by the Pentagon’s official social media accounts. “Her entire job is to make his image,” one source told Vanity Fair.

House Republican Thomas Massie, who brought the articles of impeachment against Hegseth last week, argued the bombing was “the result of systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defense infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians.”.

Her role extended well beyond production, alarming senior officials in the Department of Defense. She interviewed candidates for Pentagon roles. She attended sensitive bilateral meetings with foreign officials. She was included in Signal chats that discussed the war plans for the Houthi operation in Yemen. The former defense official said they warned Hegseth about his wife’s involvement in Pentagon affairs. “She did not have a fucking clearance,” they said. “She shouldn’t be privy to this shit.”.

Recent findings suggest that hegseth himself seemed too smitten to care. When The New York Times examined Jennifer’s influence at the department over the summer, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell called the former cable news producer “an accomplished leader.” He added that the Pentagon “not only welcomes her current leadership but actively intends to involve her even more deeply in the future.” Politico later reported that while advising the secretary of defense, Jennifer was being paid for consulting work by Watchtower Strategies, a Washington lobbying shop that counts Lockheed Martin as a client.

One source told me that after NBC News was kicked out of its Pentagon office, Hegseth aides took a full-length mirror from the vacated room and installed it in his makeup studio.

According to recent reports, as Hegseth purged senior officials, he grew closer to Buria. #16757. The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth Review: Fincher And Tarantino's Mean-Spirited Hollywood Sequel

The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth Review: Fincher And Tarantino's Mean-Spirited Hollywood Sequel

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that there was a time in my life when a movie made by David Fincher and Quentin Tarantino would be the biggest cinematic event ever.
  • Industry observers note that as for Tarantino, while he tends to make everyone's eyes roll when he gives a latest hot take-laden interview, I still think he has the juice.
  • But his previous film, "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," might just be his best.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there was a time in my life when a movie made by David Fincher and Quentin Tarantino would be the biggest cinematic event ever. Not to get all film bro on you, but Fincher and Tarantino were very important filmmakers to me in my youth. That's not to say they aren't still important to me now ... but the luster has faded a bit. Fincher has spent the last few years making movies specifically for Netflix, and while those films — "Mank" and "The Killer" — have their charms, they pale in comparison to his previous work, so much so that I'd say the last great movie was "Gone Girl" in 2014 (for what it's worth, Fincher's exclusivity with Netflix is now over).

Industry observers note that as for Tarantino, while he tends to make everyone's eyes roll when he gives a latest hot take-laden interview, I still think he has the juice. However, the "Pulp Fiction" auteur has decided that he will only direct 10 movies and then hang up his filmmaking spurs. Because of this, Tarantino seems hesitant to direct a movie again, since that hypothetical movie would be his last. He came close to making "The Movie Critic" only to drop the idea entirely, and now he's working on directing his first stage play, "The Popinjay Cavalier.".

But his previous film, "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," might just be his best. It's certainly near and dear to my heart, as I find it inherently rewatchable. It's a funny, sad, surprisingly sweet hang-out movie that doubles as a slice of alternate Hollywood history. Tarantino has now returned to the world of "Hollywood" with his latest script, but again, since he doesn't want to direct his tenth and final movie just yet, he's handed the project over to Fincher.

Sources indicate that all of this is a long-winded way of saying that everything about "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" should, in theory, appeal to me, a movie nerd who still considers Fincher and Tarantino to be among the greats. But Fincher's not-so-stellar Netflix output coupled with Tarantino's weird insistence on not directing the movie himself muted my enthusiasm a bit, as have some lackluster trailers. On top of all that, Fincher and Tarantino have vastly different movie making styles. Would a union between the pair even work? I'm pleased to say the answer is "Yes." Sort of. While I was cautious about "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth," it eventually won me over. But it's not quite the movie I think anyone is expecting, and that's going to catch a few folks off guard.

It has been revealed that "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" introduced us to washed-up actor Rick Dalton, played by Leonardo DiCaprio, and his trusty stunt man sidekick Cliff Booth, played by Brad Pitt. Pitt turned in a funny, scene-stealing performance that landed him an Oscar, but Cliff seemed destined to be a supporting player in Rick's life. "Cliff Booth" turns him into a leading man, and I'm not entirely sure that's a good idea. Because without Rick Dalton by his side, what is Cliff Booth? I think the case can be made that Cliff Booth is a very charming psychopath. He's certainly not against brutally murdering people, and while he's highly capable and smooth as silk, there doesn't seem to be a whole lot going on in Cliff Booth's head. Rick and his internal struggles were part of what gave "Hollywood" its heart. Without him around, "Cliff Booth" ends up frequently feeling cold and cruel.

Pitt's Cliff became so lovable and likable in the first movie that I can't help but think Tarantino, always one to subvert expectations, is deliberately hammering home the point that for all his charms, Cliff is not exactly a good guy. He's a cypher; an idealized version of machismo — a men's pulp magazine hero brought to life. He lives fast and hard, likes drugs and booze, constantly risks life and limb, flirts with every woman he encounters, can kick everyone's butt, and still finds time to chill out and watch TV with his dear old dad. And yes, he occasionally murders people. Is "Cliff Booth" an attempt by Tarantino, or maybe Fincher, to remind us that this guy isn't nearly as cool as he seems?

In a recent development, in "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth," it's 1977, and Cliff's movie stunt days seem to behind him, especially since Rick Dalton has moved to Australia, where he's currently starring on a popular Aussie TV show. Cliff keeps busy, though, working an assortment of odd jobs. He runs the projector at the Latest Beverly Cinema, he works as a bartender making all sorts of elaborate margaritas, he participates in a demolition derby, and he even occasionally appears in an X-rated movie or two.

In a recent development, on the side, however, Cliff also works as a fixer for some of his old Hollywood friends. If they get into a jam that they can't go to the cops about, Cliff is willing to step in and work something out — for a price. And sometimes that results in a body count.

Cliff has become a legend due to his fight with Bruce Lee and the time he killed those damn hippies who broke into Rick's home (it's also worth noting that in "Hollywood," people suspected Cliff of murdering his wife, although that incident isn't mentioned here). At the end of the day, Cliff comes home to the apartment he shares with his dad Gus (Peter Weller) to watch old movies and TV. Weller's Gus is the warmest part of this surprisingly cold movie, and the banter between Cliff and his father is laid-back and believable in a way that made me wish the entire movie was just the two of them shooting the breeze.

According to recent reports, "Cliff Booth" is in no hurry, but eventually a shaggy Hollywood crime thriller plot emerges. The logistics of what's going on are hilariously convoluted, but Cliff is hired by manic actor Charlie Peters (Scott Caan, looking eerily like his late father in nearly every frame) to help get him out of some trouble. Cliff doesn't exactly like Charlie, but he does like Charlie's wife Toni (Carla Gugino), whom he had a love affair with over a decade ago. And Cliff really likes Charlie's agent, amazonian goddess Karen Crosby, played Elizabeth Debicki.

The flirty relationship between Cliff and Karen is meant to be sweet and romantic, but while Pitt and Debicki are both quite good in their respective roles (Debicki is particularly funny, bugging her eyes out at all the ludicrous things that happen), they don't have much chemistry. There's the glimmer of something interesting in how Cliff reveals he's a masochist who gets off on the idea of Karen slapping him around, but this angle is ultimately treated as little more than a throwaway gag.

Sources indicate that while "Cliff Booth" has the same hang-out movie vibes as "Hollywood," there are bursts of brutal violence that left me uncomfortable. Tarantino is no stranger to violence, and the big finale of "Hollywood" is drenched in blood. But here is where the styles of Fincher and Tarantino seem to clash the most. Tarantino's violence is almost always hyper-stylized and over-the-top. Influenced by countless splatter flicks and kung-fu movies, Tarantino shoots his violence in ways that are so ludicrously graphic that they become funny in a twisted sort of way.

Fincher, however, has a more realistic approach, which results in a handful of brutal scenes — most notably when the film's villains, a pair of gangsters from the Philippines (played by Matt Groove and JB Tadena) butcher an entire family during a home invasion. This moment has no bearing on Cliff's story, and seems to only exist to show us how bad these bad guys are. Which is fine, in theory, but Fincher stages it in such a cruel, unpleasant way that when he tries to lighten the mood in the following scenes, it rings hollow.

Recent findings suggest that there's a conversation worth having here about movie violence, I suppose. Which is the more questionable approach: depicting these moments in an unrealistic over-the-top fashion, or making them as real (and therefore upsetting) as possible? Again, I can't help but think that Tarantino is intentionally trying to flip the script and deliver something harsher after the good vibes of "Hollywood." The '60s are over, and here we're at the tail-end of the '70s, nearing the '80s. It makes sense for the vibes to be drastically different. But intentional or not, this contrast between Fincher and Tarantino makes "Cliff Booth" more mean-spirited than expected.

In a recent development, midway through the film, Tarantino's script gives Karen a meaty monologue about movies. Before becoming an agent, Karen was a budding film critic, and in her professional opinion, movies should entertain above all else. While she thinks movies can be artistic, she doesn't think of them as art. It's 1977, and the movie everyone is talking about is "Star Wars," which Karen thinks proves her point: audiences don't want a fancy cinematic meal, they want movie fast food. Even "The Godfather" is little more than pulp in her estimation.

In a recent development, I don't think a lifelong movie nerd like Tarantino actually believes this (and I don't think Fincher does, either), but this little speech must be here for a reason. Are we meant to just sit back and enjoy the ride of "Cliff Booth" and not think too much about what's unfolding here? Or is the film itself trying to prove Karen's theory wrong? For all it's moments of comedy, there's a cold darkness lurking beneath "Cliff Booth" that keeps it from being fully entertaining. It's as if Fincher and Tarantino don't quite have a grasp on the material.

Recent findings suggest that regardless, "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is Fincher's best movie in years — since "Gone Girl," really. While I do think he and Tarantino don't quite mix as well as we'd all hoped, the material has energized the filmmaker to craft a great-looking movie with several standout set pieces (I particularly liked a montage, told entirely via press photographs, showing Karen attending the premiere of "Looking for Mr. Goodbar").

Sources indicate that still, I can't help but wish Tarantino had just gone ahead and directed this himself. If he had, I think the tonal clashes might've been smoothed out considerably. "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" felt like something of a masterpiece to me when I first saw it, and the film's hefty runtime was a blessing rather than a curse — I wanted to spend as much time in this world with these characters as possible.

Sources indicate that but that world is nowhere to be found in "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth." Tarantino clearly didn't want to tread the same ground all over again when he banged out this script, and there's nothing wrong with that. But if everything is so different this time around, why would we want to check back in with Cliff at all, then? Especially without Rick by his side? "Cliff Booth" builds towards a memorable, brutal, action-packed climax before just sort of giving up and rolling credits. It's as if, in the end, everyone involved realized that old "Hollywood" magic was finally gone.

"The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" will be released exclusively in IMAX on November 25, 2026 for a two-week engagement before streaming on Netflix December 23, 2026.

It has been revealed that if you're looking for a complete surround sound system without spending several hundred dollars, the LG S6FTR is down to $249.99 from $399.99, saving you $150, or roughly 38%. This should give movie soundtracks a greater sense of direction than a basic soundbar, while the subwoofer handles the lower frequencies that smaller TV speakers often struggle to reproduce.

Industry observers note that at just under $187, the S60T is the least expensive system in this roundup, pairing a 3.1-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer for clearer dialogue and fuller sound than your TV’s speakers. That said, it lacks rear speakers and Dolby Atmos height channels, so it’s better suited to someone who wants a simple, affordable upgrade without filling the room with additional hardware.

Recent findings suggest that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

It has been revealed that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

As GameRoll reported on X, the novel describes the demise of Flaco Hernandez, whom Arthur Morgan cut down in Red Dead Redemption 2’s “The Noblest of Men, and a Woman” mission. The book also references Red Dead Redemption 2 locations like New Austin, Armadillo, and Blackwater. The book isn’t the only reference to Rockstar’s western. You can spot license plates from New Austin, Red Dead’s fictionalized version of Texas. Jason can even rock a cowboy hat that looks exactly like Arthur's.

Sources indicate that this isn’t the first time that Rockstar's franchises have crossed over. Franklin's house in Grand Theft Auto 5 contains a Red Dead book written by J. Marston. It’s hard to imagine John having time to document his exploits, but his son, Jack, may have provided an in-universe account of what went down in the first Red Dead game.

The following contains major story spoilers for GTA 6.

Beyond the ties to Red Dead, GTA 6 predictably includes many references to past Grand Theft Auto games. Jimmy De Santa, the son of GTA 5 protagonist Michael, makes a minor appearance. He's part of a mission where the player chooses whether to let him into a club. In Chapter 5, near the end of the game, Lucia and Jason begin working with GTA 4 protagonist Niko Bellic, who has returned to a life of crime.

Recent findings suggest that this isn't the first time GTA games have crossed over. GTA 5 infamously included a scene where Trevor killed Johnny Klebitz, the protagonist of GTA 4: The Lost and the Damned. At least Niko seems to fare much better.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, if you were having trouble accessing certain services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook, you were not alone.
  • When I first published this article on Thursday, I couldn't even load Microsoft 365's status page.
  • Looking specifically at Outlook, Microsoft's email service had hundreds of thousands of user reports Thursday afternoon, signaling a major matter somewhere in Microsoft's pipeline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you were having trouble accessing certain services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook, you were not alone. Early Thursday afternoon, many of Microsoft's biggest apps and services were experiencing downtime. According to Downdetector, which tracks user reports of problems with websites and platforms, Microsoft 365, Teams, Copilot, Teams, and OneDrive were all experiencing issues. As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft has restored service to many owners, and has officially apologized for the outages.

When I first published this article on Thursday, I couldn't even load Microsoft 365's status page. (I've reported on many service outages, but I can't recall a time when a service's status page was also down.) Even as of Friday afternoon, the page still indicates "Service degradation on Microsoft 365 (Business or Enterprise)," and Microsoft says the following services may be affected: Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center, Microsoft 365 Education, Microsoft Copilot 365, Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Graph, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Planner, Microsoft Power Apps, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft To Do, Power BI, SharePoint Online, Universal Print, and Windows 365.

Looking specifically at Outlook, Microsoft's email service had hundreds of thousands of user reports Thursday afternoon, signaling a major matter somewhere in Microsoft's pipeline. The reports did "slow down" throughout the day, but Downdetector still revealed over 50,000 reports coming in every 15 minutes when I checked Thursday afternoon.

Industry observers note that while the root cause of the problem was a mystery throughout Thursday's outage, Microsoft confirmed the problem in an apology on Friday. According to the firm, "This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI [or] agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.".

Microsoft notes it is "deeply sorry" for the disruption to its customers and partners. The tech giant says the fix rolled out slower than some might expect, since it wanted to restore service gradually to evaluate stability at each stage. It also says it will release a full post-incident report once it completes a review.

Recent findings suggest that during the outage, the company had confirmed that some of its infrastructure was experiencing elevated load, which it said was likely contributing to the issues. Microsoft then said it was pausing all deployments and moving traffic from affected infrastructure, and that it found that a number of its servers were unexpectedly unavailable after failing health checks. The company then thought a specific component responsible for processing server health may be the reason the system is failing health checks. Microsoft said an alternative service health check method successfully restarted some of the affected servers. The company was then actively restarting and validating affected servers to bring them back to service.

Recent findings suggest that brad Pitt is back as Cliff Booth. The character he first played in Quentin Tarantino's "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" is back for his very own spin-off with the aptly-titled "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth." Pitt won Best Supporting Actor for his work at the confusing, chaotic, cathartic 2020 Oscars. So having him back in that role is a major deal. But does his return as Cliff end when the credits roll? Or is there more to it?

Tarantino only wrote the script this time, with Pitt's friend and frequent collaborator David Fincher ("Fight Club," "Seven") taking over as director. Neither of these filmmakers are known for including post-credits scenes in their movies, but it's the sort of thing we can never really rule out these days. Especially since this spin-off is being made for Netflix. To that end, the "Cliff Booth" movie marks the end of an era for Fincher and Netflix, as the director has opted not to renew his deal with the streamer. So this is a swan song of sorts. One that viewers will be paying very close attention to.

Sources indicate that we're here to offer up a spoiler-free guide when it comes to the movie's credits scene situation. Seriously, we're not going to spoil anything meaningful at all, merely arming viewers with essential information to enhance the viewing experience. So proceed without fear. With that out of the way, let's get to it.

In a recent development, yes, "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" has one credits scene that audiences very much need to be aware of. It's more of a mid-credits scene that appears around 30 seconds (maybe a little more) after the credits initially begin. Without getting into details, this is a fairly important scene and something that viewers will want to stick around for. Whether you're seeing it in a theater or streaming from home, keep this in mind.

This is one of the biggest upcoming titles coming to Netflix in December 2026, which should help end the year on a high note for the streaming service. The sequel/spin-off takes place in 1977, eight years after the events of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood." Cliff is no longer working as a stuntman, instead spending his days as a projectionist and bartender. But he also works as a "fixer," solving situations for Hollywood's great and, sometimes, not so good.

Sources indicate that critics have been united in praise of Brad Pitt's Cliff Booth movie. It seems like a contender to become one of the best movies of 2026 and a very likely awards season favorite. The star-studded cast also includes Elizabeth Debicki ("The Crown"), Scott Caan ("NCIS: Upcoming York"), Carla Gugino ("The Fall of the House of Usher"), Yahya Abdul-Mateen II ("Wonder Man"), and Peter Weller ("RoboCop").

"The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" hits IMAX theaters on November 25 before arriving on Netflix on December 23.

Sources indicate that sarah J. Maas’ lush, romance-soaked series A Court of Thorns and Roses has blossomed into a sprawling, complex fantasy series with millions of dedicated fans, and with good reason. A complex heroine who keeps discovering new depths in herself, fascinating supporting characters who shift from antihero to antivillain in unexpected ways, creative and beautifully rendered world-building—the series has it all, while also being unapologetically romantic (and steamy).

The story of a huntress who is kidnapped by a fae prince and brought to the Spring Court as a prisoner, only to become a key player in all that fae drama, ACOTAR is special, but Maas can only write so fast. If you need more books with the same lush feel, here are 10 to get you started.

Recent findings suggest that it’s no shock that one of Sarah J. Maas’ other series would be recommended for fans of A Court of Thorns and Roses, but there’s a specific reason you should jump into her Crescent City series, especially the third book, House of Flame and Shadow. The most recent ACOTAR book, A Court of Splintered Harmony, revealed that the events of House of Flame and Shadow tie directly into the events in Splintered Harmony, particularly with regard to the character of Feyre’s sister, Nesta. In other words, if you read Splintered Harmony and wondered why Nesta was being so weird, there’s a whole other book series you should dig into immediately.

If Feyre’s grit and determination are your favorite aspect of ACOTAR, Julie Kagawa’s Iron Fey series (starting with The Iron King) will be your next obsession. Meghan Chase has never felt ‘normal’ in her life, and she’s been haunted by her father’s disappearance since she was a child. When her brother also vanishes, she goes on a quest for answers, learns that she’s actually the daughter of a faerie king, and finds herself in a magical world that blurs in elements of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream. Meghan is determined to save her brother (and herself), but a certain ice-cold fae prince captures her attention, even though he’s as dangerous as he is beautiful.

Industry observers note that if you’re looking for some serious romance in your fantasy, Jennifer L. Armentrout’s A Blood and Ash series is a must. Poppy was chosen at birth to be the kingdom’s Maiden, isolated and untouched in order to be ready for her Ascension to ensure the land is protected from the evil force that took her family. But it’s a lonely existence—until Hawke is assigned as her sworn protector. Golden-eyed and beautiful, Hawke offers Poppy the connection she’s craved. When chaos erupts around her, Hawke takes the opportunity to spirit Poppy away. But Hawke has a secret, and Poppy is soon in danger of losing both her heart and the favor of the gods themselves.

If you love how A Court of Thorns and Roses takes the “enemies-to-lovers” trope and builds it into a deep, complex mesh of emotions and plot twists, you’ll love Shelby Mahurin’s Serpent & Dove series. When witch Louise le Blanc flees her coven, she takes shelter in the city of Cesarine, where magic is forbidden, and witches are unceremoniously hunted and burned. Louise’s life gets infinitely more complicated, dangerous, and steamy when she’s trapped into an unwanted marriage with Reid Diggory—who happens to be a huntsman of the Church, charged with tracking down and eliminating witches. And then Louise starts to realize that Reid is actually pretty darn hot.

If you’re looking for a romantasy that’s broadly similar to ACOTAR while being its own thing, read A.K. Mulford’s The Five Crowns of Okrith series, starting with The High Mountain Court. Remy is a red witch, which means she’s in hiding and ready to make a run for it if the fae get near. So when a group of fae demonstrates up at her tavern, she makes for the exit—only to be captured by Prince Hale of the Eastern Court. Instead of striking her down, however, Hale asks Remy for help—he needs to locate two ancient magical artifacts created by red witches, and he needs her red magic to find them. Hale promises to set her free and even reunite her with the red witches still living. More importantly, Remy finds Hale irresistible and has a primal urge to stay with him, no matter what the cost.

Looking for a romantasy with a slightly different vibe from ACOTAR? Variety is the spice of life, after all—and The Fourth Wing delivers. Rebecca Yarros’ Empyrean Series made a huge splash when it debuted, and for good reason—it has everything, from a capable, intelligent heroine thrust into a dangerous scenario (in this case, a dragon rider academy where failure can be deadly) and forced to navigate alliances, conspiracies, and her own heart, which is pushing her towards a romance that might be as dangerous as the dragons themselves.

Industry observers note that love the moral complexity of ACOTAR, where everyone has at least a touch of darkness? Check out The Folk of the Air series by Holly Black. When Jude was a child, the father of her half-sister, the faerie Madoc, murdered her parents and took her back to the Faerie world with him. Raised as part of the gentry, Jude lives in a world where her mortal nature is hated and despised, but she battles for her place at court anyway while struggling with her love-hate relationship with her adoptive father and a growing bond with the titular prince, a relationship that is strictly forbidden. Jude is a fierce and extremely morally gray character, and one that fans of Feyre will adore.

Looking for more smart women at the center of beautifully-rendered fantasy stories? You’ll love Princess Lucero-Elisa de Riqueza of Orovalle, star of this series-starter by Rae Carson. Elisa was chosen for “Service” as a baby, when a godstone was placed in her navel by the gods, signaling that she was destined for greatness. But as a young woman, Elisa is self-hating and miserable. She’s never done anything even remotely great, and spends her time isolated, overweight, and reading military strategy books. One day she’s shocked to discover she’s been married off to the king of a distant land on the brink of war—and suddenly all that rage and book learning becomes invaluable as she struggles to survive an unfamiliar court and help her new homeland survive a dangerous onslaught.

Industry observers note that if you loved Feyre’s journey as she discovered unknown reservoirs of power and courage inside herself, you should read Leigh Bardugo’s Grishaverse novels, starting with Shadow and Bone. As a child, Alina was tested by the Grisha and found to possess no magical ability. As an adult, she serves as a cartographer in the army. Charged with guiding the Darkling—the most powerful of the Grisha—across the dangerous and terrifying Shadow Fold, Alina is unexpectedly revealed to have incredible powers and is packed off to train with the Grisha. There, she must determine who her friends and enemies are, even while falling under the spell of the charismatic Darkling.

Sources indicate that emilia di Carlo and her sister Vittoria are very different—Emilia is bookish and shy, Vittoria outgoing and brash—but they share a secret: They’re both streghe, and have spent their lives learning to use magic. In this version of Italy, the Malvagi (the seven princes of Hell) haven’t been seen in a long time, but a terrifying accident summons the Prince of Wrath and leaves three witches dead, including Vittoria. Emilia swears to use her power to avenge her sister, but when her revenge is delayed and she’s forced to work with Wrath, unwanted feelings begin to tick up the spice level to an uncomfortable degree.

"Spider-Man: Brand New Day" broke box office records, cementing Spidey as a reliable draw at a time when most other superhero movies aren't bringing in the crowds like the used to. Now, Marvel Studios and Sony Pictures have decided to re-release the movie for the holiday season, complete with previously unseen footage that will reintroduce a cut Daredevil crossover. We just got a sneak peek at that same crossover via a picture posted to Claire Temple actor Rosario Dawson's Instagram.

According to recent reports, temple originally appeared in Netflix's "Daredevil" series before becoming a mainstay in that small-screen universe. The nurse not only tended to Charlie Cox's Daredevil but also his fellow Defenders: Krysten Ritter's Jessica Jones, Mike Colter's Luke Cage, and Finn Jones' Iron Fist. (Temple didn't appear in Jon Bernthal's "The Punisher" series.) Alas, the Netflix series were all canceled by early 2019. Since then, Cox's Matt Murdock has returned in the Disney+ show "Daredevil: Born Again," in addition to making a brief cameo in 2021's "Spider-Man: No Way Home.".

Originally, "Brand New Day" also featured a crossover with the erstwhile Netflix "Daredevil" series. Sadly, a scene that featured Temple was removed from the final cut prior to its debut in July 2026. Now, however, that scene has been reinstated for the extended cut, awkwardly titled "Spider-Man: [Brand New] Brand New Day," which hits theaters on December 4, 2026.

Per The Hollywood Reporter, "Spider-Man: [Brand Newly introduced] Brand New Day" features 10 minutes of extra footage, most of which remains a mystery. One thing we do know, however, is that Rosario Dawson's Claire Temple cameo has been reinstated.

In a recent development, the actor took to Instagram to post a photo from the scene in question, which shows Temple standing alongside Tom Holland's Spider-Man inside a hospital room. This clearly takes place at the end of the movie, following Spidey's tumultuous final showdown with Sadie Sink's Jean Grey. Beyond that, however, Dawson didn't reveal much about what happens in the footage. "So excited to enjoy this record-breaking movie on the substantial screen," she wrote in her caption."[...] with an extended cut of new scenes and surprises... Ahhhh!".

Dawson previously revealed how she felt about being cut from "Brand New Day," saying that she had a BTS post ready to go about her time on-set that she ultimately had to scrap. Clearly, the actor was disappointed, which isn't surprising considering "Brand New Day" absolutely ruled the box office. Still, as she noted at the time (via Variety) "Because everybody's in it, it still means that my character is somewhere in that same universe, and I really love that. So, I hope I get to be Claire again." Now, with her footage being added back into the movie for the re-release, she has even more reason to be hopeful.

According to recent reports, with Rosario Dawson's Claire Temple appearing in the "Spider-Man: Brand Upcoming Day" re-release, the question becomes whether she'll show up again as the Marvel Cinematic Universe enters its next phase. As of now, "Daredevil: Born Again" has been canceled at Disney+, which means the upcoming third season will be its last. Thus far, Claire Temple hasn't appeared in the revival series, but there have been a few oblique references to a friendly nurse. Whether she'll show up in "Born Again" Season 3 remains unclear, but it wouldn't be surprising if she did.

With the show having been axed, however, Temple's MCU future remains even more uncertain. Perhaps if we get a fifth Tom Holland Spidey outing, she might come back. But such a film is also yet to be confirmed. "Brand Latest Day" producer Amy Pascal has one rule for making another movie, which essentially amounts to focusing on one film at a time. Still, with "Brand New Day" becoming nothing short of a phenomenon, it seems almost certain Sony Pictures and Marvel Studios will want to get Holland back for another outing ASAP.

Sources indicate that indeed, "Brand New Day" has made $2.5 billion at the global box office, and the re-release will likely bring in a decent bit of extra profit. Hence, with "Born Again" ending after its next season, a "Brand New Day" sequel seems like the most likely venue for a Temple return. For now, though, we'll have to await further news.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's been almost a decade since Toby Fox released the first chapter of Deltarune, the celebrated indie developer's follow-up to Undertale. Now the end of the story is in sight. In a recent newsletter enhancement, Fox revealed that his team is making good progress on the game's final two chapters.

Fox opened the Fall 2026 Deltarune newsletter by sharing that Chapter 6 is now "structurally complete" and can be played from beginning to end. He added that "some key scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation" but that preliminary testing and localization would begin soon. Fox also revealed that Chapter 6 will be shorter than past chapters, but that he's still taking his time with development to make it as good as possible.

Sources indicate that chapter 5 was released in June, and Fox shared that Chapter 6 is expected to release in 2027.​​​​​​​ The newsletter included a short scene for the upcoming chapter featuring the character Queen​​​​​​​. Even though Chapter 6 isn't out yet, some members of the Deltarune team are shifting their work to the game's ending​​​​​​​.​​​​​​​.

In a recent development, work on Chapter 7 has just begun​​​​​​​, and Fox is teasing his team with the plot of the finale​​​​​​​. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team," he wrote in the newsletter. "However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens.".

Fox said he's learned a lot from the game's long development, admitting that "unlike every other chapter​​​​​​​, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time." Fox has also stated that Deltarune, unlike Undertale, will not have multiple endings.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article contains discussions of addiction.

Don't go to the old reaping site with your buddies and reminisce if you haven't seen "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." Spoilers ahead!

Industry observers note that we've known, for quite some time now, that Jennifer Lawrence's Katniss Everdeen and Josh Hutcherson's Peeta Mellark would return in the highly anticipated big-screen prequel "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." If you've read the book, you know that they come back for an epilogue, and in late October 2026 — just about a month before the film's release — Lawrence opened up about the experience and confirmed that Woody Harrelson, who plays the older version of "Sunrise's" protagonist Haymitch Abernathy in the original Hunger Games films, is also part of the scene. So ... what happens?

It has been revealed that there are some differences between the epilogue in the book and the film adaptation helmed by Francis Lawrence, but the gist is the same — and I'll return to those differences later on. After we see how Haymitch wins his games and how the Capitol punishes him for attempting to destroy the 50th Games arena — Haymitch attempts to blow up a water tank and essentially drown the machine, but safeguards stop his strategy from going through, and his family and loved ones are killed upon his return to District 12 — we see Harrelson's Haymitch approach an ivy-covered structure that's the old site of the annual reaping that chose one boy and one girl to compete in the deadly Games. He's joined by Katniss and Peeta, who wish him a happy birthday; it's a major plot point in "Sunrise" that reaping day always falls on Haymitch's birthdays. They thank him for everything, and Haymitch notes "Nevermore" before departing.

Putting the prequel "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes" aside — because none of the characters I'm talking about were alive during that story — it makes complete sense for Katniss and Peeta to show up to close out Haymitch's standalone movie. The three are, for all intents and purposes during the original Hunger Games timeline, a package deal. We see, at the end of "Sunrise on the Reaping," that Haymitch arrives home in District 12 and sees the coffins of his fellow tributes, and we also see a montage of Joseph Zada's younger take on the character overseeing the delivery of coffins that are clearly tributes he was forced to mentor as a former victor.

Industry observers note that by the time we get to the 74th Games, Haymitch is constantly drunk and imbibes to survive, telling his tributes his only advice is that they stay alive. When he and Katniss click, though, he starts to wonder if these tributes have what it takes ... and thanks to a plot conceived by him and Peeta that presents Katniss and Peeta as star-crossed lovers forced to compete, they get to jointly win the Games.

That next year, only previous victors can be reaped, and Katniss and Peeta go back in to fight, though Haymitch hatches a proposal with other rebels to break them out of the arena. Though Peeta is kidnapped, tortured, and brainwashed by the Capitol, they eventually rescue him and take down the Capitol, ultimately returning to District 12 to live out the rest of their days together.

In "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," this ending for Haymitch, Katniss, and Peeta feels hopeful and optimistic. Suzanne Collins, the author of the franchise, takes a darker approach in the literary epilogues for both "Mockingjay" and "Sunrise on the Reaping." In "Mockingjay," Katniss notes that both she and Peeta have post-traumatic stress disorder and still suffer greatly, experiencing night terrors and other symptoms. In the book version of "Sunrise," Haymitch speaks directly to the reader about how he didn't even want to care about his two tributes initially because he felt too broken, but he was worn down. "I didn't want to let them in, her and Peeta, but the walls of a person's heart are not impregnable, not if they have ever known love," he muses before mourning his one true love, Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak in the film), who was poisoned by Capitol forces when Haymitch initially returned to District 12 as a victor.

It has been revealed that beyond that, Haymitch is blunt about the way that chronic drinking has affected his body. "I'm not sure I'll be here in the old therebefore much longer. My liver's wrecked and I only dry out when the train's late," he claims. "I drink differently these days, though, less to forget, more out of habit. When my time comes, it comes, but I've no idea when that will be." Still, Haymitch gets a relatively happy ending with Katniss and Peeta.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is in theaters.

Industry observers note that the evening began with an outdoor cocktail hour, where guests enjoyed passed apps and specialty drinks like the “Parisian Refresher” and “Worth It Spritz” under sparkling bistro lights. As honorees and attendees mixed and mingled, they also had the opportunity to pose for a photographer and peruse a beauty bar stocked with L’Oréal-brand lipsticks, lip oils, and glosses, which were available for guests to take home in a plush velvet bag with “I’m Worth It” embroidered on it.

It has been revealed that as the gala officially began inside The Ebell’s picturesque ballroom, longtime brand ambassador Eva Longoria gave the introductory remarks, noting that “this night always gives me goosebumps. I’m always crying.” She saluted her 20-plus-year partnership with the brand and joked that it made her “112 years old,” though she doesn’t look like it, the actor-director noted, “because I use Revitalift.” She gave a shout-out to the many beauty influencers in attendance, including Laura Lee and Desi Perkins. “You guys really changed the game of beauty, and I just applaud you,” she said. “Put me in your TikToks.”.

Industry observers note that L’Oréal Paris USA president Laura Branik followed Longoria, emphasizing the brand’s commitment to and pride in its Women of Worth program, which continues to celebrate “the power of women who know their worth and use it,” she said. She then welcomed the organization’s newest global ambassador, Kristen Bell, to the stage. Bell, who was attending her “first Women of Worth ever,” said she was “very happy to be here” and introduced moving presentations for the first two honorees: Vy Le of WhereWear, which transforms clothing donations into targeted support for women’s and housing-insecure shelters and the people they serve, and Amanda Rice of The Chick Mission, a nonprofit dedicated to ensuring that every young woman newly diagnosed with cancer has the option to preserve her fertility.

Actor and brand ambassador Aja Naomi King was up next, taking note of the room full of glamorous gowns and festive energy. “Everyone revealed up and showed out,” she mentioned, “and we appreciate that because these women deserve to be celebrated properly. I had the immense honor of helping select this year’s Women of Worth, and I keep thinking about how much it matters when someone believes in your potential.” King introduced two honorees: Maya Bird-Murphy of Mobile Makers, an award-winning nonprofit that expands access to design education through workshops, community engagement, public installations, and pop-ups, and Christy Vogel of Sounding Joy, a nonprofit dedicated to providing hearing aids to children whose families cannot afford them.

Longoria then returned to present another pair of honorees: Marisa Hamamoto of Infinite Flow Dance, an award-winning disability-led nonprofit and professional dance manufacturer with a mission to reimagine possibilities, one dance at a time, and Chanel Power of Mentor Me Collective, a technical institute transforming how emerging technologists are identified, developed, and positioned to lead.

In a recent development, during a break in the program, guests enjoyed dinner from a menu that included roast chicken, citrus-soy-and-apple-cider-braised short ribs, and vegan pan-seared “scallops.” Another highlight? The venue’s bathrooms were stocked with more coveted L’Oréal goods like lip oil, mascara, setting spray, and velour puff makeup applicators.

According to recent reports, following the break, ambassador, actor, and model Cara Delevingne led the room in a cheerful group proclamation of “We’re worth it!” before introducing her honorees: Emily Cho of Juvie for STEM (JSTEM), an international nonprofit dedicated to expanding access to high-quality STEM education for justice-involved youth, and Arielle Galinsky of The Legacy Project, Inc. (TLP), a national nonprofit connecting younger and older adults for multigenerational friendship and storytelling.

Sources indicate that legacy L’Oréal ambassador Andie MacDowell had the pleasure of introducing the event’s final honorees. “For 40 years I have been a part of the L’Oréal Paris family,” she said, with the milestone receiving enthusiastic applause from the audience. “After all these years, the thing that stays with me [about the Women of Worth honorees] is the determination to make life better for someone else. That kind of care is powerful.” MacDowell introduced Jordan Pine of Greenlight Operation, a Pennsylvania nonprofit that strives to strategically combat human trafficking and serve sex trafficked women through a continuum of restorative care, and Dr. Christie Brungardt, cofounder of Jana’s Campaign, a Kansas-based nonprofit dedicated to preventing gender and relationship violence through education.

Eva Longoria and Andie MacDowell.

Proud “newbie” Bell returned to the stage to offer closing remarks and thank all the honorees for their tireless efforts to make life better for others. “I will be thinking of all 10 of these stories and the women we met tonight for quite some time,” she noted. “Even though their stories couldn’t be more different, they seem to have one thing in common: that they all saw what needed to change and they did it. They didn’t wait for someone else to do something; they stepped forward and they did it themselves. And honestly, I think that’s gonna be my biggest takeaway from my first Women of Worth celebration ever: Never underestimate what one woman can set in motion.”.

Each of the 10 Women of Worth 2026 honorees received a $25,000 grant, mentorship, and national visibility. As the program concluded, honorees, their proud guests, and other attendees continued to soak up the special evening and shared in a few more hugs and photo ops. Before departing for the evening, guests were invited to enjoy a final “sweet moment” in a separate room where a colorful candy bar and glasses of Champagne awaited.

It has been revealed that FFmpeg only provides source code. Below are some links that provide it already compiled and ready to go.

You can retrieve the source code through Git by using the command:.

FFmpeg has always been a very experimental and developer-driven project. It is a key component in many multimedia projects and has latest features added constantly. Development branch snapshots work really well 99% of the time so people are not afraid to use them.

Since FFmpeg is developed with Git, multiple repositories from developers and groups of developers are available.

All FFmpeg releases are cryptographically signed with our public PGP key and should be verified for authenticity.

It has been revealed that to verify a release: Import our public key into your local keyring: $ curl https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-devel.asc | gpg --import Download a release tarball and its corresponding signature. Verify the signature: $ gpg --verify ffmpeg-4.3.2.tar.xz.asc ffmpeg-4.3.2.tar.xz gpg: Signature made Sun 21 Feb 2021 06:35:15 AEST gpg: using RSA key FCF986EA15E6E293A5644F10B4322F04D67658D8 gpg: issuer "ffmpeg-devel@ffmpeg.org" gpg: Good signature from "FFmpeg release signing key " [full] Optionally, you can verify that git and tarball match, the only differences should be the absence of .git* files in the tarball and a VERSION file in the tarball containing the version. The git tags should be signed with EDDSA key DD1EC9E8DE085C629B3E1846B18E8928B3948D64.

A release that also has a .pq.asc file carries post-quantum signatures (RFC 9980) made with both of these keys:.

GnuPG cannot verify these yet; use sq 1.4 or later built with a cryptographic backend that supports these algorithms (OpenSSL 3.5 or RustCrypto), both of these must succeed: $ sq verify --signature-file ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz.pq.asc --signer-file ffmpeg-mldsa87-ed448.cert.pgp ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz $ sq verify --signature-file ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz.pq.asc --signer-file ffmpeg-slhdsa256s.cert.pgp ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz.

In a recent development, approximately every 6 months the FFmpeg project makes a new major release. Between major releases point releases will appear that add notable bug fixes but no new features. Note that these releases are intended for distributors and system integrators. Consumers that wish to compile from source themselves are strongly encouraged to consider using the development branch (see above), this is the only version on which FFmpeg developers actively work. The release branches only cherry pick selected changes from the development branch, which therefore receives much more and much faster bug fixes such as additional features and security patches.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Home Alone is one of the most beloved Christmas movies ever.
  • In a recent development, it hurts my heart, and it hurts my heart that every Christmas I have to deal with this.
  • Roebuck has had a busy career since, including substantial roles in movies like The Fugitive and Agent Cody Banks, but he never worked with Columbus again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home Alone is one of the most beloved Christmas movies ever. Families watch and rewatch it every year around the holidays. For most, it’s a celebratory time, but for one actor, Daniel Roebuck, it’s bittersweet. Roebuck, if you didn’t know (and I didn’t), was the original actor cast in the role of one of the Wet Bandits, Marv, who was memorably played by Daniel Stern. Behind the scenes of Home Alone, Roebuck was fired by director Chris Columbus just four days into filming, and ever since, Christmas has meant he has to relive that tough moment.

In an interview with PageSix, Roebuck explained:.

In a recent development, it hurts my heart, and it hurts my heart that every Christmas I have to deal with this. I have the utmost respect for Chris Columbus. When he did fire me, and he said he’d put me in his next movie, I waited by the phone, man.

Roebuck has had a busy career since, including substantial roles in movies like The Fugitive and Agent Cody Banks, but he never worked with Columbus again.

This all stemmed from a story Columbus recently recounted about filming Home Alone on The Wildmen Podcast, where the director explained that the studio would only pay for either Daniel Stern or Joe Pesci (who played Marv’s partner Harry), but not both. So Roebuck was cast and, according to Columbus, the first screen test with Roebuck and Pesci was “terrible.” Roebuck, however, disputes that version of the story, telling PageSix:.

According to recent reports, they never, ever, ever filmed me and Joe Pesci together. I never, ever filmed anything with Joe Pesci. The camera never rolled on us.

Sources indicate that he added that he only worked with Pesci for one day. He also adds that, despite Columbus telling him they would work together (something Columbus also notes), that never happened, and they haven’t spoken since. Roebuck still doesn’t understand the reasoning behind his firing, but he doesn’t have any ill will towards Columbus, saying:.

I can’t speak to his motivations. He’s a good Catholic guy. I try to be a good Catholic guy. I try to be a man of faith, and I’m certainly a man of forgiveness. So I never held a grudge against him for firing me. I’m disappointed that every Christmas I have to put up with this when I’ve contributed so much more to the world than not being in ‘Home Alone.'.

Ultimately, though, Roebuck didn’t star in the movie, and, at least according to Columbus, the director got the actor he wanted all along. It’s pretty hard to imagine the movie without Stern, but these events bring a little bit of a dark cloud over the casting. I guess in the end, Columbus did what he thought he had to do, but it’s easy to understand why Roebuck has mixed feelings about what many consider one of the best Christmas movies ever.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unlike the "Star Wars" saga, the "Hunger Games" franchise has defied the odds to deliver two stellar prequel films set before the events of the very first dystopian sci-fi action movie adapted from author Suzanne Collins' original books.

After launching in 2012, "The Hunger Games" delivered a four-part substantial screen property telling the story of rebellious Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and an ensemble of revolutionaries attempting to topple the oppressive, wealthy government known as The Capitol. But the franchise has since returned with stories set decades in the past. This started with 2023's "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes," which offered a rich portrait of a young Coriolanus Snow (Tom Blyth) acting as a mentor to a bold Hunger Games tribute named Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler).

Now, the story continues 40 years later, with the excellent "Sunrise on the Reaping" focusing on a young Haymitch Abernathy (Woody Harrelson in the previous movies, now played by Joseph Zada in the prequel) as he's forced into the 50th Hunger Games. This event marks the second Quarter Quell, which takes place 24 years before the first installment of the overall franchise.

"Sunrise on the Reaping" (watch the trailer) might be the most brutal, heartbreaking chapter of the "Hunger Games" franchise yet, if only because the fall of Haymitch Abernathy — from charming, kind-hearted District 12 citizen to hopeless, grizzled, bitter, and drunk Hunger Games victor turned tribute mentor — is incredibly heartbreaking.

It has been revealed that what happened to Haymitch after the 50th Hunger Games that sent him on a downward spiral? Join us as we explain the ending of "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" to break it all down.

Before we explain the ending of "Sunrise on the Reaping," we need to set the stage a bit, so you know how and why Haymitch ends up where he does by the end of the movie.

Industry observers note that haymitch didn't have rebellion burning in his heart as the 50th Hunger Games were beginning, though his girlfriend Lenore (Whitney Peak) put the spark of revolution in his mind, longing for a day when the sun would not rise on another reaping, overshadowing Haymitch's birthday. But Haymitch took it all in stride, even going out of his way to get a little bag of gumdrops for Lenore.

Unfortunately, Haymitch ends up in the 50th Hunger Games while trying to break up an altercation between Lenore and the Capitol police after she tries to let a grieving mother embrace her son, who has just been shot following an attempted escape from his obligation as one of the four District 12 tributes. District 12 tribute escort Drusilla Sickle (Glenn Close), a cruel Capitol citizen, then punishes Haymitch by forcing him to be the replacement tribute, with a little behind-the-scenes editing help from Hunger Games broadcast producer Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons, playing a younger version of the character portrayed by the late Philip Seymour Hoffman in the original franchise).

If that wasn't enough to light the spark of rebellion in Haymitch's heart, the events of the 50th Hunger Games welcome parade for the tributes certainly did the trick. After Capitol citizens throw colorful smoke flares into the Capitol arena where the parade is held, the horses pulling tributes in chariots get startled, creating a chaotic scene that results in the death of Louella McCoy (Molly McCann), a younger girl who admires Haymitch and was drawn as one of his three other fellow tributes.

After the death of Louella, Haymitch wants nothing more than to lash out at the Capitol, and he begins doing so by walking up to President Snow's (Ralph Fiennes) balcony in the parade arena and mockingly applauding him for directly bringing about the death and destruction laying in front of him.

Meanwhile, Haymitch is also joined in the 50th Hunger Games by fellow District 12 tributes Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), a somewhat snobby and sassy 16-year-old girl who has a reputation for being a bit mean. But once forced into the Hunger Games, she softens and allies with Haymitch and the rest of the District 12 tributes. That includes Wyatt Callow (Ben Wang), who comes from a family known as the "Booker Boys," because their family calculates odds and takes bets on the Hunger Games, which many view as a cruel practice. And despite the death of Louella, a Capitol-controlled lookalike replacement girl (Iona Bell) is forced to take her place, and the District 12 tributes take her under their protection.

Sources indicate that wyatt is killed almost as soon as the Hunger Games begin, when the tributes make a wild dash for weapons. But Haymitch, fake-Louella, and Maysilee make it out alive, though the former has chosen to disassociate himself from the rest of the group, having been told directly by President Snow that he will not make it out of the Hunger Games alive, as penance for his mocking defiance at the parade. Haymitch doesn't want anyone else to suffer for his defiance. But little does Snow know that Plutarch Heavensbee, with the help of several other Hunger Games mentors and tributes, are using Haymitch as a vessel for a rebellion meant to stop the games once and for all.

It has been revealed that in the games, Haymitch works with a clever tribute named Ampert Latier (Percy Daggs IV), who is mentored by his father Beetee (the tech-wise character played by Jeffrey Wright in the original films, now played by Kelvin Harrison Jr.). They've concocted a plan to break the Hunger Games by blowing up the water tank that supplies the entire arena, flooding the computer systems and cutting off power to the entire operation. Haymitch succeeds initially, but the power is repaired rapidly, Ampert is killed by woodland creatures swarming and gnawing his body to death, and as retaliation for the attack on the arena, Snow orders that the arena's volcano be activated.

Haymitch survives the eruption, and the deadly fire that engulfs the mountainous woods of the arena, but most of the surviving tributes do not (including fake-Louella, who died earlier by way of a poison pollen), leaving just five of them: Maysilee, a young girl named Wellie (Rada Rae), and two of the deadliest career tributes, Silka and Panache (Laura Marcus and Jhaleil Swaby).

Recent findings suggest that after a series of attacks, both by deadly birds and Silka and Panache, all of the other tributes have died, including Maysilee, but not before they promise each other to be the worst Hunger Games victor ever, should they emerge victorious. Haymitch is crowned as the victor of the Hunger Games, and he intends to stay true to his promise. But his battle is only just beginning, and it's about to get much worse.

In a recent development, haymitch might have won the Hunger Games, but all of his actions in the arena are painted in a completely different light. His attack on the arena itself is not televised, and when he's presented to the Capitol as the winner in the recap hosted by Caesar Flickerman (Kieran Culkin), he's painted as a traitor and a coward, one who promised to help his fellow tributes against the careers but abandoned them as soon as the games started. Even the final kill of Silka, which happens after her thrown axe is deflected back at her by a shield protecting the power plant that gives energy to the arena, is mocked, as Haymitch couldn't even deliver the final blow himself to declare victory.

Things don't get better when he returns home, either. As soon as he arrives back in District 12, his mother and brother are killed in a house fire, clearly orchestrated by President Snow. But the final crushing blow comes when he reunites with Lenore. As they embrace, she eats what appears to be the gumdrops that he told his brother to give to Lenore before he left for the Hunger Games. But those aren't the same gumdrops. They're poisoned, courtesy of Snow, and Lenore dies in Haymitch's arms.

It has been revealed that all of this pushes Haymitch to the brink, and he begins to drink heavily and isolate himself from the rest of District 12, even shunning the friendly Everdeen family, despite their efforts to help him work through the pain. He stays true to his word by becoming the worst Hunger Games victor, letting his tributes fail for years, refusing to participate in this barbaric entertainment. But there might yet be hope for Haymitch.

Sources indicate that why did President Snow let Haymitch live after defying the Capitol so clearly? In addition to being the victor of the Hunger Games, making it difficult for him to merely dispatch with him in the arena, Plutarch Heavensbee convinced Snow to reconsider killing Haymitch after the games were over. Knowing that their stunt to end the games didn't work, and the public was unable to see the tributes working together and sparking the rebellion in the districts needed to overthrow the Capitol, Heavensbee is pulling a move that feels reminiscent of Albus Dumbledore using Harry Potter to draw out Voldemort.

Plutarch is the one orchestrating the presentation of the Hunger Games to the public, and he knows what they need to see in order to sew a revolution properly. He's willing to turn Haymitch into an outcast and upend his life if it means there's even the smallest possibility that his defiance will eventually grow into the rebellion they need. He knows the continuation of the games will continue to create resentment, and they just need to wait for the right spark to emerge that will set fire to the hearts of every district in Panem. While it might feel like they've failed, this is still a small success that will lead to a future generation following in their footsteps.

According to recent reports, we already know how that story turns out, and "Sunrise on the Reaping" ends with Woody Harrelson returning as Haymitch Abernathy, admiring a memorial that now lies where the reaping once took place in District 12. He's joined by Katniss and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson), who wish him a happy birthday, allowing Haymitch to fulfill Lenore's dreams of keeping the sun from rising on another reaping. Haymitch paid dearly for decades, but the Hunger Games are finally over.
