You’ve been outspoken about distinguishing criticism of Israel from antisemitism, but do you think that there are moments when legitimate anger at Israel can create an environment in which antisemitism becomes acceptable, even among people who would never consider themselves antisemitic?

And what responsibility do you think you have, given the size of your audience and your influence with it, to call that out when it happens?

In a recent development, I do call it out when it happens, and it happens quite frequently. It’s not a secret that antisemitism has exploded in the Western world, especially after October 7. And that is why I take special care and consideration when talking about this concern in particular. Whenever I talk about Israel, there’s always going to be some people who will be like, “Well, you know how the Jews are.” And I will always take the time out to explain to my audience, and to whoever’s saying an offensive statement or an antisemitic statement, why they’re wrong. And I think it’s crucial to do that, not because—it’s not like the canary mission of the ADL is gonna be like, “This guy that we have presented to you as a prominent critic of Israel, that we’re desperately trying to paint as an antisemite, has actually spent thousands of hours combating antisemitism and will continue to do so because he’s an antifascist.” They don’t want to present the complexity of that argument because, let’s be real, it’s pretty tough trying to defend Israel. It’s not an easy endeavor.

Can you think of a time when you contributed to that problem, not intentionally, but maybe through something you said and the way your audience responded?

In a recent development, no, because every clip that people post, or every moment that people have posted to point to this suspected antisemitism that I harbor, oftentimes is sandwiched between a comment that I have made leading up to it that completely destroys the narrative. The example I will present to you is the famous moment where I got disavowed by the entire Democratic Party. I said something that I have said as an anti-Zionist for the last decade and will continue to say because it’s the truth: that Jews are not monolithic and that Israel should not be the responsibility of the entire Jewish population, and that anti-Zionism is not antisemitism; however, that forced conflation of Jews in Israel is increasing antisemitism. And they chopped it up and packaged it and turned it into this major media moment.

Recent findings suggest that so speaking of misinterpretations, you recently filed a defamation lawsuit against conservative commentator Scott Jennings, although you’ve said you were very deliberately anti-litigation for a long time before that. So what changed? Why this suit? And who else are you planning to sue?

In a recent development, so what changed is the heinous nature of this defamation. It was definitely a bridge too far. I feel like there is a boundary that was crossed that I could no longer abide by. And there’s a level of defamation and slander that takes place in the political conversation, but what Scott Jennings did was so disgusting and so malicious that I had to demand a retraction. Snopes did an article immediately because it was so heinous. He claimed that I was on video advocating to lynch Black voters. I’ve spent my entire life fighting against white supremacy, and the fact that they maliciously edited this video to make it seem like I was in favor of something that I’ve always been in opposition to, something so heinous, a hate crime, was outright unacceptable. So I wish that it didn’t have to get to litigation, but for some strange reason, they decided not to respond to our request for a retraction and now we’re here.

Who else are you planning to sue?

I mean, there are a lot of people who have engaged in that exact same kind of defamation and slander. So whoever has participated in it should probably be on the lookout.

It has been revealed that okay. In the national chapter of the DSA, there are some pretty extreme platform positions that—I saw Mamdani answer these questions on Fox News the other night. I’m sure you did too.

And I'm actually just curious where you stand on some of them.

So here’s the thing with the platform in its entirety. I think the format itself doesn’t actually do justice to the program, to describe the program, and it’s almost impossible to explain it as an elected representative or a mayor in a hostile or contentious media environment, if you’re on Fox News or whatever. The issue, I think, with the program is, there are certain elements of it that I don’t agree with fundamentally, but it’s a democratically organized, democratically voted-on program that DSA members voted for. And the way I see it is, these are very, very long-term goals, and I think this is not talked about in mainstream media at all. It is a platform, but it’s more so a North Star that we are working toward. Designing society in a way that yields egalitarian outcomes. That we do away with certain systems of cruelty is an honorable goal, is a just goal, even if I don’t fully agree with some elements of it.

I’m not a prison abolitionist; I’m not a police abolitionist. The reason why I don’t believe in that concept is because I think that these are necessary functions that must exist, but also must serve the people. Right now it doesn’t. It serves capital and that needs to change, that needs to be retooled. However, I also recognize that the current system that exists is far more ruthless, far more insane, even if we’ve normalized it, than even police abolition is. So from my perspective, if we look at where we’re at, the carceral state that exists, where America has 25% of the entire planet’s prisoner population despite only making up 4% of the overall population, and the recidivism rates that we have in this country, and the fact that we even have a private prison system in this country—that’s insane. That is insane by global standards. So it’s tough for me to sit here and say I oppose the DSA platform and program when I understand what they are trying to communicate.

It has been revealed that and also, I think what is the regular order of business right now is far more insane than even prison abolition. Even though prison abolition is far-fetched and I don’t agree with it, I think the best possible way to go about it would be to have an electoral program, the perceivable, the permissible, the possible, and then the long-term goals, the long-term agenda, ’cause it’s not going to be easy to run and try to win on a platform that is not only idealistic, but also does not reflect the current societal understandings of concepts. Because most people think cops are awesome, they can do no wrong, they’re heroes, they’re constantly fighting crime, and they’re stopping rapes from happening, and they’re diving in front of bullets, but that’s not the case. I wish that was the case, but that’s not the case. But people overall [have] a very positive attitude about policing as an institution.

Recent findings suggest that but there’s also quick and quippy ways to respond fast. I just told you I’m a law-and-order Democrat, right?

Immediately that signals something. Another thing that I always say about policing is, I want police to do their jobs. I think that, by and large, they have a profoundly notable task that they have to accomplish. Their presence is supposed to invoke law and order. Their presence sometimes invokes lawlessness and disorder. That’s unacceptable. They’re very well paid. They have the best unions. Do your jobs better. That’s my attitude on policing. So it’s antagonistic, but it’s also a demand that I’m making from this institution that I truly do believe is important for society to function. That’s one way to tackle this matter in a way that Americans understand. I like to call it chudifying your commentary. Zohran does a very good job of libifying his commentary. He’s very liberal-appealing. I like to do the opposite. I like to chudify it. I appeal to the chuds. I speak from that tone and that language when I advocate for certain things.

It has been revealed that yeah, edgelord vernacular, sure. But it’s kind of like, whether we’re talking about abortions or whether we’re talking about transgender bills, like anti-trans bills, I’m like, I don’t want the fucking government getting involved in these affairs. What do you want? You want some creepy pervert to do penis inspection day at your high school? What are you, a pervert? Are you a pedophile? I want small government when it comes to this kind of stuff. And that is a way to argue from a perspective that I think right-wingers can understand.

In a recent development, switching gears, we talked a little bit about suits for a second, but I want to talk about style more largely. So at the RNC’s midterm convention in September, there was a 25-foot selfie of you in underwear displayed on the jumbotron. How do you think about that?

“And he’s also sexy. Look at him shirtless. Look at him shirtless.” Because I thought these guys were peak masculinity. I thought that’s what they were about. The Joe Rogan Experience, you know, Brazilian jiujitsu, and working out was supposed to be the thing in the right.

There’s nothing unmasculine about being gay.

It has been revealed that I’m kidding. That’s not how they think of it. I know.

And not only that, but also, ultimately, why are they showing a shirtless photo of me where I look jacked?

Do you like it in some regard, or does it bother you?

It has been revealed that it’s attention. I like it. In the past, when people would approach me and be like, “Why is The New York Times only talking about how you look and not talking about your ideas?” I was like, “Look, that is terrorism insurance.” If I’m getting into these legacy publishers and not being called a terrorist and instead being called a hot guy, I’ll take it.

Okay. Okay. One last question about your looks. If Calvin Klein calls tomorrow and wants you to do the Houston Street billboard, are you doing it?

According to recent reports, okay. I wonder, with your audience, because there are a bunch of young guys looking up to a guy who’s maybe slightly older than them, looks like they might want to look, is that homoerotic at all?

Recent findings suggest that but I do have a fairly queer community as well. We do a census. We do a yearly census. Fourteen percent of my audience is trans, which is obviously much higher than the American population.

What are some other demos that would be interesting that we wouldn’t expect?

Well, the classic ones are obviously—it’s like 60% white men under the age of 35.

You perform best with all the people that Vanity Fair performs worst [with].

What about you captured them? How did you do it?

I was a young man at some point, and I also have the same interests, and I think that’s part of it. And I also speak—going back to the crude, the language that I deploy, the vulgar language that I deploy, it’s like I speak like a normal person. I speak and get angry in the same exact ways that normal people do.

Industry observers note that all right. Hasan, what’s your attitude toward money? How do you think about money?

It has been revealed that for me personally, it has a corrosive influence, I think. It has the capacity to make you unbelievably out of touch. It’s something that I think about quite a bit in my own personal experience. I was a very stubborn person with air travel. Even when I had a little bit of additional income, I refused to pay the extra for the economy-plus seats.

Industry observers note that I’m a major dude. I’m 6’4”, I can’t fit in the seats, and I would still. It’s a point of pride. Until one day I was put in a business class seat for some kind of business travel. And at that point I had enough money to purchase business class seats on my own, and I was like, I’m never looking back.

According to recent reports, you were ruined. You were ruined.

Industry observers note that it ruined me. It completely ruined me. So now—.

Industry observers note that tina Brown says that the private plane ruins people, that when you see how that works, it’s over. Hook, line, sinker, people are done.

That corruption is almost—she doesn't say this, but I’m interpreting that it’s almost inevitable after that.

Recent findings suggest that yes. I think that every instance of financial stability or financial freedom that I’ve gained has made me more out of step with the struggles that I used to experience and the struggle that everyday people experience. And I think you have to always be in touch. Especially in my line of work, you have to understand where people are. On the other hand, though, it is editorial freedom, because I have been able to maintain complete editorial control, complete editorial freedom, because I am completely unbought, completely unbossed, completely unshackled. There have been numerous instances where I’ve obviously had contracts with Amazon and stuff like that because I know I need to play ball also to make sure that I am a reliable team player so they don’t deplatform me. However, there have been so many instances where people have come to me with tremendous sponsorship opportunities.

Polymarket is one that I talk about all the time. [For] 2024 election night, their opening salvo was a million dollars just to have their ticker on the side. I stated, of course, no, because I feel like it’s deeply unethical to be sponsored by a gambling organization, a prediction market, while, you know, you’re engaging in news commentary. But I know that if I did not have that economic freedom, that financial freedom, I would’ve probably had to think about whether or not I’d make this ethical compromise.

So Calvin Klein would be an exception.

Industry observers note that calvin Klein’s fine. I mean, I take sponsorships every now and then, like gaming companies and stuff like that. If Rockstar came to me and were like, “Grand Theft Auto VI is coming out. We want to sponsor a stream,” I would fucking love that.

Industry observers note that some people have a number that’s like their retirement number, at which point that’s all the money they need. They close up shop and call it a day. I wonder if you have a number after which you think it would be unethical to accumulate any more. What is the maximum amount of net worth or income that you could generate after which you would feel it’s morally reprehensible?

Great question. I have no idea. I’ve never thought about it like that because there’s no world in which I will reach that number. But all the revenue that I generate goes immediately back into this broader project. It allows me to be able to travel around the country. It allows me to be able to hire people on a moment’s notice if necessary. So that’s the way I see it. I don’t have an unethical number, but I think to each their own, because I don’t want people to hear me say this and then be like, “Well, you know, you’ve collaborated with Saikat Chakrabarti. He’s a centimillionaire. You’ve talked to Tom Steyer. He’s a billionaire.” I care more about what people’s actual advocacy is and if they’re real about it or not. And I think how much they pay into certain things can show that, for sure. But anything past the point of having—not your net worth, right, but anything past the point of just having $10 million, I feel like is insane. It’s like, What are you doing? Does that make sense?

Because you noted you differentiate with net worth.

I differentiate it with net worth because everyone will say, “Oh, well, I have assets. I have stocks,” or whatever. But in general, if you have—.

According to recent reports, the capacity to deploy—I feel like even $10 million is too much. If you have the capacity to deploy a million dollars into something, you’re done, you’re set. I think everything past that point is outright ridiculous.

All right. I want to look ahead to the future because 2028 is not far away, and I think all signs would show that you’re going to be a character in that cycle. So here’s the inevitable 2028 question: Do you think the public has met the 2028 candidate that you’ll champion yet, or do you think that person is still waiting in the wings somewhere?

It has been revealed that I mean, the top answer, obviously, since we’re doing this will-they-won’t-they thing, is AOC. Right? She is the one figure, I think, on the left that has the capacity to unite the base, and she’s competent, she’s charismatic, incredible progressive track record as a legislator, and—.

Who is moving more to the center.

Well, I think all that stuff is—it’s pragmatism. I don’t think that means that she is going to come out and be like, “I am no longer in favor of the same comprehensive policy agenda that I’ve sought to advance my whole life.”.

But it might mean that she wants to unite the base.

Recent findings suggest that yeah. But I don’t think you necessarily have to do compromise on the legislative front to unite the base. If I was being fully transparent, fully honest, or maybe a little harsh, my criticisms around AOC would probably be that she’s not aggressive enough and that at times she’s come across as perhaps a little too liberal, too woke, on social concerns in a way that is not appealing to broad subsets of the base.

Recent findings suggest that okay. Say AOC runs but loses the primary, and you’re dealing with Josh Shapiro or Gavin Newsom or insert centrist Democrat here.

According to recent reports, what do you initiative to do? Do you urge your audience to get behind them?

I don’t know. I don’t know what I would do at that point. I haven’t even thought about it because I don’t think I need to think about it.

I don’t think it’s even going to be a problem.

So, I guess AOC or not, how do you want to be involved in the 2028 election?

I’m gonna do what I did in the primaries and the midterm broadly, and hopefully we’ll have a slate of hundreds of democratic socialists that will be running in every district that will be bold, that will excite the base, and that will chart a different path forward for the Democratic Party by force.

Do you think that—we’ve talked a little bit about this toxicity of the brand of Hasan Piker, which has been burnished by the right and by some on the left.

It has been revealed that do you think about trying to clean that up, as it were, so that you could be more helpful to whoever that progressive candidate is? Or is it more useful for you to be ethically pure, I guess, in your estimation and stay as the stick in the mud on the far left?

Look, I got to the point I got to by being honest and sometimes being hardheaded, being stubborn, but always saying the truth. And that policy’s not going to change. So I say, if this is considered too toxic for politicians to take advantage of this platform, then they’ll lose. Because my goal is not to change myself. My goal is to change politics. I want American politics to be more responsive, not only to our demands, but also reflective of our anger as well. I truly believe that we are in the moral majority. People who look at the current system and say, “This is not helping,” people who look at their insurance premiums going up and say, “We need to change this,” that is a morally righteous fury that people feel, and there is a great deal of time and effort spent on mainstream outlets, legacy publishers in the media broadly, to try to quiet that frustration. I believe that I have a more honest approach to the matter, and that is precisely the reason why my audience continues to grow as their audience continues to age out or diminish.

Industry observers note that I want to end on a slightly different note. I want to do a lightning round with you. I’m gonna say a series of names and I just want you to give me word association, the first thing that comes to your mind—just don’t say their job. It’s too boring.

According to recent reports, yeah, yeah. Please give me money. Fund the DSA.

Industry observers note that ooh, that’s a good one. I can’t say my house because I feel like it’s very expensive, but it’s expensive because of the housing market in Los Angeles. So I’ll say business class travel.

In a recent development, okay. What’s your most marked characteristic?

I don’t know. Probably my looks.

I feel like there are different ways that I could have gone about things and how I manage them, but ultimately I’m stronger on the other side.

When and where were you happiest?

Zohran victory party 2025 was peak. Even the Bluenami was really good, but I think that was so significant for me because it was the first time I had approached a campaign hands-on and played somewhat of a role in that victory. And I was surrounded by all these people that were door knockers that had worked on the campaign. They were coming up and they’re like, “Dude, I’m here, we’re all here, because I saw Zohran on your stream, and I was like, This guy is the truth, this guy’s the real deal. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that peter Farrelly's "I Play Rocky" tells the story of the making of the very first "Rocky" movie. Anthony Ippolito plays "Rocky" star/writer Sylvester Stallone, and much of the film centers on his negotiations with "Rocky" producers Irwin Winkler (P.J. Byrne) and Robert Chartoff (Toby Kebbel). The movie also traces the early romantic days between Stallone and his first wife, Sasha Czack, who kept their home in order and offered support — while pregnant — throughout the production of "Rocky.".

Sasha is played by AnnaSophia Robb, who has been racking up screen credits since she was a kid. Her first major screen role was that of the title character in the 2004 TV movie "Samantha: An American Girl Holiday," and she promptly became one of the more ubiquitous child actors of her generation. Just a year later, she appeared in the dog-based film "Because of Winn-Dixie" and played the bratty Violet Beauregard in Tim Burton's "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory." Then, the year after that, she played a possibly evil child in "The Reaping" and starred opposite Josh Hutcherson in the heartbreaking book turned film "Bridge to Terabithia," which is easily one of the saddest movies Disney has ever made.

According to recent reports, robb has only continued to work steadily up to the present. She's popped up in low-profile straight-to-video movies like "Spy School," franchise starters like "Jumper," reboots like "Race to Witch Mountain," and soulful dramedies such as "The Way Way Back." Meanwhile, on the TV side of things, she's starred in the "Sex and the City" prequel show "The Carrie Diaries," PBS's "Mercy Street," and NBC's short-lived crime drama series "Grosse Pointe Garden Society." Her acting career is a healthy mix of projects significant and small, and she comes across as wholly devoted in practically all of them, "I Play Rocky" included.

According to recent reports, those who might be concerned about AnnaSophia Robb's personal well-being as a former child actor (a profession that doesn't always treat kids well) should know that she has always endeavored to live a regular life beyond her career. As she told the Arapahoe Herald in 2009:.

According to recent reports, "Living in Colorado grounds me, it makes me keep perspective. [... When I fly to Los Angeles], all my problems in Colorado disappear, and I start to think about work. I change positions. I only think about working stuff, and all of my stuff at school seems so small [and vice versa].".

This seems healthy for a teenager traversing Hollywood, and she appears to have survived high school well enough. When CBS News caught up with her in 2014, she had enrolled at Latest York University and explained that she never wanted to be a "star," per se, noting that she's rather devoted to her craft. Indeed, Robb has apparently succeeded in showbiz by retaining a healthy personal life and remaining focused on acting rather than stardom. And her career has offered her a wide variety of roles in which to ply her craft.

Recent findings suggest that case in point: Robb is excellent in "I Play Rocky" and plays Sasha Czack as a no-nonsense individual who speaks very frankly to Sylvester Stallone. To be sure, Robb possesses a natural confidence that continues to serve her very well. "I Play Rocky" itself may be "syrupy" (to quote /Film's review of the movie), but Anthony Ippolito is a standout as Stallone, and Robb does not vanish next to him, either.

"I Play Rocky" is currently playing in theaters.

Yellowjackets Season 4 Features The Show's Most Heartbreaking Scene Yet

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (911 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spoilers ahead for "Yellowjackets" Season 4, Episode 1, "Hivemind.".
  • "Yellowjackets" Season 4 isn't letting up on the heartache, even now that the girls are out of the Wilderness.
  • Recent findings suggest that last season, Natalie snuck away from the girls' latest cannibal hunt and used a salvaged satellite phone to call for help.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers ahead for "Yellowjackets" Season 4, Episode 1, "Hivemind.".

"Yellowjackets" Season 4 isn't letting up on the heartache, even now that the girls are out of the Wilderness. The show has had plenty of tearjerking moments already, from Jackie's (Ella Purnell) death in Season 1 to Shauna's (Sophie Nélisse) stillbirth in Season 2. But "Hivemind" has one to rival all of those, especially if, like me, Natalie (Sophie Thatcher) is your favorite.

Recent findings suggest that last season, Natalie snuck away from the girls' latest cannibal hunt and used a salvaged satellite phone to call for help. "Hivemind" picks up with everyone freshly rescued and recuperating in a Canadian hospital. The team's parents all fly in — including the parents who then discover that their kids didn't make it, like Mari's (Alexa Barajas) mom (Patricia De León).

The surviving Yellowjackets and their parents reunite — except for Natalie, because her mom didn't bother to show up. That everyone else's parents came only makes it worse, like the universe twisting the knife in her side yet again. She has to stand alone surrounded by reminders of the parental love she's never had and face that she's back to being the neglected kid she was before the plane crash. No wonder Natalie makes a quick exit and bums a cigarette off a hospital worker.

When Natalie hears the authorities couldn't reach her mother, she smiles through the tears and states "sounds about right." You spend 19 months thinking your daughter is probably dead, and you don't drop everything when there's a chance she isn't? What kind of mother does that? We've seen before that Natalie had a rough home life. Her dad was an abusive drunk, and when Natalie threatened him with a rifle, he grabbed it and accidentally shot himself, for which Natalie's mother blames her.

When we initially see Natalie in "Hivemind," she's taking her first hot shower in 19 months, as if also washing off her brutal time in the Wilderness and her sins while there. Then the rest of the episode drops cold water on her. She kept her teammates alive through the winter as a hunter and leader, and she led the effort to get them home in the last stretch of Season 3. Her reward is resettling into her crappy life.

Recent findings suggest that on one hand, it's easy to forget struggles like a broken home when you're stuck miles away from civilization. Or, alternatively, this only makes Natalie more heroic, for she knew she didn't have much of a home to go back to but still risked everything for everyone else. But let's not overlook Natalie's (cannibalistic) complicity, either. She's the team's savior but not a saint, and that conflict is what makes her so compelling.

Recent findings suggest that back in the Season 2 episode "It Chooses," Natalie — the starving girls' chosen sacrifice — lets Javi (Luciano Leroux) drown so they can eat him instead. I asked after Season 2 if we'd been misjudging Natalie as the "good one," the same question Natalie was asking herself. Now, I'd say the answer is yes and no. She's good but not so much that she'll throw her own life away for someone else. Most people never have their morality put to the test like that, but Natalie did. She failed and has to live with proof of the kind of person she is. Now, in "Hivemind," she faces what the life she fought to hold onto so hard looks like. Before she could assuage her guilt with the imagination of rescue, now the reality can't give her that same solace.

In a recent development, when Natalie goes for the smoke, the hospital worker says she shouldn't be smoking. "I shouldn't be alive," Natalie replies. Is she talking about the realistic odds of surviving 19 months stranded? Of trading her life for Javi's? Of deserving to be alive? All of the above? Searching for comfort with a cigarette ties together well with Natalie in the adult timeline (Juliette Lewis), who had developed a drug addiction to cope with her guilt.

Sources indicate that natalie also stated in the pilot, during a rehab group session, that she lost her purpose after the Wilderness. Now we know that she had blossomed into a leader out there. It's crucial to contrast her with the group's other queens, Shauna and Lottie, because all three became people they couldn't be back home.

Sources indicate that lottie, without access to her medication, embraced her illness as clairvoyance and became a prophet. Shauna lived in Jackie's shadow her whole life, then came into her own in the most horrifying way possible. Before the plane crash, Natalie was viewed by everyone as a burnout. She was already hitting drugs and liquor in high school, and her teammates looked down on her for that, for her sexual proclivity, and for being poorer than them. In the Wilderness, she became a leader without intending to become one.

In "Hivemind," Lottie is almost catatonic, and Shauna is stewing in silent anger. None of the three Antler Queens are going to have an easy time readjusting, but with Natalie, it feels like she could have if she'd had a better support system waiting for her. Natalie's mom not showing up for her may lack the violence of other "Yellowjackets" tearjerker moments, but it remains quietly heartbreaking all the same.

"Yellowjackets" is streaming on Paramount+.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In April, Ecohustler disrupted Carnival Cruise's AGM calling on the shareholders to reduce their tech giant's pollution using straight forward and affordable methods - like burning cleaner fuel.
  • Carnival Corporation, the world’s largest luxury cruise operator, emitted nearly 10 times more sulphur oxide (SOx) around European coasts than did all 260 million European cars in 2017, a new analysis by sustainable transport group Transport & Environment reveals.
  • In a recent development, royal Caribbean Cruises, the world’s second largest, is second, yet four times worse than the European car fleet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In April, Ecohustler disrupted Carnival Cruise's AGM calling on the shareholders to reduce their tech giant's pollution using straight forward and affordable methods - like burning cleaner fuel. Since then, a new report outlines the corporation's impact on the coastline of Europe. These vast floating cities are burning dirty bunker fuel and creating shocking levels of air pollution wherever they go. Shipping has been an unregulated industry for too long and action is urgently required.

Carnival Corporation, the world’s largest luxury cruise operator, emitted nearly 10 times more sulphur oxide (SOx) around European coasts than did all 260 million European cars in 2017, a new analysis by sustainable transport group Transport & Environment reveals.

In a recent development, royal Caribbean Cruises, the world’s second largest, is second, yet four times worse than the European car fleet. SOx emissions form sulphate (SO4) aerosols that increase human health risks and contribute to acidification in terrestrial and aquatic environments.

In absolute terms, Spain, Italy and Greece, closely followed by France and Norway, are the European countries most exposed to SOx air pollution from cruise vessels while Barcelona, Palma de Mallorca and Venice are the most impacted European port cities, followed by Civitavecchia (Rome) and Southampton.

These countries are so exposed because they are major tourist destinations, but also because they have less stringent marine sulphur fuel standards which allows cruise ships to burn the dirtiest most sulphurous fuel all along their coastlines.

Sources indicate that faig Abbasov, shipping policy manager at T&E, said: “Luxury cruise ships are floating cities powered by some of the dirtiest fuel possible. Cities are rightly banning dirty diesel cars but they’re giving a free pass to cruise companies that spew out toxic fumes that do immeasurable harm both to those on board and on nearby shores. This is unacceptable.“.

NOX emissions from cruise ships in Europe also heavily impact some cities, equivalent to about 15% of the nitrogen oxides (NOx) emitted by Europe’s passenger car fleet in a year, the report finds. In Marseille, for example, 57 cruise ships emitted in 2017 almost as much NOx as one-quarter of the city’s 340,000 passenger cars. Along the coasts of countries such as Norway, Denmark, Greece, Croatia and Malta a handful of cruise ships are also responsible for more NOx than the majority of their domestic car fleet.

Recent findings suggest that europe should implement a zero-emission port standard as soon as possible, this could then be extended to other ship types. The report also recommends extending emission control areas (ECAs), right now in place only in the North and Baltic Seas and English Channel, to the rest of the European seas. Furthermore, the report recommends regulating NOx emissions from existing ships, which are currently exempt from NOx standards applying in emission control areas.

Faig Abbasov concluded “There are enough mature technologies to clean up cruise ships. Shore-side electricity can help cut in-port emissions, batteries are a solution for shorter distances and hydrogen technology can power even the biggest cruise ships. The cruise sector are apparently not willing to make the shift voluntarily, so we need governments to step in and mandate zero emission standards.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that many players have a habit of optimizing the fun out of video games, and that tendency has unsurprisingly found its way into Grand Theft Auto 6. Apparently, the game has many ways to “get rich quick,” and these exploitive strategies are going viral online.

In one method, the player drives to the Apollo Aggregates warehouse in South Vice-Dale County, where a drug deal went wrong. The building is full of narcotics, spare bills, and dead bodies, letting you easily pillage close to $8,000 worth of loot. After grabbing the goods, the player stores the contraband in their car, then saves and loads to teleport back to their house. At this point, they bring the contraband to Brian’s place to cash out. A YouTube video outlining the method claims you can make around $4,000 every five minutes, which is more efficient than nearly everything else in the early game.

According to recent reports, in another strategy that falls more into the "glitch" category, the player robs the stores near Jason’s house, loses the cops, and then enters any story mission. After the story mission cutscene begins, the player selects Restart Mission in the menu and then pauses and quits. This causes all the stores the player just robbed to instantly reopen with fresh loot, allowing them to rob them again.

However, despite how efficient these early-game earning strategies are, many players are swearing off the temptation. “Nah I’m good! Didn’t wait 13 years just to glitch my way through the game,” one user wrote on X. “Top tip, if you just play the game the amount of money you can make is unlimited, no special trick needed,” a sardonic YouTube comment reads.

These users point out that earning so much money early undermines the game’s economy, ruins the gradual progression of unlocking better gear, and invalidates many of the game’s cash-earning side missions. On top of this, these methods directly counter the narrative flow of GTA 6, which is about Lucia and Jason attempting to scrape together some semblance of the fabled “American Dream.”.

Recent findings suggest that while some are baffled by why anyone would use such mind-numbing strategies, players are obviously entitled to play the game however they want. Still, it seems likely that Rockstar will patch the game soon to remove these methods, especially the second one, which seems to be a bug.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is now available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

Sunrise On The Reaping's Connection To Edgar Allan Poe's The Raven, Explained

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Don't read any poems about ravens if you haven't seen "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." Spoilers ahead!
  • Recent findings suggest that we don't know precisely when the Hunger Games world exists.
  • The book takes great pains to "transform" this poem — which begins with the line "Once upon a midnight dreary, while I pondered, weak and weary" — into a song, which gives Haymitch's girlfriend Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak) her first name.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Don't read any poems about ravens if you haven't seen "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." Spoilers ahead!

Recent findings suggest that we don't know precisely when the Hunger Games world exists. We just know, from the books and films, that North America has been redrawn into a totalitarian regime called Panem by that point in the future. There's a very interesting reference to American culture, though, in both the novel and movie version of "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," the origin story of future District 12 mentor and rebel Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada in this film). Specifically, Edgar Allan Poe's poem "The Raven" just ... exists.

The book takes great pains to "transform" this poem — which begins with the line "Once upon a midnight dreary, while I pondered, weak and weary" — into a song, which gives Haymitch's girlfriend Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak) her first name. As Haymitch claims of Lenore Dove, a member of District 12's musical Covey, "She tends to take a dark view of things, but maybe that's to be expected from someone named for a dead girl. Well, half for the dead girl called Lenore in this old poem and half for a shade of gray, which I found out the day I met her.".

In case you're foggy on "The Raven," here's a snippet:.

Recent findings suggest that ah, distinctly I remember it was in the bleak December; And each separate dying ember wrought its ghost upon the floor. Eagerly I wished the morrow;—vainly I had sought to borrow From my books surcease of sorrow—sorrow for the lost Lenore— For the rare and radiant maiden whom the angels name Lenore— Nameless here for evermore.

It has been revealed that interestingly, the "Sunrise on the Reaping" book by Suzanne Collins never mentions Poe by name. The movie, however, takes a different approach.

Again, in Suzanne Collins' 2025 novel "Sunrise on the Reaping," the author makes it clear that "The Raven" is a song of, I suppose, unknown provenance. As Haymitch explains while he's preparing for the Games, he keeps dreaming about Lenore and thinking about what he calls her "name song," saying, "In it, a guy loses the love of his life, Lenore, and he's going crazy for missing her. Then this big old raven shows up at his house and won't leave and whenever he asks the bird anything, it just indicates 'Nevermore' — which, as you can imagine, just makes him crazier.".

Across the board, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is a pretty faithful adaptation of the novel, and a scene between Haymitch and Capitol cameraman Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons on-screen) plays out roughly the same as it does on the page. There is one notable difference, though, which is that the film has a physical prop book that claims "'The Raven' by Edgar Allan Poe" on the cover.

Sources indicate that both versions have Plutarch ask Haymitch if he knows what "nepenthe," a mythical potion, means when the Hunger Games tribute sees a bottle of it on a bar. When Plutarch inquires if Haymitch has heard of it in the book, he internally scoffs: "Not only have I heard of it, I know it from the poem that gave my love her name. I'm tired of being patronized, so I decide to put him in his place." When Haymitch recites a line about nepenthe from the poem, Plutarch finishes it in both versions. So, why is this poem so horrifyingly perfect for this Hunger Games story?

Sources indicate that putting aside the wild idea of Edgar Allan Poe being, I think, the only tangible link between our world and Panem, Suzanne Collins picked a horribly appropriate name for Lenore Dove Baird. The woman in "The Raven" is, obviously, dead, and by the end of "Sunrise on the Reaping," Lenore Dove meets the same fate.

It has been revealed that when Haymitch, working with fellow tribute Ampert Latier (Percy Daggs IV) and Ampert's father, Haymitch's assigned mentor, and former District 3 victor Beetee (Kelvin Harrison Jr.), tries to destroy the Games arena itself by blowing up a subterranean water tank, he does technically succeed. Unfortunately, the water tank bursts, yet the arena remains intact, and Haymitch wins the Games by utilizing a force field just outside of the arena's range ... and is summarily punished when he returns home to District 12. Not only does he find his house burning to ash immediately upon arrival, he learns that his mother and younger brother, his only family members, are inside. Then, not long after, he reunites with Lenore and feeds her a gumdrop, her favorite candy ... but it's a poisoned bag direct from President Snow, and she dies, too.

"The raven. The unforgiving songbird. Repeatedly reminding me of President Snow's crystal-clear message to me on my homecoming," Haymitch thinks to himself bitterly as he mourns. "That I will never get to love anyone ever again. Nevermore. Because he will make sure they end up dying a horrible death." Still, the word "Nevermore" ends the film adaptation as Haymitch surveys the now-peaceful reaping site, giving it a slightly brighter meaning when the story ends on-screen.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is in theaters now.

According to recent reports, there are a lot of characters in the wider "Hunger Games" universe, so I'll forgive you if you're only familiar with some of the bigger players like Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence), Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada in his origin film and Woody Harrelson in the original movies), Coriolanus Snow (Tom Blyth, Ralph Fiennes, and Donald Sutherland at various points throughout his life), Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson), or Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler). The latest installment in the literary and cinematic franchise, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," brings back some familiar faces and introduces new ones too — so, who, exactly, is Proserpina Trinket?

Introduced in both the book and film version of "Sunrise on the Reaping," Proserpina Trinket is a bubbly, enthusiastic, and quick-thinking young stylist working to prepare Hunger Games tributes for all the Capitol-centric pomp and circumstance that takes place before the bloody Games themselves. (Yes, the teenage tributes get all dolled up before they're forced to fight to the death in a dangerous arena that's also trying to kill them. This world is sick!).

We don't know a ton about Prosperina besides the fact that she works with the extremely unreliable Magno Stift (Billy Porter), she's assigned to work on Zada's Haymitch alongside Vitus (Edvin Ryding), and her older sister is future District 12 chaperone and stylist Effie Trinket (played in this film by Elle Fanning and the original movies by Elizabeth Banks). What we definitely know is that she's played by Iris Apatow, a rising talent from a famous family who's shown up in a handful of TV reveals and several huge comedy movies from the 2000s.

Iris Apatow was born in 2002, and odds are you're familiar with her family. Her older sister, Maude Apatow, starred in "Euphoria" throughout its entire run. Her mother, Leslie Mann, is an acclaimed comedic actor. Then there's her dad Judd Apatow, a comedy kingmaker, producer, writer, and director who's helped make projects like "Superbad" and "Bridesmaids" and directed his own like "The 40-Year-Old Virgin," "Knocked Up," "Funny People," and "This is 40." Let's talk about those last three, because all of them feature the youngest Apatow. (The less said about Judd Apatow's 2022 COVID movie "The Bubble," the better.).

Industry observers note that maude and Iris Apatow play Sadie and Charlotte, respectively, in both "Knocked Up" and "This is 40" — with their on-screen mother, Debbie, portrayed by Mann, and their father Pete by Paul Rudd as an Apatow stand-in. As for "Funny People," they also play Mann's daughters (in this one, Maude is Mable and Iris is Ingrid) with Mann as Laura, the ex-girlfriend of comedian and actor George Simmons (Adam Sandler), who's dealing with a life-changing health crisis. Sure, the Apatow daughters don't do a ton here, but they flesh out the universe in all three of their dad's films ... and it's notable that we watched Maude and Iris grow up on-screen, basically.

Recent findings suggest that all things considered, Iris Apatow's career is just getting started. Still, over the past few years, she's dabbled in more adult fare (especially on the small screen), so it definitely seems like she's trying to show off her range.

Recent findings suggest that from 2016 to 2018, Apatow portrayed a supporting character, Arya Hopkins, who's tutored by series lead Gus (Paul Rust) on the Netflix TV show "Love," while on another Netflix exclusive, "Unstable," she appeared alongside Rob Lowe and his real-life son John Owen Love. The latter duo play tech CEO Ellis Dragon and his creatively inclined son Jackson, respectively, whereas Apatow plays Anna, an intern at Ellis' company, itself aptly named Dragon, who also happens to be the former stepdaughter of the company's CFO Anna ("Fleabag" standout Sian Clifford).

Then there's "Tell Me Lies." A deliciously dramatic and dishy Hulu series created by Meaghan Oppenheimer, "Tell Me Lies" adapts (and improves) the book of the same name by Carola Lovering and ran for three seasons on Hulu. Apatow shows up as a college student named Amanda in the third and final season, creating a problem for series regular Bree (Cat Missal) as she mentally and emotionally recovers from an affair with a professor named Oliver (Tom Ellis). After she finally gets out of Oliver's clutches, Bree notices that Amanda seems to be Oliver's next victim, sending her into a spiral.

You can see Apatow as Proserpina in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" in theaters now.

During IndieWire’s recent Craft Roundtables, “Backrooms” VFX Supervisor Edward Douglas broke down the unique workflow that he developed with Parsons during pre-production. Five Hacks Every Apple Watch Series 12 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (807 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the latest Apple Watches have a lot of fresh features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks.
  • The Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models.
  • You don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the latest Apple Watches have a lot of fresh features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks. While our general Apple Watch and fitness tracking hacks are still golden, Series 12 devices offer new features like native step counting, a Readiness app, an upgraded heart rate sensor, an AI-based version of Siri, and "audio intelligence" that can replay and summarize real-life conversations, within limits. Here's how to get the most out of them.

The Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models. Enjoy it! To add a step counter to your watch face, long-press on the clock screen to edit it, tap on a complication (that’s what Apple calls those little icons and numbers that appear on some watch faces), choose Activity, and then tap Steps.

You don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion. A button in your Apple Watch’s Control Center can turn the feature on and off. Keep it off except when you have a structured conversation that you’ll want to refer to later. This feature is at the moment in beta (which you can try now if you want to), but is expected to be available to everyone later this year.

It has been revealed that it's worth turning off the default setting not just because of the creepiness factor, but also because the recaps work best when there is a single subject of conversation, with a clear start and end, and just one context. If you leave recaps running all the time, your doctor’s appointment will get mixed in with your grocery shopping, YouTube watching, and everyday chatter.

To finish off a recap and make it useful, take a look at the recap shortly after the conversation, tap the three-dots menu, and hit Edit. You’ll be able to adjust the notes and add your own important details. Siri won’t identify speakers and seems to shy away from including certain details, like people’s names. You can add in what it missed and also create your own bullet points so that everything gets noted down while it’s still fresh in your mind.

This one isn’t specific to the Series 12, but if you haven’t gotten on board with the pinch and wrist flick gestures yet, now is a great time.

First, the wrist flick: If a notification is on your screen, or you’re otherwise looking at something you’d rather be done with, just flick your wrist away from you and then back toward you, as if there were a crumb on the watch face and you wanted to knock it off. This will bring you back to the watch face and close whatever you were looking at.

According to recent reports, the double pinch is another useful one, although Apple calls it double tap. This is confusing because you aren’t double tapping the watch, you’re tapping your thumb and forefinger together while wearing the watch. You don’t need to touch the watch face at all. So, when you get a notification or a call, look at it on your watch, and pinch your thumb and forefinger (of the watch hand) together twice. The watch detects the pinch from subtle movements in your wrist, and it will open the notification. You can then use the wrist flick to close the notification. Performing a double pinch when no notification is on screen will bring up your smart stack. You can then double-pinch to move to the next card in the smart stack, or single-pinch to open that card and see its details.

Sources indicate that if you want to learn even more gestures, go into the Watch app, and select Accessibility and then Hand gestures. You can remap a whole-fist “clench” to do the same thing as pressing the digital crown, for example, or to open the control center or Siri.

A little rude, perhaps, but helpful: With the newly introduced AI-based Siri, sometimes answers to questions can be long-winded. If Siri launches into a novel-length response and you’re not interested in hearing all that, just put your palm over the screen. You’ll instantly be transported back to your watch face, and the Siri response will stop.

In a recent development, if you still want to see those longer responses without having Siri read the whole thing to you, you can set this up on your phone, and the settings will carry over to your watch. On your iPhone, go to Settings and tap Siri, then Responses. Select Silent responses instead of Spoken responses. You can then read through her answers, or skim them, as you prefer.

GTA 6's Autosave Is Ruining The Game, But Not For The Reason You Think

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (654 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 might be the best-rated game of all time, but that doesn't mean players love every single thing about the open-world shooter.
  • The issue began attracting attention after high-profile incidents involving Twitch streamers like JasonTheWeen, who lost 12 hours of progress after accidentally turning off his PlayStation 5.
  • Most people aren't losing half a day's worth of progress.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 might be the best-rated game of all time, but that doesn't mean players love every single thing about the open-world shooter. Some drawbacks, like the game's wonky controls, can be adjusted. Others, players are simply stuck with. One of the biggest complaints is that GTA 6's autosave feature simply isn't good enough.

The issue began attracting attention after high-profile incidents involving Twitch streamers like JasonTheWeen, who lost 12 hours of progress after accidentally turning off his PlayStation 5. It's reasonable to expect that closing a game suddenly might result in some lost progress, but losing 12 hourswas so frustrating that the streamer burst into tears on camera.

Most people aren't losing half a day's worth of progress. Early reports suggest that streamers accessing the game early via the "New Zealand trick" are encountering unforeseen issues with the workaround. Still, many GTA 6 fans were incensed enough about lost playtime to complain about the autosave feature​​​​​​​ on social media.

Recent findings suggest that "4 hours gone, no autosave, no save file..." one fan wrote on a gaming Facebook group. "What the actual! A billion dollar game and this has broken already!".

"I lost 10 hours to their​​​​​​​ dumbass save system," one Redditor alleged.

"What genius came up with this save feature," another complained.

In a recent development, the problem is partially due to a knowledge gap. GTA 6 does autosave​​​​​​​, typically at the start of a mission or at a checkpoint​​​​​​​. If a player elects to spend hours between missions shopping or cruising the streets, GTA 6 won't autosave any of that game time. Players should regularly pause the game and save manually.

In a recent development, the problem isn't just infrequent saving.​​​​​​​ Progress in GTA 6 is slow-going compared to previous games.​​​​​​​ It's harder to steal cars now, and the map is much bigger, so getting anywhere takes time. The roads are narrower, so it's easier to get into a car crash. Many players find themselves struggling with the game's idiosyncratic controls. It's easy to aggravate an NPC by pressing the wrong button, which can set off a chain of unwanted events. Loading an earlier save to undo the damage might also mean losing significant progress.

In a recent development, many of GTA 6's systems mimic real life, and the autosave glitch can make the quiet yet rewarding gameplay feel tedious. Even if a player loses just 20 minutes, during that time they could havewoken up​​​​​​​, worked out, drunk a protein shake, showered, chosena upcoming outfit, and answered some texts​​​​​​​. They spoke to the neighbor, picked up a new quest, and biked to the grocery store. While buying bread,​​​​​​​ they accidentally pulled out a gun and scared the cashier. The worker called the police.

It wouldn't take that long to do it all over again from an earlier save file​​​​​​​, but repeating everything would be a major bummer. The player could try to outrun the cops — but then getting back to what they intended to do might take twice as long. That's assuming that nothing goes wrong during the chase, which is a tall order in the world of GTA.

In a recent development, that propensity for chaos might explain why Rockstar's current system works the way it does. If GTA 6 saved more often, players would be perpetually stuck with the haywire consequences of their actions. There must be a middle ground, though.​​​​​​​ The game could autosave more frequently, across multiple temporary save files. That tweak still wouldn't change GTA 6's focus on the monotony of day-to-day life, which is what fans are truly struggling with.

Sources indicate that the likelihood of an update here seems slim since Rockstar has used a similar system for saves across many of its games​​​​​​​. Perhaps the best GTA 6 fans can do is save often​​​​​​​ — and learn to embrace the pandemonium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disney has produced many of the best animated movies of all time. They've been doing it longer than anyone else and, arguably, better than anyone else for decades. Unfortunately though, original animation has been a tough sell to audiences in recent years, and Disney's "Hexed" looks like it's going to suffer at the box office as a result of this trend.

"Hexed" is presently eyeing an opening in the $23 million range, per Box Office Theory. That's across the full five-day, Wednesday to Sunday stretch since this movie is opening mid-week for the Thanksgiving holiday. The comedy "Focker In-Law" pits Ben Stiller against Ariana Grande and looks to win the weekend with around $36 million. For what it's worth, earlier tracking (via Deadline) had both movies doing between $40 and $50 million across the five-day stretch.

More than A24's "Club Kid" or or the "Hershey" biopic, also releasing over Thanksgiving, it's "The Hunger Games" that will be a bigger problem for Disney's latest. "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" will be a bigger hit than you realize, doing well over $100 million on opening weekend. That means, in its second frame, it could still easily take number one over Thanksgiving.

Recent findings suggest that disney's latest centers on an impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie (Hailee Steinfeld) who discovers secret magical abilities which. Once unleashed, they hurtle her out of suburbia and into a vast witch realm called Hexe. Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand directed the movie, with Josie Trinidad co-directing.

Recent findings suggest that the major glitch for "Hexed" is that these movies don't come cheap. We're looking at a budget of at least $150 million, if not much more. Even at $150 million, an opening under $30 million across a robust, long holiday weekend is close to a death sentence. Yes, there are overseas markets to account for and family-friendly movies can have long legs. Even so, the early estimates are rough, to put it kindly.

Industry observers note that it's especially disappointing because this feels like the right place on the calendar for the movie. "Moana 2" smashed box office records and led to the biggest Thanksgiving ever in 2024. That eventually became a $1 billion hit for Disney. But that was a sequel to a much-beloved move from the 2010s. Originals, from both Disney Animation and Pixar, have struggled mightily in the 2020s.

Case in point, "Strange World" bombed at the box office in 2022, taking in just $73 million worldwide. "Hexed" doesn't appear to be in such terrible shape but it's not looking good. Disney's "Wish" was also a massive disappointment at the box office in 2023, doing $255 million worldwide. Decent for an original movie by today's standards but not nearly good enough to turn a profit.

The only thing Disney can hope for is that word of mouth amongst moviegoers is outstanding, which could give "Hexed" unusually long legs. Or that tracking is just wildly off and the movie actually comes in closer to earlier estimates. Either way, as it stands, this one looks like it just has one too many hurdles to clear.

Disney's "Hexed" hits theaters on November 25, 2026.

Why Good Voice Acting Doesn’t Have to Happen in Isolation

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1167 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Film is always a collaborative medium, but one of the special things about animation is that you can craft incredibly nuanced performances with people who never get to meet.
  • Sources indicate that “Wildwood” director Travis Knight did a lot of the directing of his voice cast in lockdown Zooms, and hodge-podge recording setups, where it can be hard to remember that you’re developing something that needs to spiritually connect to the animation, whether existing animatics already exist or not.
  • “It asks something very different of an actor, which is challenging because an actor can bring so much to performance before they even utter a word,” Knight told IndieWire on an episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit podcast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Film is always a collaborative medium, but one of the special things about animation is that you can craft incredibly nuanced performances with people who never get to meet. Voice acting in animation is a discipline in its own right — as legends like Mel Blanc and Eric Bauza show — where actors impart a kind of electric energy that carries through into the art style of what they’re voicing. So is voice directing. And the secret to both is in providing foundations for animators to build something bigger.

Sources indicate that “Wildwood” director Travis Knight did a lot of the directing of his voice cast in lockdown Zooms, and hodge-podge recording setups, where it can be hard to remember that you’re developing something that needs to spiritually connect to the animation, whether existing animatics already exist or not. There isn’t the same kind of immersiveness for actors that live-action sets, costumes, and the basic pleasure of getting to read lines against other actors all provide. They have to build it from scratch. Related Stories Watch the ‘Backrooms’ VFX Supervisor Explain His Unique Process of Collaborating with Kane Parsons Aaron Pierre on ‘Lanterns,’ the DC Shake-Up, and Landing a Role in Ryan Gosling’s ‘Star Wars’ Movie.

“It asks something very different of an actor, which is challenging because an actor can bring so much to performance before they even utter a word,” Knight told IndieWire on an episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit podcast. “So when you cast these things, it’s really interesting because sometimes the things we love about actors are not their voice; it’s everything else. So we will always listen, we’ll take clips from actors’ other films and their interviews, and we’ll put them against a design of a character.”.

Hearing a voice against a design can be revelatory, Knight believes, because it can teach a director and an animation team about who a character really is, whether a performer is really going to work or not, even before they step into the booth. It’s also an key way to help sort the whole of an ensemble so that actors occupy different aural frequencies and accents, and don’t sound too similar. You want to really be able to feel the difference between Carey Mulligan’s powerfully sinister Alexandra and Angela Bassett’s regal General.

And then, once the voice cast is in the booth, it’s also on the director and the team to help each voice actor sketch out all the different permutations of emotion the animators will then use as inspiration, and as tools.

Industry observers note that “You’ll get the scene 30, 40, 50 different ways,” Knight noted. “It takes forever. But, in the end, if you can do it properly, it feels like these characters are living in the same scene at the same time. And then it comes down to the animator to try to figure out how they can match the beauty of the vocal performance with the physical performance.”.

Recent findings suggest that that’s the normal process for feature animation: finding compelling voices, matching them with a design that feels spiritually connected to that voice, covering the performance many different ways, and then assembling a template for animators to build off of. And it’s the director, really, who has to hold in their head the many ways that the disparate parts will all come together.

It has been revealed that “An animator is an actor, but they’re just acting through their hands and through a puppet, and it’s two actors collaborating to create a complete performance. But oftentimes it happens across space, across time. And when it comes together in a harmonious way, it’s really beautiful because this thing seems like it’s completely alive,” Knight noted.

It has been revealed that but sometimes, voice actors’ performances do get to be alive together. That was a key creative choice that director Leah Nelson made for “Tangles” — it’s hard to argue with the logic of putting Abbi Jacobson, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, and Bryan Cranston all in a room together to act out an earnest family drama, even if there’s a bit of mic bleed.

It has been revealed that “I’m so glad we [put them together]. And it wasn’t that hard. It took a little bit of scheduling Tetris to get it done, but it was so worthwhile,” Nelson told IndieWire. “Abbi does a ton of voice work, and often they’re alone and not even able to have someone to read against them. Sometimes they’re just doing the lines and sort of jumping around. And what I ultimately wanted was to have this really naturalistic dialogue.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Tangles” boasts naturalism when it comes to sound, from bespoke foley to overlapping banter that isn’t meant to be precisely understood but to convey the chaos of one’s own (infuriating, loving) family. So Nelson and her team embraced the ways actors can build on each other, and even on improv, in recording the dialogue.

“A lot of humor came out of giving them time to not only play with the dialogue but to play with each other. But also, those really intimate and difficult moments of the film, they could look in each other’s eyes and work through those moments. That was important to me, and it was important to them as well. So it was an experience we all went through together.”.

The one downside of treating recording sessions more like the rehearsals for a play is the risk of wrecking takes. “We spent a lot of time at the table trying to hold [our reactions] in or like, ‘Don’t sneeze! Nobody move!’” Nelson joked. “But I didn’t want it to sound like there was so much suturing; the mastery of the dialogue editing to make it all sound naturalistic, so we also did a lot of work to make that happen. But what we had to work with felt very naturalistic to begin with.”.

The ultimate example of naturalistic voice acting, however, might be on display in “Wildwood.” Knight’s own son was a newborn while the team was laying down track for the film, which made him the perfect actor for the role of kidnapped Baby Mac.

“I essentially chased him around the house with a digital recorder. Sometimes with my iPhone. I was just trying to coax things out of him, make him laugh and giggle and verbalize. And the thing about babies is that they’re constantly trying to make sense of the world,” Knight stated. “They’re always babbling and trying to make shapes with their mouths. So we have a lot of that babbling in the movie, and it helped make it feel naturalistic.”.

It speaks to the wide-ranging power of voice acting in animation: you can get to naturalism through a grounded collaboration between actors, an actor in complete isolation, or hitting “record” on an iPhone while you’re changing a diaper.

“Wildwood” is now in theaters. “Tangles” releases in theaters on January 15, 2027.

Breaking: 10 Hacks Every watchOS 27 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1373 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, watchOS 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your Apple Watch supports it.
  • In a recent development, with watchOS 27, Apple changed what double-pressing the Digital Crown does.
  • It seems Apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchOS 27.2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, watchOS 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your Apple Watch supports it. While the newest enhancement isn't Apple's most feature-filled, it does include a number of changes that improve the way you exercise, track your health, and locate missing items. That's especially true for anyone with the latest Series 12 or Ultra 4. If your Apple Watch supports watchOS 27, you should know about these 10 hacks:.

In a recent development, with watchOS 27, Apple changed what double-pressing the Digital Crown does. Instead of opening the app switcher, it now triggers Audio Intelligence—if you have an Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4. If you don't have access to those features, the gesture now does nothing.

It seems Apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchOS 27.2. When you're using an app while running this latest revision, press and hold the bottom part of the watch's screen, and you'll trigger the app switcher. You can now jump to a different app, or close an app that isn't working. Sadly, this only works when you're already in an app, and not when you're on the Home Screen, but it's certainly better than nothing.

While you can load up multiple complications on your Apple Watch, they aren't exactly dynamic. That's why I'm a big fan of the Smart Stack widgets on the Apple Watch, which update dynamically to show contextual information. Now, with the new Siri Modular Face, you can access dynamic widgets on the Home Screen. If you've just parked your car, for example, you'll see a widget showing its location; likewise, if you have an upcoming calendar appointment, it will be front and center.

In a recent development, to use the Siri Modular watch face, tap and hold on the screen, go to the end of the list, tap the Plus button, and find and add the Siri Modular watch face. Once you do, you'll start seeing dynamic widgets when you wake up your watch. Don't expect much personalization from this watch face, however. You can customize the colors and add three small complications, but that's it.

Sources indicate that the double-tap gesture is one of my favorite Apple Watch features. By tapping your thumb and index finger together twice, you can do things like answer a call or reply to a message. In watchOS 27, Apple took the gesture one step forward. You can now use the double-tap gesture to scroll through your widgets; if you perform a single tap, it then opens the highlighted widget or the shortcut. This means you can open and browse the weather app, or start a workout, without ever touching your Apple Watch's screen.

In a recent development, your Apple Watch's latest Music Recognition app has native Shazam integration. What's more, Shazam will record your request even when you're offline and away from your iPhone. The moment you reconnect, the service will identify the songs, which you can see in the Shazam app on your iPhone or Apple Watch.

It has been revealed that it seems like Apple has a library of songs it uses for offline recognition, because in my testing, it was able to recognize a Coldplay song instantly, even when in Airplane mode. To use it, you can either open the Music Recognition app, or you can add the widget for faster access. Scroll up on the Home Screen, go to the bottom of the screen, tap the Edit button, then the Plus button, and add the Music Recognition widget.

It has been revealed that apple Watches have traditionally lacked a live step count widget or complication. To find your step count, you had to go to the bottom of the Activity app, or rely on third-party apps. But even still, these apps never highlighted live data. You’d always have to wait a couple of seconds to see the updated stats.

It has been revealed that now, if you own the latest Apple Watch Series 12 or the Ultra 4, you can add a live step count widget or complication to the Apple Watch face or the Smart Stack. This will show you your precise step count at all times. To use it, go to the bottom of the Smart Stack, tap the Edit button, then tap the Plus button. Here, find and add the fresh Step count widget.

Sources indicate that siri is no longer a voice assistant that you use for one-off tasks. With Siri AI, you can now carry on multiple conversations with context and memory. It's not as robust as ChatGPT or Claude, but you can use Siri AI for brainstorming, researching, and jotting down ideas for later.

It has been revealed that the Siri AI app on the iPhone reveals all your conversations, and so does the Apple Watch. This means you can continue your Siri AI conversations and view past chats on your Apple Watch. To use it, press the Digital Crown once, then tap the Siri app icon in the center. This will open up all your conversations instead of calling upon Siri. Tap a conversation to continue your chat on the Apple Watch. Of course, anything you do here will be reflected in the Siri app on your iPhone.

The upcoming Find My app on the Apple Watch demonstrates a single map for finding people, devices, and items. This means you can now locate your family members who are sharing their location with you, as well as AirTags or other Find My items from the watchOS app.

After opening the app, you can use the Digital Crown to zoom in or out of the map. Use touch to pan around. The map doesn't show all items and people at once, though. Tap the Menu button at the bottom-right corner, and then switch between People, Items, or Devices. If you have multiple items, you can scroll through them using the Digital Crown.

While it's not a Whoop-level feature, the Apple Watch now includes a Readiness score. Instead of individually looking at your training load, sleep score, and vitals, you now have one number that gives you the whole picture.

It has been revealed that the Readiness score ranges from 0 to 10 and is based on your recent fitness activity, sleep data, and background health monitoring. If you have a score of 8 to 10, your Apple Watch thinks you can push yourself, or "go for it," as it claims; if it's below 5, the watch thinks you should consider lighter activity. This feature, though, is only available on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. You can use the new Readiness app on your Apple Watch to see this data, but you can also access it on your iPhone in the Fitness app's new Readiness section.

According to recent reports, low Power Mode isn't your only option when it comes to extending the battery life for your Apple Watch. watchOS 27 offers a special Max Extended Workout mode just for long workouts. With it, your Apple Watch disables some features, like splits and alerts, and reduces the frequency of GPS and heart rate readings, in the hopes of extending your battery throughout your entire exercise. To use it, go to the Workout app and select the workout you want. Tap the Goals button in the top-right corner, and choose the Extended option. Then, switch to the Max Extended option and start your workout.

Industry observers note that the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 come with a set of Audio Intelligence features that use the microphones on the Apple Watch, paired with AI models (both local and cloud-based), to identify sounds, music, and record conversation. Thanks to this newly introduced feature, one of the iPhone's accessibility features also makes its way to the Apple Watch.

Sources indicate that sound Recognition can alert you when it hears sirens, alarms, doorbells, and more, even when your iPhone isn’t around. To set this up, go to the Settings app on your iPhone and navigate to Accessibility > Sound & Name Recognition > Sound Recognition. Here, enable the sounds you want to monitor, and make sure to turn on the Detect using Apple Watch toggle.
