Star Trek fans are always opinionated, especially about captains, but there's one captain in Paramount+'s Star Trek indicates that everyone holds in high regard. Star Trek: Discovery, Star Trek: Picard, Star Trek: Lower Decks, Star Trek: Prodigy, and Star Trek: Starfleet Academy introduced a slew of new captains leading those shows, but everyone agrees about Captain Christopher Pike (Anson Mount) on Star Trek: Strange New Worlds.

Recent findings suggest that star Trek under executive producer Alex Kurtzman took great pride in expanding diversity in the final frontier, fulfilling Gene Roddenberry's 60-year-old vision of Infinite Diversity in Infinite Combinations. From Michael Burnham (Sonequa Martin-Green) to Carol Freeman (Dawnn Lewis) to Seven of Nine (Jeri Ryan) to Nahla Ake (Holly Hunter), female captains, two of them Black women, took on greater prominence in Star Trek on Paramount+.

It has been revealed that unfortunately, Star Trek's attempt for any type of audience member to see themselves reflected in Starfleet doesn't please a vocal segment of the fandom, who use social media to condemn Star Trek's inclusiveness and call it "woke." Roddenberry created a future where every type of human (and humanoid, and other beings) can belong, and Star Trek's canon highlights a diverse cavalcade of captains. Yet Burnham, Ake, and others are 'controversial.'.

Christopher Pike is the lone modern Star Trek captain who is accepted by every type of fan. Let's face it, there is an obvious reason why, of course: Pike is a Caucasian heterosexual male. When he was created to lead 1965's rejected Star Trek pilot, "The Cage," Pike was played by Jeffrey Hunter. Star Trek: Discovery reintroduced Pike 53 years later, and they didn't try to reinvent Chris' race or gender. Rather, Anson Mount took a long-unused character and made him better and multidimensional.

Industry observers note that tall, handsome, dashing, and commanding, Captain Pike is agreeable to every viewer. To Anson Mount and Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' credit, however, Pike eschewed Jeffrey Hunter's original, weary version of the character, who was conceived with 1960s values. Captain Pike in Strange New Worlds is collaborative and compassionate. Chris' assertiveness is backed by a deep respect for and protectiveness of his crew. Pike treats his crew as his family and regularly invites them to his home-cooked meals.

Captain Pike also broke the mold of the Captain of the Enterprise as a lonely individual 'married to his ship.' For the first three seasons of Star Trek: Strange Fresh Worlds, Chris was in a monogamous relationship with Captain Marie Batel (Melanie Scrofano). Other women from Pike's past occasionally returned, but Chris was devoted to Marie until he lost her. Still, Pike remembers an alternate future where he married Marie and had a child, a parting gift Batel gave them both.

It has been revealed that what's inherently admirable about Pike isn't that he's a white male, however. That's on the surface. In truth, Pike is not-so-secretly progressive; he surrounds himself with bright, capable women on the Starship Enterprise's bridge, and he values their talent and opinions. Pike also carries the unimaginable burden of knowing his tragic future will rob him of his autonomy. Yet Chris is in touch with his feelings and lives his life to the fullest, making the most of the time he has left.

One of the concerns that Star Trek: Strange New Worlds fans raised about seasons 3 and 4 is that Captain Pike seems to be somewhat diminished. Strange New Worlds is an exceptionally talented ensemble, and stories are spread out amongst them throughout each season's limited episode count. Star Trek fans who are used to the captain being the center of most episodes groan that Pike often takes a back seat to other characters.

Pike is still the Captain of the Enterprise and Strange Newly introduced Worlds' lead character until the series finale in season 5.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, as Star Trek: Strange Latest Worlds warps toward its inevitable conclusion, the prominence of James T. Kirk (Paul Wesley) increases. Strange New Worlds' endgame is for Pike to pass command of the USS Enterprise to Captain Kirk. Strange New Worlds is naturally building up Kirk's laurels to meet his destiny as a legendary captain, and it feels like it's at Pike's expense. However, Pike is still the Captain of the Enterprise and Strange New Worlds' lead character until the series finale in season 5.

Sources indicate that anson Mount is also a gifted comic actor, and Strange New Worlds has taken full advantage of his talent. Mount loves to play alternate versions of Pike, and he excels at embodying oddballs with Pike's face, like Strange New Worlds' holodeck spin on Gene Roddenberry in season 3's holodeck episode, or the sniveling Sir Armand Rauth in the fairy tale fantasy world of "The Elysian Kingdom.".

It has been revealed that no matter which Star Trek on Paramount+ series is someone's favorite, or even if they loathe Alex Kurtzman's era of Star Trek entirely, Captain Pike stands tall and apart as the lone modern captain accepted by all sides. Star Trek: Strange Latest Worlds has endured much criticism in its last two seasons, some of it justified, but Captain Pike maintains the gold standard expected of Star Trek's greatest captains.

Star Trek: Strange New Worlds is streaming on Paramount+.

Industry observers note that [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on October 2, 2026 during the 2026 Upcoming York Film Festival. Janus Film will release the film in limited theaters on Friday, November 20.].

Paul Thomas Anderson‘s eye for vivifying music onscreen dates back to the late 1990s when, after “Boogie Nights,” he made Technicolor mini-masterpiece music videos with his ex-girlfriend Fiona Apple — or made a San Fernando Valley-sized shrine to Aimee Mann with his third feature, “Magnolia.” Since then, he’s kicked around with HAIM while turning one third of its Los Angelino triumvirate, Alana Haim, into a screen actress. He’s shot for Radiohead and made a regular collaboration with band member Jonny Greenwood to create some of the 21st century’s most memorable scores. Many young cinephiles now associate the mischievously lilty notes of “Phantom Thread” with the poison promise of fresh love and obsessive creation. Related Stories Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Scores $21 Million in Previews, Second-Best Result of 2026 ‘Josephine’ Review: Another Heartsick Horror Film About Real Monsters from ‘Soft & Quiet’ Filmmaker.

Industry observers note that last December, PTA teamed up with Geese frontman Cameron Winter to film, while operating his own Panavision camera, his solo stage performance at Carnegie Hall, running through sparse piano arrangements of tracks off his solo album, “Heavy Metal.” The result, a 72-minute film now being distributed roadshow-style by Janus Films before inevitably living on the Criterion Collection, is a stunning arrangement of its own: a deeply achey, sincere but never cloyingly earnest concert movie that’s tender to the point of frailty. (Benny Safdie counts as a co-producer, and the film’s scratchy Latest York quality and setting can’t help but have his imprint.).

The matted-hair, lithe Winter can seem a bit uncomfortable in his own skin in the public eye, as he did onstage ahead of “Cameron Winter at Carnegie” at its Newly introduced York Film Festival world premiere at Alice Tully Hall. But on the piano, laser-beamed into his songcraft, he’s quietly electrified, at seemingly at peace as his tenorous vocal glissando and nimble fingerwork on the piano produce shiveringly tender folk ballads that echo Harry Nilsson and Van Morrison. (The usual comparisons to Tom Waits and Rufus Wainright are right, too, but Winter is his own strange thing.) If you weren’t previously sold on the wily Winter antic rock chaos of Geese — rapidly becoming one of the most popular contemporary art rock bands of these times — you’re about to. Paul Thomas Anderson has created a rhapsodic shrine to the man that is nonetheless ballad-sized in its emotional scale.

Winter, in December, played and sang to a sold-out crowd of more than 2,700 at the stately cultural temple that is Carnegie Hall, and this film can at times feel like a religious experience, an incantation, a lonely vigil. The singer/songwriter was 23 at the time of the performance, one year older than Bob Dylan when he headlined Carnegie Hall, and similarly at the precipice of major fame. Fixed on a mobile rig that will at times careen and whoosh across the stage when not otherwise holding on Winter, Anderson’s camera catches the expressionism and chiaroscuro of stage lights illuminating and fading off the singer’s face.

The result is hynoptic, a concert film up there with “Stop Making Sense” but for introverts. Songs like the popular single “$0” acquire an even more wrenchingly somber quality as a lovelorn protagonist rues being exploited by a relationship (“You’re making me feel like a dollar in your hand / You’re making me feel like I’m a zero dollar man”). Stripped of production, his indie hit “Love Takes Miles” plays even better. While many of the songs sort of hover in the same key and bleed into one another, that makes for an all the more transfixing experience. The lack of an interstitial anything save for a sweet prologue and moving coda make for experience also that’s immersive, deep, and the kind whose truth you can feel somewhere in your body even if you can’t quite articulate it.

In a recent development, “Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall premiered at the Fresh York Film Festival. Janus Films will release it in theaters starting November 20.

Google Killed Its Dark Web Report, but You Can Still Monitor Data Breaches

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (770 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let people scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers.
  • Google indicates it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for customers whose data was found on the dark web.
  • Dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let owners run scans free of cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let people scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers. But the company discontinued the service at the start of 2026, with new scans stopping on Jan. 15 and all accounts deleted on Feb. 16.

Google indicates it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for customers whose data was found on the dark web. Google promised a latest service that would provide more actionable intel, but that service has yet to materialize, and there haven’t been any further announcements about it yet.

Dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let owners run scans free of cost. Now that it’s gone, however, there are plenty of other services that offer the same service at varying costs and levels of effectiveness. Let’s talk through the nature of the insight that Google's reports offered, how it collected that information in the first place, and what options exist in the market to replace it.

Google debuted the Dark Web Report in March 2023 as a premium feature available to Google One consumers, but later extended it for free to anyone with a Google account and moved it to the "Results about you" dashboard.

Recent findings suggest that you'd set up a monitoring profile with your name, date of birth, physical address, phone number, emails, and Social Security Number if you lived in the U.S. After that, you could head to the dashboard anytime you wanted to run a free scan across dark web forums and marketplaces, publicly disclosed corporate data breaches, and other hidden online spaces to see if any of your personal information had shown up there. It was easy to use—but not a lot of people knew it existed in the first place.

It’s unclear what prompted the internal decision at Google, but in the absence of concrete next steps, it is reasonable to think the reports could create panic for the uninitiated. There’s no way to remove your information from the dark web once it’s already in circulation there. Still, having an early warning so you could reset 2FA or self-lock your SSN isn’t without merit.

Sources indicate that but perhaps more importantly, most people with Google accounts didn’t know and hadn’t heard of the Dark Web Report’s existence. Google has likely taken it as a hint that owners want more active remediation tools than simple alerts, which is why it’s now directing users to the Password Manager, Passkeys, and “Results about you” dashboard instead—though, again, the company hasn't followed through on a direct replacement for Dark Web Report, despite teasing such a feature.

Sources indicate that many of the top dark web scanners draw from the same well of information, scanning against major data breaches and dark web spaces. Several also offer breach notifications that send you email alerts when your details show up in a periodic scan. However, none of that is worth paying for because Have I Been Pwned or Mozilla Monitor cover those features quite well for free. Even the default password managers from Google and Apple come with some ability to monitor leaked credentials.

There isn’t an easy way to scrub your information from the dark web once it ends up getting leaked. But you can take steps to protect sensitive information or financial data once you know there’s been a leak. If a password has been compromised, reset it immediately. Also, enable 2FA on the affected account for added security. Even better, switch to a passkey if that account supports it. If not, authenticator apps are a safer way to receive 2FA codes than standard SMS.

In a recent development, if your Social Security number has been leaked, freeze your credit with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. You can do this by contacting each agency separately. Freezing your credit will prevent unauthorized credit withdrawals and protect your credit score from abuse by attackers. If one of your credit or debit card numbers has ended up in a breach, call your bank to freeze transactions on that card immediately.

Finally, get in the habit of using email aliases instead of sharing your actual email address with every platform and service provider. Addy.io and Proton’s SimpleLogin are both popular services that let you generate temporary email aliases that point to your inbox.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tom Cruise‘s performance in Alejandro González Iñárritu‘s “Digger” is one of the boldest and most entertaining of the actor’s career, as he suppresses not only his usual movie star charisma but his entire way of walking and talking to play paunchy, aging oil tycoon Digger Rockwell.
  • To aid in his complete transformation, Cruise called on one of the best prosthetic designers in the business, Kazu Hiro.
  • According to recent reports, “Alejandro is an amazing director, and he has lots of ideas,” Hiro told IndieWire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tom Cruise‘s performance in Alejandro González Iñárritu‘s “Digger” is one of the boldest and most entertaining of the actor’s career, as he suppresses not only his usual movie star charisma but his entire way of walking and talking to play paunchy, aging oil tycoon Digger Rockwell. Cruise is barely recognizable in the role, which is about as far from heroic characters like Pete “Maverick” Mitchell and Ethan Hunt as Cruise’s Ron Kovic in “Born on the Fourth of July” was from race car driver Cole Trickle almost 40 years ago.

To aid in his complete transformation, Cruise called on one of the best prosthetic designers in the business, Kazu Hiro. Hiro has turned Gary Oldman into Winston Churchill (“The Darkest Hour”), Charlize Theron into Megyn Kelly (“Bombshell”), and Dwayne Johnson into “Smashing Machine” Mark Kerr, but transforming Cruise into Texas oilman Digger Rockwell was a whole fresh task — one made even more challenging by Iñárritu and Cruise’s persistent striving for perfectionism, and constant eagerness to try new approaches. Related Stories ‘Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall’ Review: PTA’s Spellbinding Concert Doc Is a Gorgeously Tender Performance Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Scores $21 Million in Previews, Second-Best Result of 2026.

According to recent reports, “Alejandro is an amazing director, and he has lots of ideas,” Hiro told IndieWire. “Every day he comes in with a new idea, and we have to come up with an answer for how to achieve it. And Tom is really professional, and expects everybody else to be at that same level, ready for any situation. After the first day of testing, I learned that I had to stay flexible to respond to whatever they wanted.”.

Industry observers note that to that end, Hiro created modular prosthetics whose parts could easily be swapped out and moved around, so that Cruise and Iñárritu could constantly try newly introduced looks. “Sometimes with heavy makeup, you can’t change it,” Hiro noted. “I created prosthetics that could be mixed, so we could make new designs on the spot — try this forehead with these cheeks and this nose, then change it.” Creating Cruise’s look was a constantly evolving process throughout the long prep period. “We didn’t have a clear answer until the end of rehearsal.”.

Recent findings suggest that hiro’s mandate at the beginning was a bit open-ended, which gave him room for artistic exploration but also made it difficult to zero in on a precise look. “Alejandro mentioned the character was 76 years old and an oil tycoon,” Hiro said. “He also said he didn’t want the character to look like Tom, but he still wanted to see Tom in the character.” To try to find a concrete image for Digger Rockwell, Hiro immersed himself in research.

“I researched real oil tycoons and how they aged and what kinds of lifestyles they had,” Hiro mentioned. “Those lifestyles affect how they age.” As Hiro did more and more research, however, he realized that there was no one look that defined the entire profession he was trying to represent. “Everybody looked so different, so in the end I relied more on the storyline and how this particular character behaved.” The idea, in keeping with the slightly heightened style of the film as a whole, was to exaggerate Cruise’s features but keep the character realistic.

Hiro began with a 3D scan and life cast of Cruise, which he used to sculpt his designs. His paramount concern was allowing the actor to be as expressive as possible under the makeup. “The vital part is to make the prosthetic very soft so he can move,” Hiro remarked, noting that three weeks before shooting, Iñárritu called with a significant change. “He decided that Digger should be 65, not 76, so I quickly made a upcoming design. Tom is around that age, but he looks much younger than a normal 65. Under his eye was exposed and the rest of the face was covered, but I made it thin to give him freedom.”.

It has been revealed that in addition to Digger’s face, Hiro was also tasked with creating an upper body for an early scene in which Cruise would be seen stripped down to his pajama pants. The body prosthetic was intended only for that one scene, with a lighter bodysuit created for the rest of the movie. “We made a light version of the padding for under the costume, because we don’t need to see the skin after that first scene,” Hiro remarked. “For the first scene we made a silicone prosthetic that was a lot heavier — the body padding was around 10 pounds, but the silicone was 40 or 50.”.

Industry observers note that during one of Cruise’s costume fittings, he told Hiro he wanted to feel the weight of the silicone throughout production. “He tried the body prosthetic on and noted, ‘I like this, I want to wear it every day,'” Hiro said. “I told him it would be really heavy and hot, but he said he was training and would be fine.” Since gluing the body prosthetic on every day would be extremely time-consuming, Hiro created a strong spandex foundation and glued the prosthetic to it so Cruise could slip it on each day.

“He wore that for the whole film,” Hiro mentioned. “One time he said, ‘This is so heavy, it’s really hard on my back.’ I thought, ‘Okay, you asked for it,’ but he went through with it and finished the film, so that was amazing.”.

Marvel drew massive crowds with an Avengers: Doomsday photo experience, a VisionQuest walk-through, daily cosplay meetups, and a joint WEBTOON collaboration. Guests of Honor like Nicolas Cage, Hayden Christensen, Matt Smith, Jamie Campbell Bower, Linda Cardellini, Michael C. Hall, and VisionQuest's Paul Bettany and James Spader headlined autograph sessions and lively Q&As. Meanwhile, Artist Alley overflowed with comic royalty, including Jim Lee, Frank Miller, Scott Snyder, Nick Dragotta, Dan Mora, Tom King, Peach Momoko, and Todd McFarlane.

Marvel fans themselves are a major attraction of New York Comic-Con every year due to their breathtakingly creative cosplays, and this time, they didn't disappoint.

Industry observers note that besides the panels, events, guests, and merchandise, cosplayers are a staple of comic conventions. This year, hundreds of passionate Marvel fans attended Upcoming York Comic-Con 2026 wearing their best self-designed costumes, with breathtaking renditions of famous and obscure character designs. On X, the official Marvel Entertainment account shared a compilation thread of some of the best cosplays seen at NYCC 2026, ranging everywhere from comics, video games, and Marvel Cinematic Universe character and costume designs. Check out the thread below:.

Sources indicate that some of the cosplays featured in Marvel Entertainment's compilation include a literally glowing recreation of Marvel Rivals' playable Daredevil, a terrifying zombie variant of Chris Evans' Captain America from the MCU's Avengers: Endgame, a movie-ready and comic-accurate Agent Venom, a female variant of Alfred Molina's Doctor Octopus from Sam Raimi's Spider-Man 2, and a rock-and-rolling Spider-Punk who's instantly recognizable even without his spiky mask. A movie-accurate Iron Man suit of armor with the Fantastic Four's color palette and logo also makes its case for an eventual appearance in the MCU, all without the need for CGI enhancements.

Recent findings suggest that cosplay has evolved from a niche convention hobby into a sophisticated multidisciplinary craft with the same level of quality and attention to detail as professional Hollywood prop houses. Creators are no longer satisfied with generic recreations of characters' regular appearances. Nowadays, it's common for modern cosplayers to obsess over hyper-specific artistic interpretations of character designs and costumes from specific comic book runs, video game skins, and movies down to the tiniest details. The cosplaying community has also expanded its creative ambition toward deep-cut characters from indie comics, anime, and cult games, as well as original reinventions and mashups of their favorite pop culture icons.

An explosion of accessible fabrication tools and engineering ingenuity has allowed the cosplay community to take a massive leap in realism and accuracy. Materials like high-density EVA foam, thermoplastics, custom silicone prosthetics, and affordable home 3D printers allow cosplayers to sculpt intricate costumes and accessories plates that used to require major studio budgets and rare tools. Modern cosplays integrate microcontrollers, programmable LEDs, and motorized servos into their builds to produce wonders like fully articulated Iron Man suits and helmets or functional mechanical wings. This explosion in creativity and skill has also paved the way for dedicated prop studios and replica designers whose products are nothing short of Hollywood-grade.

Recent findings suggest that magic, mystical creatures, and exciting newly introduced worlds are what make the fantasy genre so alluring for many. It's the perfect genre for escapism. You're not exactly likely to be thinking about work when you could be thinking about dragons. It's no wonder the internet is buzzing about many upcoming movies in the genre.

From another Shrek movie to a fresh video game adaptation in the form of The Legend of Zelda, there's a lot to like for fantasy lovers who enjoy going to the theater. If fantasy is one of your favorite genres, then there are certain movies you absolutely need to know that are coming out soon, so you can order your tickets ahead of time. You're not going to be the only one dying to see these films.

Recent findings suggest that the newer Jumanji movies are a guilty pleasure franchise for many. So, while it's highly likely the movie will pack theaters upon release, there aren't as many people posting about it on social media. The brave fans who are willing to publicly admit they watch the movies are all thrilled to be getting the third installment of the new Jumanji movies. And with good reason, it's certain to be a fun movie packed with action and humor.

Jumanji: Open World will be the fourth movie in the series, including the one from 1995. The upcoming movie will hit theaters on December 25, 2026, making it a great family outing during the week between Christmas and Newly introduced Years. The movie will feature the same star-studded cast we're accustomed to, including Dwayne Johnson, Jack Black, Karen Gillian, and Kevin Hart. Open World will take place in the "real world." Instead of characters being sucked into a video game, the game will be exploding into the real world — just like the original movie. This means the teens who have been getting dragged into the video game will be contending with the characters they play rather than becoming them. This will be the final movie in the new trilogy of Jumanji movies.

Video game to movie adaptations have a rough reputation for disappointing fans of the original source content. That doesn't stop Hollywood from continuing to try and lure gamers into flocking to their local theater, though. The latest attempt is The Legend of Zelda and no, it will not be animated. The production will be a live action starring Benjamin Evan Ainsworth as Link and Bo Bragason as Zelda.

Life-long fans of the Zelda games are understandably wary of the movie and whether the film's interpretation of the games will match their expectations. Anyone curious will have to wait a few more months though, because The Legend of Zelda movie is expected to release in theaters on April 30, 2027. So far, social media has mostly been hesitant about the movie, but if the past is any indication, that won't stop fans from lining up to see it.

Children of Blood and Bone is a high fantasy movie based on a book with the same name. The book was written by Tomi Adeyemi and Children of Blood and Bone is the first of a trilogy. The story takes place in a fictional country called Orïsha, which many people presume to be a magical version of pre-colonial Nigeria. This isn't the Euro-centric style of fantasy Hollywood usually produces, so it's not surprising that many people are thrilled that this movie with a fresh perspective will be releasing soon.

According to recent reports, there was a social media scandal during the summer of 2026 when the author of the original story, Adeyemi, blocked some of the people working on the movie adaptation and even posted that she was distancing herself from the film. However, the author also made it clear that she did not want anyone to boycott the movie. Confusion further erupted when Adeyemi enthusiastically posted the movie trailer for Children of Blood and Bone when it was released.

Readers are still hyped to see Children of Blood and Bone when it enters theaters on February 5, 2027. The movie is directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood. The cast is composed of powerhouse stars including Idris Elba, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Cynthia Erivo, Regina King, Viola Davis, and more. If you're always on the lookout for a movie that isn't a reboot, remake, or sequel, this needs to go on your must-watch list immediately.

In a recent development, this one is a contentious one online, but it has certainly received a lot of discussion, both good and bad. Narnia: The Magician's Nephew is based on the sixth Narnia book published by C.S. Lewis, but chronologically in the Narnia timeline, it's the first story. The Magician's Nephew hasn't ever been turned into a movie, despite the existence of multiple versions of The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe.

Industry observers note that this new Narnia movie is directed by Greta Gerwig, the same director as The Barbie movie from 2023. While Gerwig has a solid fanbase who will watch anything she makes, those who adore the source material for Narnia are less excited about this movie. Gerwig's trailer features an Aslan voiced by Meryl Streep, a new setting in the 1950s instead of the early 1900s, and a rock-opera theme. While some have found their curiosity piqued by the trailer, others are already disappointed that the source material was so readily ignored.

Recent findings suggest that the movie will be in theaters on February 12, 2027. But Narnia: The Magician's Nephew is already set to enter Netflix's catalog on April 2, 2027, for anyone who would rather stream it. Other notable actors in the movie include Carrie Mulligan and Daniel Craig.

In a recent development, four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

Industry observers note that you want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

Recent findings suggest that you would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Sources indicate that godzilla x Kong: Supernova is the sixth Godzilla movie to come from Hollywood production companies and is directed by Grant Sputore. The movie will reach theaters on March 26, 2027. The movie, written by Dave Callaham, will star Sam Neill, Kaitlyn Dever, Jack O'Connell, and Dan Stevens. A teaser trailer was released on May 29, 2025, letting fans know that production had begun.

This movie will bring in a new threat in the form of SpaceGodzilla, though not much more is known about the storyline at this time, aside from the phrase "cataclysmic threat" being tossed around. Despite having few details, that hasn't been stopping Monsterverse fans from being very excited and chattering online with enthusiasm. At this time, there is no full-length trailer for Godzilla x Kong: Supernova.

Far and away, the fantasy movie coming to theaters in the near future with the most hype is Shrek 5. Theories, hopes, and dreams regarding a fifth installment of the animated franchise were shared long before it was ever confirmed. And there was plenty of celebration when the announcement of Shrek 5 finally came. The movie has been a long time coming and fans are clamoring for what comes next in the series of movies.

Recent findings suggest that the animated movie will be released to theaters on June 30, 2027. However, it had originally been slated for a December 23, 2026 release. This new date will likely give it the space to dominate the box office without competition from the likes of Jumanji: Open World and other Christmas-time releases such as Dune 3. The cast of the other four films have been brought back for the latest movie, including Eddie Murphy, Mike Myers, and Cameron Diaz. The cast will also feature Zendaya, Marcello Hernández, and Skyler Gisonodo as the voices of Shrek's three children.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, google has given its AI-powered "Ask Maps" feature a major upgrade, adding tools for trip planning, real-time route guidance, appointment finding, and saved-list search. The updates begin rolling out today on Android and iOS.

Google debuted Ask Maps last March as an AI assistant designed to handle questions and requests more complicated than simply searching the word "bar" or "groceries." Instead of performing simple keyword searches, the idea behind Ask Maps is that you can describe several specific requirements at once, and Maps will find places that match them all. For example, you could ask for a restaurant with outdoor seating for a certain number of people, and "Ask Maps" will factor in your past searches and give you results. Of course, AI assistants have a habit of making things up, so even with today's roll-out, you'll want to double-check your sources before you drive an hour to the wrong restaurant.

According to recent reports, to me, this is the most useful new feature launching today. Whether you're planning a day trip for holiday shopping or something more ambitious, like a three-day road trip with coastal hikes and oceanfront dining, Ask Maps will put together a day-by-day schedule. Each plan includes insider tips and numbered map pins for every stop, so you can see the whole route at a glance. Once you're happy with the plan, you can share it with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop.

When it's time to head out, you can ask Maps to pull up your itinerary, or look for the "itinerary" badge in your chat history. You'll see real-time details such as live traffic conditions, whether a place is currently open, and even the vibe at your next stop.

Plans can change on the fly, too. Ask Maps to add a scenic viewpoint or a lunch spot along the way, then tap to get directions to your next stop straight from the itinerary.

Here's what else you can use Ask Maps to do, starting today.

Industry observers note that pulling up directions now surfaces "Know Before You Go" tips for your route. These include where to park or charge your car, along with real-time conditions like weather, potential delays, and tolls.

Ask Maps is also gaining some agentic capabilities. Allegedly, you can just ask, “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me,” and Ask Maps will show you open slots across nearby businesses. In addition to finding appointments, Google says this agent will be able to call local businesses on your behalf—stay tuned while I wait for the upgrade and test this one out myself.

If you keep lists of saved places, Ask Maps can now search them for you. Ask something like, "Which spots saved in my lists have availability for 5 in the next 30 minutes?" Ask Maps looks across your lists and checks live availability, so you can pick a place and go.

These updates start rolling out today on Android and iOS. Travel itineraries and saved-list search are available everywhere Ask Maps is offered. "Know Before You Go" route tips and appointment finding are launching first in the U.S., with more regions coming soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sharon Horgan had a string of British hits (including a couple we'll talk about here), before scoring stated successes with Divorce, Shining Vale, and Bad Sisters. She's swiftly rising in the ranks of TV super-producers, the acerbically funny HBO Max rom-com Youth (in which she also stars) being just the latest.

This earlier series created by and starring Sharon Horgan is a family sitcom that feels far more believable than most, seeing Irish primary school teacher Sharon (Horgan) hooking up with American ad exec Rob (Rob Delaney) over the course of a week, only to discover that she's pregnant once he returns home. They don't really have feelings for each other, but decide to give it a go at being a couple, eventually falling into marriage just before the birth of their child. There are lots of jokes and plenty of acerbic dialogue, but this isn't Married... with Children. Sharon and Rob can be a bit nasty to each other and to their sloppy friend group, but there's also something rather sweet in the show's conviction that having someone to be a mess with can be one of life's great joys. Stream Catastrophe on Prime Video.

A little more of a high-concept here, but nevertheless an effective show about reimagining yourself in middle age. Younger follows Liza Miller (Sutton Foster), a recently divorced woman in her 40s who finds that age is a barrier to reentering the publishing industry she left years earlier. After a compliment convinces her that she could pass for a younger woman (poor thing), she manages to convince the right people that she's just 26 in order to land an entry-level job. Seven seasons of misadventures ensue, but much of the show revolves around the twisty-turny relationship between Liza and Josh (Nico Tortorella), a tattoo artist in his twenties. Stream Younger on Netflix.

Bridget Everett stars as Sam Miller, who struggles to find her new direction after moving back to her hometown to care for her dying sister. (Don't worry: There's plenty of comedy in the drama, and it's not as heavy as it sounds.) She's solidly middle-aged and starting over, kinda—making new friends in a familiar environment where she has to confront the past and the future alike. Luckily, her love of singing—and a community of goofy oddballs—are there to help. It's another story of a person of a certain age, trying to rebuild their life following an upheaval. Stream Somebody Somewhere on HBO Max.

In a recent development, when all else fails: Start a punk band. This drama from Sally Wainwright (Gentleman Jack) sees five women start a punk band as a lark, just a fun way to kill some time by entering a local talent context. The women realize very promptly, though, that they're very, very pissed off—about the workplace for women, menopause, a diminished dating pool, caring for aging parents and grown children—all of it tied up in the ways in which we treat women, and particularly middle-aged women. The band is a way to reclaim their voices, which doesn't erase or negate any of their problems nor drama (and there's plenty here), but gives them a platform with which to make some noise about it. Stream Riot Women on Britbox.

More of a traditional sitcom, not that there's anything wrong with that, this one builds a lot of goodwill with the performance of Leanne Morgan, its lead and co-creator (alongside Susan McMartin and Chuck Lorre). She plays the show's lead: a Knoxville, Tennessee wife and mom, who finds herself suddenly single in her 50s after her husband of 33 years leaves her. It's a genial, old-school hang-out show with a phenomenal veteran supporting cast that includes Kristen Johnston, Ryan Stiles, and Tim Daly. Stream Leanne on Netflix.

Michele Buteau, who also co-created the series) stars here as a fashion-forward stylist who'd devoted herself to the wrong guy for way too long. As the series opens, Mavis Beaumont is ready for a fresh start, putting herself and her career first—which does not preclude falling into a number of romantic entanglements. As she claims more than once, she's going to take on the fashion world with a "body-positive attitude, cute v-neck, and some lip-gloss." Stream Survival of the Thickest on Netflix.

Sources indicate that certainly the goofiest take here on the idea of starting over in mid-life, this is very much a traditional three-camera sitcom, albeit one with a stacked cast of TV legends. Writer Melanie (Valerie Bertinelli), beautician Joy (Jane Leeves), and soap diva Victoria (Wendie Malick) wind up spending a wild night in Cleveland after a plane to Paris is diverted, discovering in the process that, while they're seen as over-the-hill back in Los Angeles, they're all Ohio 10s—though the sassy caretaker of their house, Elka (Betty White), might not agree. Stream Hot in Cleveland on Paramount+.

She'a s hair younger than Alex, but Fleabag (she's only ever referred to as "Fleabag") is trying to rebuild her life after a bad breakup, with extremely mixed results. This very dark comedy-drama follows a free-spirited, deeply angry single young woman living in London and sharing her romantic ups and downs via confessional asides to us, the audience. She falls, rather reluctantly, for "The Priest" (Andrew Scott)—while she's a confirmed atheist, and he's obviously not, the show doesn't turn aside from the general messiness of the situation. Phoebe Waller-Bridge won separate Emmys as the star, creator, and writer of the series. Stream Fleabag on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that maisel was one of Prime’s first truly buzzy original series, a comedy-drama from Amy Sherman-Palladino (Gilmore Girls) about the title’s Midge Maisel (Rachel Brosnahan), a long-time New York housewife of the late 1950s who discovers a talent for stand-up comedy. Inspired by the real-life careers of comedians like Totie Fields and Joan Rivers, the show is warm and welcoming, with great performances and dialogue; it also achieves something rare in being a show about comedy that’s actually funny. Stream The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel on Prime Video.

The substantial life change in this earlier Sharon Horgan hit is a little different: Julia Johnstone's mother had been a big help in taking care of Julia's children, but she's not going to do it anymore, leaving this working mom (Anna Maxwell Martin) to take the full brunt of childcare for the first time (her husband in the picture, but not much use). She joins up with other working moms involved with a local support group, including shallow Amanda (Lucy Punch), star of her own ongoing spin-off. Stream Motherland on Prime Video and Britbox.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The legacy-quel is alive and well, and it only makes sense that a sequel/reboot/reimagining would eventually come for “Home Alone,” Chris Columbus’ 1990 holiday classic starring Macaulay Culkin.

In a recent development, there was buzz that Culkin over the summer pitched an idea to Disney as to where a grown Kevin McAllister would be today after enduring two child abandonments and harassment and attempted murder from bumbling bandits (our interpretation, not necessarily his read on Kevin’s childhood shenanigans and trauma). Disney now seems to have warmed to the idea like a cup of hot cocoa, especially thanks to the two additional names who are working with Culkin on the project: Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg. Related Stories What ‘Digger’ Has in Common with Gary Oldman’s Winston Churchill and Charlize Theron’s Megyn Kelly ‘Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall’ Review: PTA’s Spellbinding Concert Doc Is a Gorgeously Tender Performance.

Disney’s 20th Century Studios is in early development on a sequel to “Home Alone” that would star Culkin reprising his original role and in which Rogen and Goldberg on behalf of their Point Grey banner would write and produce the film, working with Culkin on his idea, IndieWire has learned.

Things are very, very early days, and any plot details are being kept under wraps for now, and no director is attached at the moment.

Chris Columbus directed the original “Home Alone” and its nearly-as-loved sequel “Home Alone 2: Lost in Newly introduced York,” and both written by the late great John Hughes. If you can believe it, there have been six “Home Alone” movies in all, with the third one at least released in theaters and doing respectable box office numbers. The others are all TV movies or in the case of the most recent 2021 film “Home Sweet Home Alone,” a Disney+ streaming movie.

The original two films though grossed $477 million and $358 million worldwide, respectively, and the original still gets tons of cable play and finds its way into the Nielsen streaming charts. It makes sense that a more serious sequel with Culkin back in the fold would be welcomed by audiences.

Sadly, “Home Alone” has been back on the minds of audiences of late after the recent passing of Catherine O’Hara, who played Kevin’s mom, and also Tim Curry, who had a small role as a hotel clerk in “Home Alone 2.” Joe Pesci and Daniel Stern as the Wet Bandits are still around, though Pesci has been mostly retired outside of his return in Scorsese’s “The Irishman” back in 2019 and his role in the Pete Davidson Peacock series “Bupkis” in 2023.

Culkin too has had a bit of a resurgence, making a cameo in the most recent season of “Fallout” and doing a voice in Disney’s “Zootopia 2.”.

You Can Try WhatsApp's New Disappearing Text Messages Early

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (454 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices.
  • Industry observers note that that's now changing.
  • It has been revealed that as WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices. You can send voice messages, photos, and videos that will "self-destruct" after they're opened, limiting (if not eliminating) the risk of your friends keeping them forever. However, View Once has a major limitation: While WhatsApp will let you send voice memos and images that way, you can't use it to send texts, meaning every one you send will live on (unless you unsend it yourself).

Industry observers note that that's now changing. As reported by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now beta testing View Once for text messages, too. Soon enough, you'll be able to send voice memos, photos, videos, and texts as one-time-only messages. That way, you can send sensitive information via text—say, a password or an vital account number—without worrying about it persisting. Here's how it works: You craft your text message as you usually do, but rather than tap the send button, you hold it. You'll see the usual "Schedule message" option, but once the feature rolls out, you'll also find a upcoming "View Once" option as well.

It has been revealed that as WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it. WhatsApp also explains that recipients cannot share, forward, save, or take screenshots of View Once text messages. Recipients won't see the text appear in the usual chat interface, either; instead, your recipient will need to open the message in a separate window. Once they close this page, the message disappears.

As mentioned above, this feature is at the moment in testing, so it's only available to WhatsApp beta testers. What's more, only the Android version of the beta has access at the moment, so iOS beta testers are out of luck. (That stated, the WhatsApp iOS beta is perpetually full, so there's not much you could do even if WhatsApp made this test available on iPhone.).

In a recent development, if you have an Android device, you can enroll in the WhatsApp beta to try out "View Once" text messages today. According to WABetaInfo, the feature is live as of WhatsApp version 2.26.45.6. To enroll, open the WhatsApp beta page on the Google Play store and enroll your account in the beta. If you don't have WhatsApp on your phone already, download it here; if you do, reload the page and install the latest update. This will update your existing WhatsApp app to the latest beta version.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Netflix's hit latest series has ignited a petition with over 135,000 signatures calling for its cancellation.

Recent findings suggest that this is far from the first instance of a controversial Netflix series. In 2019, the Brazilian comedy, The First Temptation of Christ (2019), sparked protests and petitions claiming blasphemy. In 2020, the French drama Cuties sparked backlash and petitions claiming it sexualized young girls. In 2021, Netflix's own employees protested outside the tech giant's headquarters, claiming that Dave Chappelle's comedy special, The Closer, was transphobic.

In a recent development, now, over 135,000 people have signed an online petition calling for the cancellation of Netflix's fresh show, The Body, calling it "blasphemous" and "anti-Christian." The show follows a group of Catholic schoolgirls who perform a mock Satanic ritual, jokingly offering one of their classmates as a virgin sacrifice. After she falls into a coma, they begin having prophetic visions of her, triggering mass hysteria.

Sources indicate that the petition, on CitizenGO, calls the show "a blasphemous anti-Christian series featuring satanic ritual," and warns, "Parents cannot screen every show teens press play on. Netflix is counting on that." The petition was launched ahead of the show's debut on November 11, urging Netflix to scrap its release. Now, at the time of writing, the petition has surpassed 135,000 signatures.

Talking to Decider, Marcel Ruiz, who appears in a recurring role as Tyler Flores, reacted to the viral petition, saying the backlash may actually be a sign the show is striking a nerve and tackling complications people care about. Whether audiences are watching because of outrage or curiosity, it's helping the show climb the charts. Despite calls for cancellation, the cast is hoping for The Body season 2. Read Ruiz's full comments below:.

Sources indicate that I wonder if all of those people that have signed the petition have seen the show? That’s like, something I wonder. And also, in a way, it doesn’t surprise me, not because the show is disrespectful, or because the show deserves to have a petition like that, but that’s sometimes art. I did hear a funny story; my dad told me that this friend of his told him that in his daughter’s private Catholic school, they were telling the kids not to watch it. And I thought, "That’s such a flex." I loved hearing that.

Sometimes, things that are moving the ball forward are also going to have some pushback in some areas. You can’t please everyone at the end of the day, I think. It’s good enough that the show is number one on Netflix. Can’t ask for much else.

We’re waiting by the phone. What was so cool is when we were shooting Season 1, you can’t help yourself but think of a future for these characters and ideas. And I remember the day that I wrapped, I went home and I was so emotional that it was over that I just went on my phone and started writing ideas for Tyler for Season 2. Just like as a way to cope and like have some closure. Definitely, I’m excited to, when the time comes, be able to pick that back up.

Ruiz is right in the sense that The Body debuted at No. 2 on Netflix's Top 10 indicates in the United States and No. 3 globally, receiving 5.1 million views and 37.4 million hours viewed worldwide for the week of November 9–15. As of today, November 20, The Body is the No. 1 show on Netflix, both worldwide and in the United States.

Despite the backlash, The Body reviews have been mostly positive from both critics and audiences, resulting in 87% and 96% Rotten Tomatoes scores from those groups, respectively. Critics claim The Body blends religious guilt, teenage angst, striking visuals, and vibrant storytelling into an unapologetically bold and queer coming-of-age tale that constantly defies expectations.

Despite public backlash, streaming services seldom cave to demands to pull titles from their platforms, so it's unlikely to happen to The Body, especially given its success.

Kevin McCallister got left behind in Illinois, then lost in Newly introduced York, and somehow Macaulay Culkin made both look like pretty appealing ways to spend Christmas. He could order his own pizza, charge an unreasonable amount of room service to his father’s credit card, and make two burglars regret every decision that brought them to his door. The obvious question for another Home Alone movie is what happens when Kevin becomes the adult somebody else wants out of the house.

Culkin has recently been playing Kevin again for McDonald’s holiday campaign, and he told Collider's Hannah Hunt there’s one thing the character would never grow out of: “Defying authority," he remarked, pointing to the rebellious streak that makes Kevin so easy for kids to root for. Culkin figures adults still understand the appeal of getting one over on somebody bigger, too, because no matter how old you are, “You always have a boss.".

Recent findings suggest that A new Home Alone movie with Culkin is now in development at Disney, according to new reports. Disney declined to comment on the report, so as of now there’s no release date attached, but the reported deal gives Kevin’s potential movie comeback a strong producing team.

Culkin spoke with Collider earlier this month about returning as Kevin for McDonald’s, and he sounded happy to have another reason to revisit the character. He described Home Alone as a “wonderful sandbox to play around in,” particularly now that he gets to see people who grew up with the movie introduce it to another generation. “It’s taken on its own life,” he noted. That becomes especially obvious whenever November rolls around. Culkin estimates he gets recognized ten times more between November and January, joking that he “cornered the fourth quarter market.”.

Sources indicate that at screenings now, he gets to watch an audience arrive with years of Christmas memories attached to the movie. “They bring their nostalgia with them,” he told Collider. For now, Culkin’s latest return is the McDonald’s campaign, which he described as a natural fit for a movie families revisit every year. “The actual food and the movie are comfort food, really,” he remarked.

Face unlock is a good compromise for the iPhone Duo – now let’s have it for the Mac

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (850 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Apple first confirmed Face ID, the company talked a great deal about how secure the system is, contrasting it to the far less secure image-based facial unlock systems used by the likes of Google and Samsung.
  • Fast-forward to 2026, and Apple is itself now offering that less secure approach as an option on the iPhone Duo – but in a way I consider a sensible balance between convenience and security ….
  • The first smartphone to offer a face unlock feature was the Galaxy Nexus back in 2011.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Apple first confirmed Face ID, the company talked a great deal about how secure the system is, contrasting it to the far less secure image-based facial unlock systems used by the likes of Google and Samsung.

Fast-forward to 2026, and Apple is itself now offering that less secure approach as an option on the iPhone Duo – but in a way I consider a sensible balance between convenience and security ….

The first smartphone to offer a face unlock feature was the Galaxy Nexus back in 2011. This didn’t include any extra hardware, simply using the front-facing camera to take a photo and compare this to a stored image of the user.

In a recent development, it took just days to discover just how insecure this approach is, with unlock achieved simply by holding up a photo of the owner’s face on another device. Yet even as late as 2019, Samsung was continuing to use this approach.

Meantime, in 2017 Apple introduced Face ID in the iPhone X. This has an entire hardware module devoted to it, with infrared emitters and receivers used to create a 3D map of the shape of our face. This cannot be fooled by photos or even models, and Apple stated at the time there was a less than a one in a million chance of it being fooled (with riders for twins, etc).

In a recent development, face ID projects more than 30,000 invisible IR dots. The IR image and dot pattern are pushed through neural networks to create a mathematical model of your face and send the data to the secure enclave to confirm a match, while adapting to physical changes in appearance over time. All saved facial information is protected by the secure enclave to keep data extremely secure, while all of the processing is done on-device […] The probability that a random person in the population could look at your iPhone or iPad Pro and unlock it using Face ID is less than 1 in 1,000,000.

Given the massive contrast in security of the two approaches, it might seem odd that Apple is now adapting a purely visual face unlock feature. The only reason the company is doing this is because the lack of Face ID has been far and away one of the biggest complaints about the iPhone Duo.

I suspect Apple made the decision reluctantly and over the protests of security engineers. But while face unlock remains a very insecure approach compared to Face ID, Apple’s approach tries to strike a good balance between convenience and security. The following safeguards apply:.

That latter restriction means it can’t be used for Apple Pay, to unlock password-protected apps, to open the Passwords app, or to do anything else that requires authentication – such as changing your passcode or adding a fingerprint to Touch ID.

I do not see any downside provided the feature is off by default and only those who want it will turn it on. Presumably with an explanation of the reasons it gives reduced security.

It has been revealed that for myself, I have got so used to using touch ID on my keyboard that I'd likely not make use of it in my business. If anything goes wrong with client information, I want to know, and be able to demonstrate, that I have taken security seriously.

There’s only one other safeguard I’d like to see Apple introduce: geolocking. Personally, I’d want to be able to allow face unlock at home, but disable it when I’m out and about. Presently, the only two ways to temporarily disable it are to toggle it off or to restart the phone. I’d like to see an option to set safe locations, like home and work, with the feature disabled in public.

Given that Face unlock requires only a front-facing camera, there’s absolutely no reason why Apple couldn’t also make it available on the Mac.

Industry observers note that face ID has been something MacBook consumers have been wanting for a great many years, and despite a decade’s worth of Apple patents for just this, it still hasn’t happened. Face unlock would be a compromise option that would at least get us some of the way there. I see I’m not the first to suggest this, with Macworld’s Roman Loyola beating me to it.

It has been revealed that what’s your view? If you own an iPhone Duo, will you choose to enable this? If you own a MacBook, would you like the same option on that? Please take our poll and share your thoughts in the comments.

  • Key Apple memory supplier SK Hynix has warned that RAM and flash memory shortages are likely to last through at least 2030, keeping product prices high.
  • Update: Apple is reportedly about to sign a similar contract with Samsung, also permitting market-driven price increases.
  • SK Hynix indicates that while AI continues to drive demand and growth, there is little that can be done in the short to medium term to increase supply.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Key Apple memory supplier SK Hynix has warned that RAM and flash memory shortages are likely to last through at least 2030, keeping product prices high. Apple is believed to be one of 14 customers who have locked in priority orders, but the contract does not protect against price increases related to the balance of supply and demand.

Update: Apple is reportedly about to sign a similar contract with Samsung, also permitting market-driven price increases.

SK Hynix indicates that while AI continues to drive demand and growth, there is little that can be done in the short to medium term to increase supply.

Supply, on the other hand, is not keeping pace with the growth of the market. Given technical difficulty of leading-edge processes and the long lead time required to build latest production facilities, it expects the structure in which demand exceeds supply to persist through 2030.

The Register reports that SK Hynix has long-term deals with 14 tech giants for priority orders, but these allow for market-based price increases.

Recent findings suggest that 14 big buyers […] will collectively buy more than half of its output during 2027 and 2028, and some of them want to extend those agreements. The Korean giant doesn’t mind that because the deals include “a mechanism that reflects market conditions within a price range agreed upon with customers”.

It has been revealed that apple is used to being in the driving seat when it comes to negotiating with suppliers, but this is not the case where memory and flash storage is concerned. Here, the shortages mean that it will have been forced to agree to contracts that allow significant price hikes in order to obtain guaranteed supplies.

Sources indicate that nikkei Asia also reports that printed circuit boards may be the next component to experience constrained supply. Once a humble commodity item, advances in the technology has turned them into specialist tech, with more layers and higher bandwidth requirements. The report says “that complexity shrinks the supplier pool and extends lead times.”.

Apple stated back in June that the company was doing its best to mitigate the price increases, but it has so far been unable to do so.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it was American author Lloyd Alexander who's credited with coining the term "high fantasy" in his 1971 essay High Fantasy and Heroic Romance, while "low fantasy" appeared later in the 20th century as a contrasting classification. Where high fantasy tells stories set in secondary worlds with their own unique set of rules, low fantasy finds the genre's magical and supernatural elements intrude into our own world—or a setting very heavily based on it.

Though live-action cinema has produced several exceptional low fantasy masterpieces over the years, there's something special about the way animation allows low fantasy filmmakers to really let their imaginations fly. From anime gems like My Neighbor Totoro to modern American blockbusters like How to Train Your Dragon, these are films which show why animation is such a perfect vehicle for low fantasy storytelling.

A girl under an umbrella stands next to Totoro in the rain at a bus stop in Studio Ghibli's My Neighbor Totoro.

A girl under an umbrella stands next to Totoro in the rain at a bus stop in Studio Ghibli's My Neighbor Totoro.

According to recent reports, the 1980s saw the birth of Studio Ghibli, the studio that quickly became the quintessential spearhead of anime filmmaking—a title they most definitely still hold. One of their earliest masterworks was Hayao Miyazaki's My Neighbor Totoro, about two young sisters who move with their dad to the Japanese countryside to be closer to their ill mother, where they find comfort and wonder in the organization of the forest's friendly spirits.

It's one of the best family movies in film history, a testament to the timeless power of slice-of-life low fantasy. Ma is a Japanese artistic concept defined by intentional emptiness or stillness, and My Neighbor Totoro is a masterful example of ma-heavy filmmaking. But though it's simple, it's also emotionally impactful beyond description, still a must-see for families everywhere nearly 40 years after its release.

In a recent development, director Henry Selick met author Neil Gaiman just as he was finishing his children's novella Coraline, and since Gaiman was such a fan of Selick's The Nightmare Before Christmas, he invited him to make a film adaptation of Coraline. It's the story of the titular girl, who discovers a secret door in her latest home leading to an idealized parallel world that's actually far more sinister than it initially seems.

Coraline was stop-motion animation studio Laika's first-ever feature film (and the only one they've ever made that has been profitable), and what an introduction to such a marvelous studio this was. It's one of the best dark fantasy movies ever made, and even though portal fantasy often makes it tricky to distinguish between high and low fantasy, Coraline's idealized parallel world makes this a clear example of one of the 2000s' best low fantasy gems.

It has been revealed that based on their trilogy of stop-motion-animated documentary short films, Dean Fleischer Camp and Jenny Slate made Marcel the Shell With Shoes On, with Camp directing and Slate voicing the titular one-inch-tall seashell. This is his story, as he and his grandmother search for their missing family after a documentary filmmaker's online videos turn Marcel into an overnight Internet sensation.

According to recent reports, one of the most emotional animated movies in recent memory, Marcel the Shell is a beautiful tale about grief, community, and finding wonder in everyday life. It's silly, it's simple, it's funny, yet it's more than emotionally complex enough to satisfy even the most cynical of grown-up viewers. Blending live-action and animation has always resulted in really interesting projects, and as far as the last decade goes, this is probably the best of the bunch.

Recent findings suggest that irish animation studio Cartoon Saloon have been making some of the fantasy movies with the best lore for years, all thanks to their stories often being heavily inspired by Irish folklore. Case in point: Tomm Moore's Song of the Sea, about a young boy and his mute selkie sister journeying across a fading world to return home after their mother vanishes into the sea.

According to recent reports, for one, the colorful visuals are absolutely gorgeous, more than enough to remind anyone of why it's still crucial to have 2D-animated features in modern times. Add to that a beautiful story, an airtight plot that's perfectly paced from start to finish, and deeply memorable characters, and there should be no question left as to why this is one of the most universally beloved low fantasy films of the 2010s, animated or otherwise.

As if any more proof were needed that Cartoon Saloon is one of the most interesting animation studios presently in operation, there's also Wolkfwalkers, one of the best fantasy films of the 2020s so far. Set in 1650s Ireland, it follows a young English apprentice hunter who befriends a wild native girl from a mystical tribe of wolf-spirits, being pulled into the magical world of the very creatures her father has been ordered to exterminate.

Stories about forbidden friendship in children's animation are aplenty, but what makes Wolfwalkers so special is the gorgeous animation, the deep low fantasy world-building, and the deeply moving father-daughter dynamic that often serves as the film's beating heart. A potent critique of colonialism, authoritarianism, and ecological destruction, this is a must-see for anyone who loves modern animation.

Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

In a recent development, you want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

You would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Industry observers note that toy Story completely revolutionized the film industry by introducing the world to fully CG-animated feature filmmaking, and Toy Story 2 somehow managed to be even better. It's Toy Story 3, however, that many still recognize as Pixar's best film to date. In it, Andy's toys are accidentally sent to a daycare center as he prepares to leave for college, forcing them to decide whether to stay together or fight their way back home.

From the phenomenal character writing to the deep themes to one of the most perfect movie endings of the 2010s, pretty much everything about Toy Story 3 is low fantasy animation perfection. Toys being alive is the only high-concept premise that makes this franchise low fantasy, and Toy Story 3 takes that premise to unprecedentedly ambitious and emotional heights.

In a recent development, it's not all Miyazaki: Studio Ghibli has also made films directed by other filmmakers who are just as talented, perhaps the most talented of whom was the great Isao Takahata. His final film as director was Ghibli's The Tale of the Princess Kaguya, an adaptation of the 10th-century Japanese story The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter. In it, a rapidly-growing child is found inside a bamboo stalk and raised by a humble cutter, eventually thrust into high society as a noble princess.

Princess Kaguya is not only one of Ghibli's greatest films to date, but also one of the best fantasy movie masterpieces of the last 15 years. With its wonderfully unique watercolor animation and its profound emotional and thematic maturity, this is both a fantasy masterpiece and a gorgeous period piece. It's complex, it's deeply moving, and it may just have the most unforgettable ending in Ghibli's entire filmography.

Based on the series of children's books by Cressida Cowell, How to Train Your Dragon gave birth to one of the best fantasy movie trilogies of all time. It tells the story of the awkward young Viking Hiccup, who lives on a dragon-raiding island and befriends a wounded dragon that challenges his tribe's traditions. What ensues is further proof that, though abundant, low fantasy stories of forbidden friendship are genuinely special.

Sources indicate that dragons have always been prevalent across both high and low fantasy stories even before cinema was a thing, but few dragon-centric fantasy films have ever been quite as universally beloved as How to Train Your Dragon. That's for good reason. With Roger Deakins as a consultant and DreamWorks' phenomenal team, the animation is obviously fantastic; but what really makes this stand out as one of the studio's best animated films is the emotional story, the tight plotting, and the excellent character work.

Brad Bird's Ratatouille is many people's favorite Pixar film to date, and it isn't the least bit difficult to see why. Visually wonderful, tonally complex, and emotionally and thematically mature, it tells the engrossing story of a Paris rate with an extraordinary palate, who teams up with a clumsy kitchen garbage boy to secretly become a master chef at a prestigious restaurant.

According to recent reports, it's a silly premise that any lesser filmmaker or animation studio may have turned into an equally silly comedy, but Bird treats the premise with such beautiful and sincere earnestness that Ratatouille rapidly becomes one of the most wonderful works of art that animation has delivered in years. It's also one of the fantasy movies with the most interesting characters, which is only one of the many reasons why it's an absolute must-see.

Who, if not Hayao Miyazaki, could be behind yet another one of the most ambitious fantasy movies ever made? It is, of course, Ghibli's Princess Mononoke, which is set in the Muromachi period of Japanese history. In it, a young prince cursed by a demon journeys into a war between an industrial mining town and the forest gods, who fight back alongside a girl raised by wolves.

Sources indicate that it's one of the darkest, most violent, and most mature movies that Studio Ghibli have thus far made, and it also just so happens to arguably be the greatest low fantasy animated feature ever made. Though its world-building prioritizes historical realism over fantasy, there's still more than plenty of it to satisfy fans of the genre. An enrapturing story about the destructive cycle of hatred and ecological exploitation, it's easily one of the best outings in Miyazaki's filmography.
